- D41 (r12, review F3): transaction identity is no longer conflated
  with commit-window membership. `write_ts` is the recording
  transaction's CREATE timestamp (D8/D14 need it constant per
  transaction), so a transaction created before the fork or a PICK
  BETWEEN boundary can commit relevant moves inside the window, and a
  `write_ts >= startPhys` / `>= lowerBound` predicate — D24's bound for
  both probe sites — reported those omitted departures as complete
  absence (live red: a pre-snapshot move replayed as legacy
  DELETE+INSERT and died on the FK; worse, an included `2->3` next to an
  omitted `3->4` plus a rebirth at 3 read as a same-key tail and claimed
  the unrelated row). Both consumer probe sites now scan full history
  through `endPhys` only; stream commit instants decide window
  membership during the walk/fold, and the full-window cache signature
  (D24) still guards inconsistent reuse. D24's lower bound is
  superseded; its endpoint bound, signature, LIMIT-budget and
  truncation-disables-provider behaviors are unchanged. Two-session
  boundary BVTs: pbc (simple straddler cascades) and pbs (straddler
  chain + impostor folds to 4, never claims 3).
- D42 (r12, review F4): one synchronization contract covers every
  provenance-map accessor: the caller MUST hold `txn.Lock`. r11's
  `notePkMoveDivertedDelete` read/iterated `pkMoveLinkTables` and
  mutated `pkMoveDeadPks` lock-free from the deleteBatch divert branch
  while parallel `UpdateWriteS3` producers (compile fan-out over one
  transaction) staged links under the lock — a map read/write race, and
  the `beginCatalogMutation` fence is only an atomic revision counter
  pair. The divert branch now batches its note calls behind a single
  lock hold per delete batch (`notePkMoveDivertedDeleteLocked`),
  matching the staging side; every utterance of the maps is inside the
  one lock. UT: `TestPkMoveDivertedDeleteOverlap` runs a staging writer
  against divert callers on one shared transaction — it reproduces the
  race pre-fix under `-race` and is quiet post-fix; whole-package
  `-race` on both packages stays green.

- D43 (r13, review F1): the NULL-identity by-key hop screens the landed
  key's tombstones BEFORE adopting a same-transaction departure. D39
  followed `successorOfSameTxnKey` on key+scope alone, so an S3-route
  vacate-before-arrival shape mis-assigned the successor's continuation
  to the anchor's lineage: the departure had vacated an OLDER committed
  generation of the landed key, not the generation the landed lineage
  arrived on. The hop now requires that no in-window tombstone at the
  landed key names the departure's recorded old row id
  (`ref.rowID == cand.oldRowID`); such a tombstone proves the departure
  consumed a committed pre-image — a foreign lineage — and the walk
  falls through to the tied-claim steps. UT: vacate-before-arrival
  RED->GREEN in `TestResolvePkMoveChain`; live: S3-route two-lineage
  key collision keeps both lineages on their own payloads.
- D44 (r13, review F2; amends D26): the durable transaction id is the
  transaction namespace; the create timestamp is only the fallback for
  identity-less rows. HLC advances the logical component when two
  transactions are created inside one physical instant (hlc.go), but
  `write_ts` stores physical nanoseconds only, so D26's salt made those
  transactions one namespace and could chain one's continuation onto
  the other. The link schema gains `txn_id binary(16)` (v4.0.8 column
  add — D149's forward version: `mo_data_branch_update_link` has not
  merged to main, so the DDL still changes freely), the producer stamps
  `proc.GetTxnOperator().Txn().ID`, the workspace link-id salt becomes
  `sha256(normTxnID(16) || writeTS(8) || rid)`, and the consumer's
  `pkMoveTxnScope` matches by 16-byte id equality when both sides carry
  one, `write_ts` equality otherwise (all-zero stored id = identity
  unknown, e.g. a defensive foreign-write fallback). UTs: two scope
  candidates sharing one physical instant resolve by txn id; salt
  differs by txn for one rowid; live: two concurrent sessions mint
  distinct 16-byte recording identities and both chains fold. (A live
  same-physical-instant collision is not reproducibly reachable: the
  HLC physical clock reads per-call nanoseconds, so the unit proofs
  above carry that shape.)
- D45 (r13, review F3): statement undo bookkeeping is constant-time
  per record. An N-row pk-unchanged update stages one continuity
  marker per row (D28), and r12 noted each undo record with a linear
  pre-append scan — N(N-1)/2 comparisons under `txn.Lock` made bulk
  non-key updates quadratic
  (`BenchmarkPkMoveMarkerFillDurableOrigins`, 4096 markers: 22.07 ms/op
  pre-fix). Paired seen-sets make first-record-wins constant-time:
  `pkMoveRetargetUndoSeen` by link id (retarget and heal records share
  one slot, preserving the one-slice semantics) and
  `pkMoveOriginUndoSeen` by row id, both retired with the undo slices
  at every statement boundary and on rollback; the
  `pkMoveLinkBirth`-population guards turn the no-link bulk case into
  a provable no-scan (4096 markers: 5.70 ms/op, flat scaling from 256).
  UT: dedup pins first-record-wins across retarget/heal/origin and
  rollback retiring the sets; benchmark red/green archived.
- D46 (r13, review F4): the ts-tie claim at a chain end tolerates a
  post-endpoint committed successor departure when that departure binds
  no in-window tombstone. D14 refused the claim whenever ANY recorded
  later departure of the claim row existed, so a straddling transaction
  (created in-window, committing past the endpoint) whose departure
  consumed no visible generation invalidated an otherwise attributable
  historical fold and degraded it to DELETE replay onto the foreign
  key. The claim now succeeds when the departure's recorded old row id
  equals the claim row's and its commit ts lies strictly beyond the
  chain end (`ref.cts.GT(&chainTS)`: not an in-window binding). UT:
  straddler-departure claim RED->GREEN; live: two-session straddler —
  MERGE over the historical window folds and cascades.
- D47 (r13, review F5; refines D13): row-less parent link reclaim is
  additionally gated on snapshot coverage. Dropping the last branch
  descendant erased the parent's provenance while a retained snapshot
  could still ground a historical branch over it
  (`data branch create table t2 from t1{snapshot="sp"}` instantiates a
  new lineage descendant whose diffs span link-bearing history recorded
  after the snapshot — the source kept evolving). The reclaim now
  name-resolves the parent via `mo_catalog.mo_tables` under the owning
  account and probes that account's `mo_catalog.mo_snapshots` for
  non-`kind='branch'` rows (branch-protect snapshots retire with the
  metadata rows D13 already covers), keeping the links when any
  cluster/account/database/table scope covers the named table; every
  probe failure keeps links (D12 tolerance), including an unresolvable
  name — the mo_tables row may be gone while a snapshot still names
  it. Sessions resolve snapshots only in their own account's catalog,
  so the per-account probe is the exact grounding set. UTs: coverage
  matrix plus gate keeps/reclaims through the drop lifecycle; live:
  drop-last-branch with a retained covering snapshot keeps the links
  and `CREATE ... {snapshot=...}` still folds; dropping the snapshot
  reclaims.
- D48 (r13, review F6): boundary tests drive the production locking
  boundary, not its interior. The D42 UT self-acquired `txn.Lock`,
  called the Locked variant directly, padded the overlap with a sleep,
  and asserted a pre-populated map entry — removing the boundary lock
  still passed. `deleteBatch` now calls the extracted
  `notePkMoveDivertedDeletes` boundary (one lock hold per delete
  batch), and the test rendezvous-synchronizes a staging writer against
  boundary callers over 64 deterministic rounds (no sleeps) and asserts
  the serializable end state (the latest statement survives:
  `pkMoveDeadPks` advances to 100+rounds-1); removing the boundary
  lock trips `-race` (RED archived), restoring it is quiet.
- D49 (r14, review F1): S3-route same-key edits record which durable
  lineage the key descends from, and a later move of that row heals its
  recorded old identity through it. D28's continuity protocol assumed
  every same-key replacement stages in the workspace so the exact
  origin map (D35) can carry lineage; on the UpdateWriteS3 route the
  replacement never stages, so the marker stayed unresolved, was
  discarded, and the later move recorded the S3-buffered replacement
  identity the statement read — while the committed stream tombstone
  names the committed pre-image. The D43 tombstone screen then missed
  the lineage's own departure, and a vacate-before-arrival arrival
  adopted the foreign departure (MERGE/PICK cross-assigning children
  onto the wrong lineage: live RED `(1,4),(2,3)` instead of
  `(1,3),(2,4)`, each child orphaned onto the other lineage's parent).
  The unresolved marker now binds the key to the durable origin it
  proves (composed through a live valid binding, else the exact origin
  map, else the marker's durable pre-image literally; workspace-stage
  pre-images anchor literally per D35 and bind nothing). Fill pass 1b
  heals the recorded old identity of every link row the exact map does
  not govern to the bound origin; a binding is valid only while no
  staged DELETE of the key outdates its bind watermark (a lazy
  incremental fold of the txn's delete entries keyed to the D27
  harvest epoch, fail-closed on any poison) and only while no recorded
  departure consumed it: a kept departure (old key bytes != new key
  bytes) consumes the binding in a statement-tagged stack entry, so a
  reincarnated generation at the key starts a fresh lineage literal to
  its own pre-image instead of inheriting the departed one. Rollback
  truncates the stacks with their statement and drops the delete-scan
  cache; a heal allocation failure fails the fill like every other
  pass (D52 posture). The consumer needs no change: the healed
  identity re-arms the D43 screen, so the "affirmative lineage
  evidence" the review demanded before adopting a by-key successor is
  exactly the screen the unhealed identity was blinding. UT battery:
  bind/heal/consume/delete-retire/rollback/alloc-failure subtests RED
  (mute the marker-bind call and the two fill-pass call-sites: the
  move keeps the S3-buffered identity and five of seven subtests
  fail; the workspace-literal and delete-retire guards pass both
  ways) -> GREEN (`TestPkMoveS3LineageHeal`). Live: `ew_` (MERGE)
  and `ewp_` (PICK) BVT sections — a same-key payload edit on B, B
  3->4, then A 2->3 in one fault-armed S3 transaction; each lineage
  keeps its own payload and child.
- D50 (r14, review F2): UpdateWriteS3 producers COLLECT provenance and
  ferry it through the S3 tail output; only the committing transaction
  stages it. The era-7 producer wrote the catalog row inside each S3
  producer via `Relation.Write`; under remote execution that write
  landed in the mirror workspace the remote-run server creates for the
  scope (remoterunServer.go), which the committing transaction never
  sees — a multi-CN update could commit replacement rows without their
  links, and the r13 single-CN captures could not see the loss. The
  producer's per-context recorder now only builds the link batch into
  `pkMoveLinkBufs`; `flushTailAndWriteToOutput` emits each buffer as a
  tail row with the new `actionPkMoveLink` action naming the OWNER
  table id; the coordinator-side `UpdateFlushS3Info` decodes each
  ferry batch, matches the owner id to its own synthetic link ctx,
  and stages the batch into the committing transaction's workspace
  through the lazily resolved per-account link relation (failing the
  statement on write errors per D52; an unresolvable catalog table —
  old-tenant mixed-version posture — degrades to drop+warn, never an
  update failure). Naming the owner instead of the link ctx's own
  table id is load-bearing, and the first r14 live run proved it: the
  synthetic ctx's plan TableDef is schema-only with TblId 0 (a
  per-account virtual catalog table carries no plan table id), so the
  initial getSourceByID(tblId) wiring resolved id 0, warned
  "skip ferried pk-move update links: link table unavailable
  table_id:0", and silently dropped every ferried batch — live RED
  `/tmp/e8_live_f1.log` (S3-forced arms commit rows with ZERO links;
  the r14 unit oracle had escaped this by letting the test link ctx
  share the owner TableDef, giving it a nonzero id the live plan
  never has). Both sides now share `resolvePkMoveLinkSource`, the
  ferry encodes `TargetUpdateCtxIdx`'s owner id, and the UT oracle
  mirrors the live shape (link ctx TblId 0; UT RED
  `/tmp/e8_red_ferry.log` -> GREEN `/tmp/e8_green_ferry.log`).
  Placement of the producer then cannot lose provenance: the tail
  output is part of the scope's S3-output contract the pipeline ships
  to the coordinator regardless of where the producer ran, and the
  producer touches no workspace for links at all. Affected-rows
  accounting stays as r13. UTs: collector capture with exact
  link/owner context rows, tail emission order/payload with
  `actionPkMoveLink` rows decoded back, coordinator staging of a
  decoded ferry batch into the resolved source with zero affected
  rows, degrade on a disabled ctx and on an unmatched owner id, and
  the direct-write restriction pinning `UpdateWriteTable` as the only
  catalog-writing action (`TestPkMoveLinkWriteAction`). Live: every
  fault-armed S3 pk-move statement in both genrs suites rides the
  ferry, and the multi-CN battery runs the update on both CNs (its
  remote-placement finding recorded in §10).
- D51 (r14, review F3): provenance verdicts are tri-state, and an
  unresolved verdict aborts the apply instead of degrading to legacy
  DELETE+INSERT replay. Earlier revisions conservatively degraded any
  non-fold to legacy replay; the review isolated the asymmetry: for a
  destination FK declaring both actions, a genuine chain longer than
  the hop budget — or a probe answering past the link budget —
  replayed the parent row's DELETE, cascaded the delete onto the
  child, and then inserted the final parent: the child was destroyed
  while the parent survived, visibly contradicting the in-txn UPDATE.
  `resolvePkMoveChain` now returns `pkMoveFolded`, `pkMoveProvenNone`
  (complete evidence affirmatively shows independent operations:
  reincarnation disproof, shape-free or disabled provider, proven
  absence) or `pkMoveUnresolved` (truncated or internally inconsistent
  evidence: hop/catalog budget exhaustion, corrupt duplicate
  same-instant births, probe failures), and
  `resolveAndBuildPkMoveFolds` fails the apply statement-atomically on
  any unresolved verdict, reserving legacy replay for proven-absent
  ones. Chain/budget boundary UTs pin the taxonomy end to end —
  including a chain exactly at the hop bound folding
  (`TestPkMoveResolveVerdictTaxonomy`,
  `TestResolveAndBuildPkMoveFoldsAbortsOnUnresolved`) — and the
  cascade/set-null boundary rows ride the same abort with the
  destructive-decode counterexample kept.
- D52 (r14, review F4): provenance bookkeeping failures travel the
  ordinary statement-error route. The r12 fill hook returned void and
  dropped allocation failures before marker removal and birth
  bookkeeping, retarget/remap failures returned silently, and the
  undo capture ignored `vector.SetBytesAt` errors — an UPDATE or a
  statement rollback could then commit with incomplete or unrestored
  identity state. The fill, the retarget remap, and the undo capture
  now return errors through the workspace-staging caller (txn.go
  staging fails the statement so no partial provenance commits), the
  rollback path surfaces restore faults while always running the
  remaining undo records to completion, and `pk_move_link.go` records
  the same seams (`pkMoveVecAppendBytes`/`pkMoveVecSetBytesAt`) the
  UTs fault-inject. Allocation-failure tests assert the statement
  fails, nothing staged by the failed pass survives (restored earlier
  links), and memory accounting stays balanced
  (`TestFillPkMoveAllocFailurePropagates`,
  `TestRetargetFaultStatementFailureAndRestore`,
  `TestRollbackPkMoveRestoreFaultSurfacesAndCompletes`, RED -> GREEN).
- D53 (r14, review F5; refines D45): per-marker continuity work
  indexes its staged-link scans instead of re-scanning the staged set.
  D45 made no-link bulk updates constant-time, but a transaction
  carrying REAL staged links still paid one full staged-set scan per
  resolved marker in both retarget (by replacement identity) and
  NULL-link continuation (by key endpoint): N same-key edits over L
  staged links cost O(N*L) under `txn.Lock`
  (`BenchmarkPkMoveMarkerFillPopulatedLinks`, 4096 populated links:
  556 ms/op pre-fix, superlinear from 256). The fill now builds the
  `pkMoveContinuityIndex` lazily on the first resolved marker —
  `byNewRow` mapping replacement identity to staged link cells plus a
  keyed NULL-identity endpoint fold — so a fill of N markers over L
  links pays O(L + N); both scans route through the index, and fills
  with no resolved marker build nothing (4096: 13.6 ms/op, linear
  from 256; benchmark RED -> GREEN archived).
- D54 (r14, review F6): the conflict-side apply ranker schedules
  ready folds through a min-heap seeded at in-degree zero and updated
  only on vacated-key unlocks, against in-window effective destination
  WHERE keys — the discipline the fold assembler already used (D25) —
  replacing the rescan of the entire surviving batch per emitted fold:
  a conflict-reconciled batch of N independent key-moving folds cost
  N(N+1)/2 rank iterations even with no dependencies
  (`BenchmarkKeyMovingApplyRanks`, independent-16384: 4.67 s
  pre-fix). Deterministic lexicographic tie-breaking and the D36
  cycle protection are preserved (the heap carries the total order
  the scan enforced); independent-16384: 43.9 ms, chain-16384:
  13.1 ms (benchmark RED -> GREEN archived), and the existing
  vacate-order UT matrix pins the emitted order against cycle
  fixtures.
- D55 (r14, review F7): the consumer's transaction-identity collision
  handling carries its own deterministic proof. r13 D44 salted the
  producer-side link ids with the durable 16-byte recording identity
  and asserted the consumer comparison only through fixtures whose
  scopes never competed, so removing the consumer's txn-id comparison
  would still have passed the suite. The consumer test now constructs
  identical-physical-instant successor candidates that differ only in
  their recorded transaction identities (scope probes answered with
  explicitly distinct txn ids, write_ts equal) and asserts the fold
  follows the identity-matching candidate, falls back to the
  create-timestamp tie when identities are absent, and refuses the
  identity-less impostor along the walk; muting the consumer
  comparison makes all three subtests fail
  (`TestPkMoveConsumerTxnIdentityCollision`, RED -> GREEN archived).
  The explicit unknown-ID behavior keeps its own coverage in the
  identity-less successor fixtures.
- D56 (r15, review F1): capped evidence must reach the abort of D51,
  not quietly bypass it. The stream capture reserves budget slots
  against `pkMoveEvidenceMaxEntries` under a single atomic counter
  shared across parallel shards (no per-shard oversubscription),
  reports `capped=true` the moment the bound is hit, and clears both
  indexes so an empty index provably means "cut off", never "nothing
  there" (D41's discipline, now enforced at the capture boundary).
  The fold pass then distinguishes capped-with-provenance from
  capped-and-quiet by asking the link provider whether the window
  holds any recorded move at all: cached links in window, or — when
  the window was not fully scanned — one bounded catalog existence
  probe. Any positive answer feeds the D51 unresolved-verdict abort
  instead of dropping tombstones into legacy DELETE+INSERT replay,
  while a fully scanned quiet window keeps legacy replay untouched.
- D57 (r15, review F2): fold plans with a genuine key-rotation cycle
  cannot be executed without semantics loss by either replay
  strategy, so the plan assembly now refuses them: draining folds in
  dependency order (Kahn, seeded by folds whose landing key holds no
  later-moving fold) leaves a residue exactly when a cycle — or a
  fold depending on one — exists, and that residue aborts the apply
  statement-atomically with an actionable message instead of falling
  through to same-key matching. The fall-through was the defect of
  record: legacy same-key pairing would swap payloads while keeping
  destination keys, re-attaching children onto the wrong lineage with
  no FK violation to stop it. A cycle is never an accident of an
  honest workload (every landing key still holds a cycle member), so
  failing loud, with a rework hint (delete+re-insert instead of
  rotating keys), is the whole protocol; MERGE and PICK BVT sections
  pin the abort and the untouched destination.
- D58 (r15, review F3): workspace compaction remap failures travel
  the same error channel as every other provenance bookkeeping
  failure (D52). The compaction-time remap of recorded link origins
  now returns its error through `mergeTxnWorkspaceLocked` to the
  statement/commit callers instead of swallowing a `SetBytesAt`
  failure inside a void helper; an injected remap fault surfaces at
  the merge and leaves already-remapped links consistent (no partial
  remap can commit user rows whose provenance points at pre-remap
  identities, and no dangling link can be pruned unseen).
- D59 (r15, review F4): provenance candidates are relevance-filtered
  before the D51 unresolved-verdict abort, because a walk that cannot
  resolve is only an apply hazard when its lineage can reach the
  destination. Candidates whose anchor never entered the destination
  window (source-only insert/move/delete netting to an empty diff)
  and PICK anchors that are dependency-only for the requested
  selection are filtered before the abort is evaluated; their
  provenance rows stay recorded for any future window that does reach
  them. The net effect the review demanded: an unchanged-LCA merge or
  an out-of-selection pick succeeds as a no-op while a genuine
  in-window unresolved lineage still aborts (the D51 BVT boundaries
  are unchanged and stayed green).
- D60 (r15, review F5): S3-route provenance retention is bounded by
  an explicit byte budget with a spill lifecycle, not by the
  statement's row count. `pkMoveLinkMemBudget` (16MB default,
  test-injectable) caps the retained link batches; crossing batches
  spill per link ctx — in ctx first-use order so the ferry preserves
  cross-ctx row order — through the same objectio sinker the user
  data uses, one object per ctx per spill wave, and the buffer list
  collapses to location entries; later in-memory batches join the
  ctx's spill group WITHOUT re-writing already-spilled rows. The
  ferry then carries the owner table id, the `pk_move_link_spill`
  transport name, and the block-info batch; the receiver resolves the
  link ctx and relation FIRST (a degraded tenant never pays read IO),
  rejects unknown transport names loudly, and rebuilds the exact
  workspace-stage row shape by `LoadOneBlockWithSpecialLayout` plus
  full `UnionBatch` appends, so fill/identity/heal see one uniform
  layout. Aborted statements release all retained batches and zero
  the counter at reset; spilled objects of uncommitted statements are
  orphaned exactly like other uncommitted flush output and reclaimed
  by ordinary storage GC; each spill logs its ctx, rows, and bytes so
  memory-pressure events are observable. r15's own validation of this
  lifecycle caught and fixed two producer defects the review did not
  enumerate: the synthesized link TableDef carried all-zero column
  seqnums, and objectio v1 writes one column-meta slot per seqnum —
  duplicate seqnums collapse every column onto slot 0 and corrupt the
  recorded extent accounting (the recorded meta extent drifted from
  the physical meta by the summed per-column length deltas, making
  spilled objects unreadable), now fixed at the plan builder by
  stamping dense seqnums (the workspace route keys inserts by column
  name and never reads seqnums); and the receiver first appended
  read-back columns through a nil-selection `vector.Union`, which by
  contract appends nothing — `UnionBatch` over the full column is the
  correct append, and `TestSpilledPkMoveLinkBatchRoundTrip` pins
  both.

- D61 (r16, review F1): the per-transaction death ledger keeps SETS of
  statement ids, so repeated same-key workspace edits and mid-transaction
  statement rollback preserve lineage continuity instead of overwriting
  it. r15 kept one "latest marker statement" slot per key: after an
  S3-route move, the first same-key edit diverted the replacement's
  death and healed the link, and the second same-key edit overwrote the
  marker slot without recording another death, so the commit prune
  retired a LIVE link and the apply fell back to DELETE+INSERT replay
  (RESTRICT rejects; ON DELETE CASCADE deletes the children).
  `pkMoveDeathLedger.dead` and `.markers` now map each key to the full
  set of statement ids that diverted a death or consumed a marker; a
  marker explains only deaths recorded in the SAME statement, and
  statement rollback removes exactly its own ids from both sets, so an
  id leaving a set revives the uncovered death it explained and kills
  only what the rolled-back statement had rescued. The first edit can
  no longer lose its heal to a later edit, and a rolled-back edit
  cannot keep a dead replacement alive. Pinned by the extended
  TestPkMoveNullHealLifecycle (the production diverted-death record of
  the first edit plus txn-level rollback cases, RED -> GREEN archived
  /tmp/e10_red_f1.log) and by the BVT ere_ (MERGE) and erep_ (PICK)
  sections: one recorded link survives both edits, the apply replays
  one native UPDATE carrying the final payload, and the child follows.
- D62 (r16, review F2): link-relation resolution downgrades only the
  explicitly supported missing-table condition; every other catalog
  failure is fatal to the statement. r15 suppressed every resolution
  error in both the prepare-time resolver and the ferry staging path,
  so a transient Engine.Database or Database.Relation failure could
  commit user rows while their links were silently skipped — and a
  later apply treats missing provenance as PROVEN ABSENCE, replaying
  DELETE semantics including destructive delete cascades. Resolution
  now classifies: the pre-upgrade missing mo_data_branch_update_link
  (and only that table-miss shape) degrades to legacy replay and
  latches the sticky disable; any other error propagates through
  operator Prepare and the UpdateFlushS3Info ferry staging so an
  injected transient catalog failure aborts user rows and provenance
  writes together (I7 atomicity). Pinned by
  TestResolvePkMoveLinkSourceErrorClassification (missing table
  degrades and latches; transient catalog error fatal, never latches;
  relation-level failure fatal unless it is the missing table; a
  missing database is never the degradable shape) and
  TestPreparePropagatesPkMoveLinkResolutionErrors (generic catalog
  failure aborts Prepare; missing link table degrades with the sticky
  disable), RED -> GREEN archived /tmp/e10_red_f2.log.
- D63 (r16, review F3): coordinator-side provenance retention is
  admission-bounded inside the committing workspace, the layer D60's
  producer budget cannot reach. Producer spill waves stage their rows
  back through source.Write into the committing workspace, which the
  pre-commit dump explicitly excludes link inserts from, so r15
  accumulated every link row of every wave in coordinator memory.
  Each staged link batch's bytes are now reserved at staging time
  against pkMoveLinkCoordinatorBudget (64MB default,
  test-injectable); admission failure aborts the statement atomically
  (user rows and links commit or fail together), and the
  prune/reset paths release the accounted bytes per kept, pruned, or
  rolled-back batch so the same transaction can run many spill waves
  without retained bytes growing with the statement. Pinned by
  TestPkMoveLinkCoordinatorBudgetWaves (several producer spill waves
  through the REAL workspace: retained bytes stay bounded, and the
  injected budget failure aborts atomically with nothing committed)
  and TestPkMoveLinkCoordinatorBudgetPruneAndRelease, RED -> GREEN
  archived /tmp/e10_red_f3.log.
- D64 (r16, review F4): every temporary provenance spill object has
  exactly one cleanup owner — the producing statement's spill
  lifecycle — across success, failure, and crash recovery. r15
  persisted spill objects through the objectio sinker and dropped the
  file references after copying block info: neither the receiver
  (which stages decoded ROWS, not the objects) nor Close (memory
  only) nor transaction GC (which discovers only workspace file
  entries) ever deleted them, so even successful spills leaked
  persistent orphan objects, contradicting D60's ordinary-GC
  assumption. Spill groups now write under an ownership marker job
  named pk-move-link-spill-<uuid> with a 6-hour GC protection window;
  successful receiver consumption frees retained structures and
  deletes the objects and markers; statement reset and error paths
  reclaim them; a group whose ownership marker itself fails is
  deleted INLINE and the spill fails closed; and crash recovery
  replays the markers through the existing GC handoff so a reclaimed
  object can never be mistaken for live uncommitted output. Pinned by
  TestPkMoveLinkSpillObjectsHaveCleanupOwner (successful consumption
  reclaims; aborted-statement reset reclaims; marker failure deletes
  inline and fails closed), RED -> GREEN archived /tmp/e10_red_f4.log.
- D65 (r16, review F5): statement-boundary workspace dumps keep every
  link owner table's staged inserts in memory, so the workspace
  identities recorded on a link survive for the WHOLE transaction and
  same-transaction chaining cannot sever. r15's forced flush dropped
  the owner batch's rowid vector and wrote the rows into an
  uncommitted object: the first move's link named workspace
  identities that no longer existed anywhere, the second move's link
  named the physical object row, and the exact successor comparison
  could not join them (key 3 never committed an intermediate image),
  so the apply reached the D51 unresolved abort for a perfectly
  honest 2 -> 3 -> 4 chain. dumpInsertBatchLocked now collects the
  owner table ids named by the transaction's staged link batches
  (pkMoveStagedLinkOwnerTablesLocked, reading the link table id
  column) and, for !dumpAll boundary dumps only, skips catalog
  resolution for those tables AND keeps their in-memory INSERT
  entries; the commit dump (dumpAll) flushes everything after the
  final prune, when intra-transaction identity matching is settled.
  Pinned by TestPkMoveDumpKeepsLinkOwnerTables (owner set scan;
  staged links keep their owner table in memory; tables no link
  references dump as before), RED -> GREEN archived /tmp/e10_red_f5.log,
  and the BVT ews_ (MERGE) and ewsp_ (PICK) sections forcing
  fj/cn/workspace_force_flush between two moves: 2 recorded links, the
  chain folds to key 4, and the child follows; the filler table proves
  unrelated tables still dump.
- D66 (r16, review F6): fold planning excludes self-dependencies the
  way the apply ranker already does, so a return to the original key
  is plan shape, never a key-rotation cycle. Two separately committed
  source updates 2 -> 3 -> 2 resolve through the advancing-timestamp
  chain into one fold whose departure and arrival share key 2; r15's
  planner counted the fold itself as a prerequisite when finalPK
  equaled oldKey, produced a single self-dependent fold, and aborted
  under D57 with "key rotation cycle" — rejecting both a net no-op
  (unchanged payload) and a valid in-place payload change at the
  original key. The producer planner now drops self edges exactly as
  the downstream ranker does: homecoming folds apply as native
  in-place UPDATEs (changed payload) or as in-place no-ops (identical
  image), the child never moves, and genuine multi-row rotations keep
  the D57 loud abort (the ecyc_/ecp_ cycle BVT oracles are unchanged
  and stay green in the regenerated results). Pinned by
  TestAssemblePkMoveFoldPlan subtests
  return_to_the_original_key_folds_as_an_in-place_update and
  return_with_unchanged_payload_still_folds_in_place, RED -> GREEN
  archived /tmp/e10_red_f6.log, and the BVT ero_/eru_ (MERGE) and
  erop_/erup_ (PICK) sections: 2 recorded links each, the changed
  payload lands as (2, 'two-b') with the child untouched, and the
  unchanged payload applies as a no-op.
- D67 (r17, review F1, extends D35): a durable row's origin stays
  pinned across a statement-boundary workspace spill. The r16
  keep-owner-tables rule keyed on staged links, but a payload edit
  recorded its origin under the replacement workspace rowid BEFORE
  any move link existed; the forced flush between the edit and the
  move then rewrote the edited row into an uncommitted object and
  stripped its workspace rowid, and the later move's link named the
  object rowid instead of the durable tombstone — the apply read the
  tombstone as unproven and replayed DELETE+INSERT, destroying the
  child through ON DELETE CASCADE (live RED /tmp/e11_live_red_f1.log
  on the era-10 binary: child EMPTY). The dump keep set is now built
  from pinned ROW IDS, and the origin ledger's keys ALWAYS pin (its
  values pin while they still name workspace stage rows): the edited
  row survives the flush, the move's link names the durable
  tombstone, and MERGE/PICK fold to one native UPDATE with the child
  following (live GREEN /tmp/e11_live_green_f1.log; BVT eef_/eefp_).
- D68 (r17, review F2, refines D65): the keep decision is per batch
  by row-id membership, never per table. D65 made statement-boundary
  dumps skip every link OWNER table, but a single staged link then
  disabled spilling for the whole table: one move plus arbitrarily
  many large INSERTs pinned user rows in memory until exhaustion,
  and the coordinator budget never saw them. The pin set (staged
  links' old/new row ids, origin-ledger keys plus live workspace-
  stage values, null-heal targets) keeps exactly the batches that
  carry provenance-pinned rows; sibling batches of the same table
  still dump, so ordinary workspace spilling stays effective
  (TestPkMoveDumpKeepsPinnedRows sibling subtests; RED
  /tmp/e11_red_f2.log pkCount 2 -> 0). D65's contract stands: every
  row a same-transaction chain still needs stays in memory, and the
  ews_/ewsp_ chain oracles stay green.
- D69 (r17, review F3, refines D63): consumed marker storage is
  released before provenance admission. Every eligible non-key
  UPDATE emits markers; once fillPkMoveLinkNewRowIDsLocked consumed
  them all, vector.Shrink left a zero-row batch whose retained
  varlena areas still entered appendWorkspaceEntryLocked and the
  D63 budget, so a marker-only wave failed with a provenance-budget
  error while moving no keys. Zero-row link batches are now Cleaned
  and return before the dump loop and before
  admitPkMoveLinkBatchLocked: markers that no longer carry lineage
  hold no workspace footprint and no budget
  (TestPkMoveConsumedMarkersKeepNoWorkspaceFootprint; RED
  /tmp/e11_red_f3.log).
- D70 (r17, review F4): a PROVEN same-transaction return to the
  original key resolves. The revisit guard rejected any revisit
  whose commit timestamp had not strictly advanced; two moves
  2 -> 3 -> 2 within one transaction share one commit timestamp,
  so the recorded homecoming hit pkMoveUnresolved and MERGE/PICK
  aborted even though explicit workspace identities join both moves.
  The guard now fails closed only on a strictly backward birth
  certificate (chainTS.LT); an equal-timestamp revisit is exactly
  the recorded same-transaction homecoming and resolves through the
  unchanged walk. Changed payloads land as in-place native UPDATEs,
  identical images as no-ops; genuine multi-row rotations keep the
  D57 loud abort (ecyc_/ecp_ oracles unchanged). Live pair
  /tmp/e11_live_red_f4.log (unresolved abort with 2 links) vs
  /tmp/e11_live_green_f4.log; BVT ehc_/ehu_ (MERGE) and ehcp_/ehup_
  (PICK).
- D71 (r17, review F5): proven TERMINAL deletion is a defined
  verdict, not incomplete provenance. A lineage moved by a link
  whose tail is a same-key tombstone with no later continuation has
  COMPLETE evidence of deletion; the walk classified it
  pkMoveUnresolved, so even a conflict-free merge on a table without
  foreign keys aborted. The walk now returns pkMoveProvenDeleted for
  that shape (a tail taken with no replacement), the apply replays
  the deletion natively: no-FK destinations delete the row,
  ON DELETE CASCADE destinations delete the row and the child,
  RESTRICT destinations reject loudly and statement-atomically.
  Tripwires keep the boundary honest: a tail that leaked past a
  cross-hop continuation and any out-of-window tail stay
  pkMoveUnresolved. Live pair /tmp/e11_live_red_f5.log vs
  /tmp/e11_live_green_f5.log; BVT etn_/etc_/etr_ (MERGE) and
  etnp_/etcp_/etrp_ (PICK).
- D72 (r17, review F6): terminal spill cleanup is cancellation-safe
  and failure-atomic. Pipeline.Cleanup cancels proc.Ctx BEFORE
  operator Reset, and LocalFS/S3FS reject canceled contexts, so the
  cleanup path used a dead context and left spills for the six-hour
  recovery window; and an object-delete failure still released the
  marker, permanently dropping recovery ownership. Cleanup now runs
  on a fresh single-call-bounded context, deletes each object first,
  and releases its marker only after the object is confirmed gone —
  a failed object delete keeps the marker so crash recovery still
  owns the object. TestPkMoveLinkSpillTerminalCleanup (RED
  /tmp/e11_red_f6.log) drives the probes through canceled processes
  and injected delete failures.
- D73 (r17, review F7, refines D64): durable cleanup ownership is
  established BEFORE the object can persist. The delegate recorded
  the marker job after the sinker had already written and synced the
  object, so a crash in between — or a marker failure racing a
  failed inline delete — left an orphan no GC path could discover
  (txn crash GC sees only workspace file entries). The sinker now
  exposes WithUnpublishedNameObserver, fired immediately before Sync
  with the unpublished object name (the pipeline-submit path
  rejects the observer), and the delegate records the
  pk-move-link-spill-<uuid> marker there: the marker exists before
  the bytes could have persisted, marker creation failure deletes
  the object inline and fails closed, and ambiguous Sync failures
  keep the same fail-closed shape. TestPkMoveLinkSpillMarkerPrecedesObject
  (RED /tmp/e11_red_f7.log) pins the ordering and the failure
  matrix.
- D74 (r18, review F1, extends D35/D67): a by-key lineage binding dies
  through the PRODUCTION deletion boundary, not only through staged
  DELETE entries. The era-11 heal checked binding validity only against
  the staged delete stream, and deletes DIVERTED before the first move
  link (uncommitted-object deletes removed at the txn write boundary,
  including the delete of a previously edited S3 row) never retired the
  binding: an unrelated same-key reinsert could then heal back to the
  original durable identity, and a later move would fold against the
  resurrected lineage — ON UPDATE CASCADE reparenting children that the
  declared delete had already removed. Every diverted delete now records
  a retire-death note unconditionally (before any link exists), the heal
  is tri-state (visible / retired / absent), and a retired heal kills the
  candidate link into pkMoveKilledLinks so the prune drops it and the
  replay keeps plain DELETE+INSERT semantics. Rollback removes exactly
  its own statement's retire notes. TestPkMoveDivertedDeleteRetiresLineageBinding
  (RED /tmp/e12_red_f1.log); BVT edv_/edr_ (MERGE), edvp_/edrp_ (PICK).
- D75 (r18, review F2, refines D29/D30): workspace-to-S3 continuity is
  REPRESENTED EXPLICITLY, and replacement harvesting excludes rows the
  statement has already logically deleted. The harvest folded only staged
  INSERTs, so after a workspace move 2->3 the deleted workspace row
  (still pending batchSelectList removal) could be returned as an S3
  same-key edit's replacement; the commit-time shrink then removed it and
  the prune dropped the genuine move link, reverting the apply to
  DELETE+INSERT. The harvest now folds with a batchSelectList-guarded
  selection (plus a generation-stamped cache invalidated with the
  selection list), and an S3-route marker whose pre-image is the staged
  new identity of an existing workspace link NULL-retargets that link
  (removing any null-heal anchored on the consumed pre-image) with a
  per-statement undo record, so the chain continues onto its S3
  replacement explicitly. TestPkMoveHarvestExcludesSelectedRows,
  TestPkMoveWorkspaceToS3RetargetToNull (RED /tmp/e12_red_f2h.log,
  /tmp/e12_red_f2c.log); BVT ewt_ (MERGE), ewtp_ (PICK).
- D76 (r18, review F3, refines D64/D73): spill-object cleanup ownership
  TRANSFERS to the consumer on successful ferry publication. Producer
  teardown used to reclaim every produced spill object unconditionally,
  but the receiver reads the objects lazily after operator reset, so a
  delayed coordinator could hold valid block metadata whose object was
  already deleted. The ferried block-info batch now carries a named
  pk_move_link_spill_marker column (located by attribute name — the
  sinker block-info layout varies — never by position), publication marks
  the spill record published, producer teardown reclaims only the
  unpublished remainder, and the consumer deletes object + marker after
  its read succeeds (a failed consumer reclaim warns and keeps the
  marker, so the D64 crash GC still owns recovery).
  TestPkMoveLinkSpillConsumerOwnership (teardown-before-read-back and
  failed-reclaim subtests; RED /tmp/e12_red_f3a.log, /tmp/e12_red_f3b.log).
- D77 (r18, review F4, refines D63/D69): the coordinator retention budget
  counts ALL retained provenance bookkeeping, not only retained link
  batches. The per-key/per-statement marker maps and the by-key lineage
  stacks live across statement boundaries unspilled and unbudgeted (D69
  released the consumed batch storage but the bookkeeping maps stayed
  charged to nothing), so marker-heavy waves on large non-key updates
  could accumulate unaccounted heap. pkMoveBookkeepBytesLocked now
  measures the bookkeeping, checkPkMoveBookkeepBudgetLocked runs at every
  fill end, and admission charges bookkeeping together with retained
  batch bytes against the same injectable budget (zero disables the
  check, matching D63). TestPkMoveBookkeepBudget (RED
  /tmp/e12_red_f4a.log, /tmp/e12_red_f4b.log).
- D78 (r19, review F1, refines D30/D44): an edit-first lineage
  switching to the S3 route composes the lineage's already-recorded
  durable origin instead of binding the workspace pre-image literally.
  bindPkMoveKeyLineageLocked consulted only the exact origin map for
  workspace pre-images and excluded the generation when that carried
  nothing, so the sequence workspace edit -> S3 edit -> move recorded
  the move's old side as the UNCOMMITTED-CN identity of the workspace
  row. That identity never appears in the committed change stream, so
  the consumer treated the anchor as absent provenance and replayed
  DELETE+INSERT — RESTRICT rejecting loudly, ON DELETE CASCADE deleting
  children a native UPDATE would have kept. The workspace branch now
  composes the by-key binding's recorded origin, else the exact origin
  map entry the earlier edit left; a generation with neither (an
  independently inserted row) stays unbound and anchors literally, the
  same distinctness rule Pass 2 applies to resolved markers.
  TestPkMoveWorkspaceSwitchBindsDurableOrigin (composition, independent
  distinctness, murdered lineage, rollback; RED /tmp/e13_red_ut_f1.log);
  live pair /tmp/e13_live_red_f1.log (era-12 binary: link anchored on
  01A156BB522975C4A59699F29B48C1D90000000000000000, MERGE leaves the
  child EMPTY through ON DELETE CASCADE) vs
  /tmp/e13_live_green_f1.log (era-13 binary: anchor
  01A15790C8677D32A2E7488F0CA962690000000000000000, MERGE/PICK parent
  (3,'edited2') + child (1,3), byte-identical to the native controls);
  BVT esw_ (MERGE), eswp_ (PICK).
- D79 (r19, review F2, refines D67/D77): workspace dumps keep exactly
  the rows staged provenance references, and post-fill bookkeeping
  growth is budget-checked at the write boundary. The era-12 answer
  recorded spilled identities for every dumped INSERT batch whenever
  any staged link existed and retained them unbudgeted (the
  pkMoveSpilledInserts ledger pkMoveBookkeepBytesLocked never
  measured), so one move plus unrelated spill waves grew uncharged
  heap until commit. The dump gate now computes the staged-link pin
  set (staged links and their origins/heals) and keeps only INSERT
  BATCHES that carry a pinned row: provenance-referenced rows stay
  workspace rows until the final prune settles identity matching,
  unrelated waves spill exactly as before, and the spilled-inserts
  ledger is gone because nothing it tracked can remain
  provenance-relevant after the spill (pin-keep makes it
  unreachable). Diverted-delete bookkeeping after the last fill is
  checked by notePkMoveDivertedDeletes behind one critical section
  (deleteBatch runs without txn.Lock for parallel UpdateWriteS3
  producers) and the error propagates atomically through the new
  deleteBatch signature. TestPkMoveDumpKeepsPinnedRows (pin set
  composition, link-pinned/origin-pinned keep, unrelated wave retains
  nothing, no-provenance tables unchanged),
  TestPkMoveDivertedDeleteBudgetWave (retirement wave crosses the
  injected budget, post-final-fill dead-pk wave crosses, zero budget
  disables, rollback releases; RED /tmp/e13_red_ut_f2.log, RC=1 ->
  /tmp/e13_ut_f2_green2.log).
- D80 (r19, review F3, refines D76): spill ownership state is
  execution-scoped and protection leases re-mint after expiry. The
  r18 producer kept PUBLISHED records in its ledger and never cleared
  the seen set or the armed lease, but Prepare reuses the writer
  across pipeline executions, so a second execution inherited the
  first execution's expiry window; after expiry plus the GC TTL a
  freshly spilled object of the new execution was reclaimable before
  its consumer read it back. Terminal cleanup now sheds published
  records WITHOUT deleting their files (the ferry consumer owns
  those), reset clears pkMoveLinkSpillFiles/Seen/Job/Valid after
  cleanup, and trackPkMoveLinkSpillObject re-mints the lease whenever
  the armed window expired, never extending a dead window over a live
  unconsumed object. TestS3WriterSpillOwnershipResetsBetweenExecutions
  (reset drops transferred records without deleting their files;
  expired inherited lease re-mints on the next spill; RED
  /tmp/e13_red_ut_f3.log -> /tmp/e13_ut_f3_green.log).
- D81 (r19, review F4, refines D75): the workspace-to-S3 NULL
  retarget rides the same continuity index as the resolved-marker
  path. retargetPkMoveLinkNewRowIDsToNullLocked scanned every staged
  link row and every heal binding once per unresolved workspace
  marker, so N moves followed by N S3-route edits cost O(N^2) under
  txn.Lock. The fill now builds the continuity index lazily once per
  staging statement (skipping fills of nothing but straight moves)
  and the null retarget resolves its targets through
  idx.byNewRow[preID] with per-statement undo and workspace
  accounting exactly like the rowid retarget; freshly nulled rows
  re-key into the index's NULL-identity side so later resolved
  markers of the same fill still bind them.
  TestPkMoveWorkspaceToS3RetargetToNullMultiRow pins correctness;
  BenchmarkPkMoveWorkspaceToS3NullRetarget over 16/64/256 links drops
  from 72409/433181/5572600 ns-op (prefix scan, /tmp/e13_bench_f4_prefix.log)
  to 49176/159880/959043 (indexed, /tmp/e13_bench_f4_postfix.log) — a
  5.8x win at 256 and scaling flattened from quadratic to linear.
- D82 (r20, review F1, refines D74): raw workspace deaths retire
  lineage bindings through the shared deletion boundary. D74's
  boundary covered diverted deletes — rows whose delete had to divert
  to per-block offsets because the row lived in an uncommitted CN
  object. A delete whose row lived in an uncommitted INSERT batch
  never diverts: deleteBatch excludes it via batchSelectList and the
  row vanishes with no tombstone, no divert record, and no staged
  DELETE, so lookupPkMoveKeyLineageLocked's split scan and the
  retire-death ledger both saw nothing and a by-key lineage binding
  could outlive the murdered generation. deleteBatch now notes the
  swallowed rows through notePkMoveSwallowedDeletes with the same
  retireDeaths/deadPks ledgers, participation gates (bindings gate
  retirement notes; surviving link rows gate the pk-level death set),
  coordinator budget discipline, and statement-rollback ownership as
  the diverted boundary, so retirement, same-statement explanation,
  and rollback revival behave identically for both row classes.
  Apply-visible outcomes on the era-13 binary were already fail-closed
  for this shape — the recorded anchor was an uncommitted identity the
  committed stream never shows — and the boundary fix grounds the kill
  at the ledger so no later anchor-composition route can bypass it.
  TestPkMoveSwallowedDeletesRetireLineage (murdered binding retires;
  participating table reaches the pk-level death ledger; same-
  statement staged departures stay explained; statement rollback
  revives the binding; no-provenance transactions record nothing; the
  budget bounds the wave; archived RED /tmp/e14_red_ut_f1.log RC=1 ->
  GREEN /tmp/e14_ut_f1_f3_triage2.log RC=0); BVT esz_/eszr_ (MERGE
  cascade and RESTRICT) and eszp_/eszpr_ (PICK keys(2) cascade and
  RESTRICT).
- D83 (r20, review F2, refines D47): direct unbranched DROP honors
  snapshot grounding exactly like the orphan-parent flow, resolved
  from caller-known names. The DROP TABLE reclamation deleted all
  links whenever the table carried no current branch metadata. A
  table with retained snapshots bracketing a move could then be
  dropped before any branch existed, and the historical branch
  instantiated later from those snapshots diffed history under the
  dropped table id with its links already gone, replaying
  DELETE+INSERT (RESTRICT rejecting loudly, ON DELETE CASCADE
  destroying children). The drop path now routes through
  reclaimUnbranchedDropPkMoveLinks with the drop statement's own
  database/table names: the snapshot probe matches kind/user/level
  coverage (cluster/account/database/table, D47's coverage rule),
  grounded keeps, probe errors keep with a WARN instead of failing
  the drop, a name miss keeps (fail-closed), and nothing grounding
  reclaims exactly as before — no retention leak. The by-id relation
  probe survives only as the nameless-call fallback because the drop
  transaction retires the mo_tables row before reclamation runs, so
  a by-id probe on the drop path always misses (see D86). TRUNCATE
  keeps routing the alter lineage machinery and reclaims through its
  own flow. TestReclaimUnbranchedDropPkMoveLinks (no-snapshot and
  unrelated-snapshot reclaim; table/database/cluster/account coverage
  keeps; gone-name keep; probe-error keep; caller-name bypass and
  fallback cases; archived RED /tmp/e14_red_ut_f2.log RC=1 -> GREEN
  /tmp/e14_ut_f2_triage.log RC=0, repair GREEN /tmp/e14_ut_f2_fix2.log
  RC=0);
  live evidence on the era-14 v2 binary /tmp/e14_live_green_f2c.log
  (snapshots bracketing a move + drop: links 1 -> 1, MERGE and PICK
  keys(2) replay dst-keep/src-insert byte-identical to the live-parent
  controls; no-snapshot drop reclaims 1 -> 0; TRUNCATE + snapshot
  keeps 1 -> 1; RESTRICT flavor stays un-rejected) vs the era-13
  defect /tmp/e14_live_red_f2.log (drop reclaimed 1 -> 0 under
  retained snapshots) and the v1 repair-shape defect
  /tmp/e14_live_red_f2b.log (degenerate keeps through the by-id
  probe); BVT esy_/esyx_/esyr_/esy2_/esy3_ (MERGE) and
  esyp_/esypx_/esyp2_ (PICK).
- D84 (r20, review F3, refines D79): pin-retained workspace bytes are
  charged to the coordinator budget at the dump gate. D79's pin-keep
  gate retains whole INSERT batches carrying any pinned row — the pin
  is row-based while retention is batch-wide, so an origin-pinned row
  from an ordinary non-key update keeps its entire batch — while the
  budget measured link batches and bookkeeping only. Repeated
  single-row updates of wide rows could therefore retain workspace
  bytes far beyond the 64 MiB bound while provenance accounting
  stayed small, and even forced workspace dumps skipped them. The
  dump gate now measures pkMovePinRetainedBytes with the exact keep
  predicate (in-memory INSERT batch holding at least one pinned row)
  before mutating the workspace, so an over-budget decision rejects
  the dump statement-atomically with no batches moved; the budget
  check charges staged link bytes + bookkeeping + pin-retained bytes,
  the admission check counts the same, a later dump releasing a batch
  drops it from the measure, and a zero budget disables the charging
  exactly as before. TestPkMoveDumpKeepsPinnedRows new subtests (the
  measure matches the keep predicate on a populated and an empty
  workspace; an over-bound dump is rejected before any workspace
  mutation with the kept set byte-identical; exact-fit retention
  passes and stays charged after the dump so a post-dump wave fails;
  a zero budget never refuses; archived RED /tmp/e14_red_ut_f3.log
  RC=1 -> GREEN /tmp/e14_ut_f1_f3_triage2.log RC=0).
- D85 (r20, review F4, refines D15): stream evidence builds one
  version index per key instead of rescanning per tombstone.
  capturePkMoveStreamEvidenceBounded fetched every version of a key
  and decoded each once per tombstone of that key: K tombstones over
  V versions cost O(KV) decodes, paid by every apply-capable diff
  because constructChangeHandle enables version preservation for all
  of them — including stable-key histories with no moves at all. The
  capture now materializes the key's versions once per shard into two
  sorted views (the key-level birth multiset for the recency tier and
  per-row-id birth lists for the exact tier) and resolves each
  tombstone by binary search with identical pairing semantics: exact
  row-id match first with recency, otherwise the newest birth
  strictly below the delete across every row id, ties in either tier
  record nothing, undecodable rows are skipped, and a key the data
  map does not hold is fetched once and pairs none.
  TestCapturePkMoveStreamEvidenceKeyIndexReuse (the data side is
  fetched once per touched key instead of once per tombstone,
  pairings byte-identical, the absent key fetched once),
  TestCapturePkMoveStreamEvidenceTierOneTieStaysClosed (a tier-1 tie
  suppresses tier 2 exactly as the scan did),
  BenchmarkCapturePkMoveStreamEvidenceKeyChurn at 64/256/1024
  same-key tombstones: 14328750/173126667/2605778458 ns-op with
  per-tombstone rescans (/tmp/e14_bench_f4_prefix.log) vs
  691583/1171084/4770083 ns-op indexed
  (/tmp/e14_bench_f4_postfix.log) — 546x at 1024, scaling flattened
  from quadratic to near-linear with wide-keyspace parity (no
  constant-work regression over many keys).
- D86 (r20, found while answering r20 F2 and the BVT authoring; not a
  review finding): three boundary facts r20 established. (a) The drop
  path cannot probe its own relation by id: the drop transaction
  retires the mo_tables row before reclamation runs, so D83's first
  shape (the era-14 v1 binary, which probed the relation by id and
  treated a miss as grounded-keeps) failed closed into keep for every
  unbranched drop, defective in the retention-leak direction; the
  repaired flow
  resolves groundness from the caller-known names and keeps the by-id
  probe only for nameless internal callers. (b) Verified capability
  boundary: a historical branch instantiated from snapshots diffs an
  ancestor recorded move as dst-keep/src-insert with NO destination
  delete, identical whether the ancestor's table is live or dropped —
  the snapshot-grounded retention protects this transparency contract,
  and reclaim fires only when no historical access path remains; the
  "reclaim now, branch later from snapshots" shape is unreachable
  because instantiating a branch from a snapshot requires a snapshot
  whose coverage itself grounds the table. r20 therefore proves
  retention, no-leak, and drop transparency, and deliberately does
  not promise a historical ancestor-move UPDATE fold (no such fold
  exists on any base; the destination keeps its row and the replay
  never deletes it). (c) BVT prefix ownership: era-14's first
  esx_/esxp_ section prefixes collided with era-5's esx_ sections in
  the shared MERGE/PICK files (the regenerated oracle exposed the
  collision as `table esx_p already exists` and duplicate-key errors);
  the era-14 sections were renamed esz_/eszr_ (MERGE) and
  eszp_/eszpr_ (PICK) with the era-5 fixture byte-intact, and both
  oracles were regenerated and re-reviewed statement-by-statement.
- D87 (r21, review F2 disposition: REJECTED — no behavior change;
  refines D18/D28): the r20 pre-PR review asked to persist explicit
  continuity so a same-key delete-then-insert in one transaction
  stays distinguishable from a same-key UPDATE across commits, citing
  the TestResolvePkMoveChain oracle case where an independent
  `DELETE 2; INSERT (2,'unrelated')` transaction followed by an
  `UPDATE 2->3` folds. The finding was verified at its cited loci
  (data_branch_pk_move_link.go:1264 anchor-side birth-equals-deletion
  tie, :1395-1419 link-less tail) and then rejected on three grounds
  established in the repository itself. (a) Stream
  indistinguishability: a committed same-transaction same-key
  delete+insert pair emits exactly the committed change-stream
  signature that multi_update emits for a stable-key UPDATE (one
  tombstone + one insert at the same key in one transaction), which
  the upstream-merged #27996 series defines as native UPDATE replay
  — refusing the tie would break precisely the same-instant re-birth
  chains #27996 requires to fold, and would make data-branch apply
  diverge from native replay and from D28's same-transaction
  non-key-update continuity contract. (b) No emission order survives:
  mini-delta update emission is DML-order dependent, so neither the
  anchor side nor the tail side can order the delete against the
  insert without new durable identity — i.e., the fix the finding
  demands is the durable-operation-identity protocol this design
  already scopes to pk moves only, and extending it to stable-key
  same-transaction delete+insert would rewrite ordinary DML
  provenance semantics (out of scope, and contradicting D18's
  same-transaction intermediate-key reuse rule which relies on this
  exact tie). (c) The cited oracle case is the intended D18/D28
  behavior: the pre-existing independent delete+insert transaction
  REWRITES key 2 (a delete+insert at the same key replays natively
  as delete+insert, children deleted through the declared ON DELETE
  action — the destination's original row is not silently preserved
  by any replay), and the subsequent move chain 2->3 continues from
  the key that exists. The oracle's fold expectation stands; the UT
  comment at data_branch_pk_move_link_test.go:1073 now records this
  rationale and the tx_p counterexample note. No code changed.
- D88 (r21, review F1, refines D35): provenance remaps across the
  workspace shrink boundary. shrinkWorkspaceEntryBatchLocked
  renumbers surviving row offsets when deleteBatch's batchSelectList
  swallow path shrinks an in-memory INSERT batch, and — unlike the
  batch-compaction path — remapped no provenance: two rows moved in
  one workspace batch with the first then deleted left the survivor's
  recorded replacement identity stale, and the subsequent prune
  dropped its valid link, replaying DELETE+INSERT and destroying its
  child through the declared ON DELETE action. The shrink now

- D93 (r22, review F1, refines D88): the shrink remap builds the new
  origins from an immutable snapshot. D88's remapPkMoveLinkRowIDsLocked

- D100 (r23, review F4, refines D11's overflow discipline): window

  lookup. The link provider scanned the table's entire historical
  link prefix for the whole walk and table-wide disabled itself once

  links accumulate across transactions beyond any writer-side budget

  keys(0) of a link-free payload update classify every anchor
  unresolved and abort against destination-held anchors. The prefix
  scan now records overflow windows/keys and answers per key:
  anchors whose own windows overflowed keep the fail-closed verdict,
  while anchors unreachable from overflowed history resolve from
  their complete windows and unrelated history can no longer abort
  them. Straddling-transaction correctness is unchanged — the
  per-key probe windows still carry the NF7 create-ts lower bound
  and commit-ts upper bound. TestPkMoveLinkProbeBudgetAndBounds
  subtests 'window overflow narrows to per-key probing instead of
  disabling' and 'unrelated overflow history cannot abort a small
  link-free pick' (archived RED /tmp/e17_red_ut_f4.log RC=1 ->
  GREEN /tmp/e17_ut_f4.log RC=0). The live witness needs the

- D113 (r26, F3 residual found by the era-20 live gates, refines

  old->new mapping into provenance, but the object route never
  retired the superseded source entries: writeFileLocked appended the

  distinguish transfer twins from genuine double-deaths (no durable
  mapping), so the fix is producer-side: when — and only when — the
  transaction holds pk-move provenance (the D110 gate), the flow
  runs pass-through: rows whose target object died ride the D110
  re-key, every other row travels VERBATIM through the leftover
  staging into the same sinker, and after the replacement publishes
  the caller retires the consumed input stats from this table's
  file-backed DELETE entries. Retirement keeps the writes slice
  indices stable — the established nil-slot convention releases a
  fully covered entry in place, a partially covered one shrinks — so
  statement offsets never shift; retired stats deep-copy into a
  statement-tagged ledger whose files are unpublished garbage in
  EVERY close outcome and whose entries RollbackLastStatement
  resurrects byte-for-byte whenever the tail cut discarded the
  replacement publications (statementSeq >= rolledStmt), and

  keep the selective staging: their pending originals must keep
  publishing, so the gate costs them nothing. UT

  untouched, stash membership follows the retired set exactly,

  exactly once — accounting asserted at every step) both GREEN

- D114 (r27, review F1, refines D113): every persisted-DELETE scan
  honors the nil-slot lifecycle. D113 retirement releases a fully
  covered entry's batch in place while preserving its DELETE type
  and fileName — the retirement invariants demand writes-slice
  indices stay put for statement offsets — but the transfer
  collector inside ConstructCNTombstoneObjectsTransferFlow
  dereferenced e.bat.Vecs[0] for any matching DELETE entry, so a
  second qualifying transfer window inside the same explicit
  transaction scanned the retired shells and died whenever the
  protective dump sweep had not run between the retirement and the
  scan. (The dump sweep at every statement-END IncrStatementID
  removes nil slots before clean statements end, so the unguarded
  window is a merge commit landing between retirement and the next
  statement's begin on a path with no dump in between — the
  statement-begin AdvanceSnapshot transfer path; the r27 live
  batteries' two-window shape therefore could not crash the pre-fix
  binary, matching the review's own 'when nil-slot compaction has
  not run' caveat.) The collector — extracted as
  collectCnTombstoneDeleteStats — now guards the slot
  (fileName/DELETE type/bat non-nil/non-empty), which loses
  nothing: a retired shell's replacement already published, and a
  statement rollback re-appends a LIVE tail entry when it undoes
  one. A package-wide audit confirmed every other persisted-DELETE
  consumer (table discovery, the retirement matcher, the pk-dup
  scan) already guarded the lifecycle, so the collector was the
  sole unguarded consumer and the guard closes the whole class at
  one chokepoint. UT

  /tmp/e21_green_ut_f1.log RC=0) enumerates retired shells, live
  entries, wrong-table and non-DELETE neighbors through the exact
  production path; the live regression the review demanded — two
  qualifying transfer windows in one explicit transaction, a
  statement rollback between them, successful commit, one
  publication per tombstone identity — is pinned by the etkf12_
  (MERGE) and etkf12p_ (PICK) BVT sections and the archived live
  GREEN /tmp/e21_green_live_f1.log RC=0 (both windows transferred,
  advance probes 4/4, four link rows, parents 12-15 with children

- D115 (r27, review F2, refines D108): a delete-compaction wave is
  failure-atomic across statements. D108 surfaced worker failures
  to the boundary, but the pre-r27 boundary still released the
  original INSERT batches BEFORE the workers succeeded, and
  IncrStatementID runs the maintenance before recording the next
  statement offset — so with the default
  mo_rollback_txn_on_error=0 the joined internal error received
  only a statement rollback that truncates the latest tail and
  could never restore entries released from OLDER successful
  statements: a spilled replacement from an earlier UPDATE could
  disappear while its committed-row DELETE remained. The boundary
  now stages each object's work in a slot (original untouched
  until publication), publishes replacements and releases
  originals in one ordered pass AFTER waiter.Wait() returns clean,
  and on any failure runs cleanFailedWave — reclaiming only the
  replacement object's own file by newStats[i].ObjectName() and
  restoring every slot's original state — so the joined error
  propagates as an ordinary statement error, and the ensuing
  statement rollback restores the pre-boundary state exactly
  (originals never released, unpublished replacements reclaimed,
  already-published tail entries cut with the tail) instead of
  leaving an irreversibly damaged transaction committable. The
  rewritten
  TestPkMoveCompactionPropagatesShadowFailure (archived RED
  /tmp/e21_red_ut_f25.log RC=1 -> GREEN
  /tmp/e21_green_ut_f25.log RC=0) now genuinely asserts the r26
  report's accidentally overclaimed invariants: an injected shadow
  failure inside the rewrite worker aborts the wave, the
  survivors stay readable, the originals are NOT reclaimed, and
  the failed wave leaves the shared-FS file inventory untouched;
  an OLDER statement's spill survives the failed boundary through
  the production RollbackLastStatement arc and the statement
  retries to a clean commit.
- D116 (r27, review F3, refines D113): partial retirement detaches
  before it records. D113's shrink path removed the retired stats
  from the read-visible stash and journaled them as detached
  BEFORE allocating the retained batch — if PreExtend or
  AppendBytes failed mid-shrink, the original entry still carried
  both retired and retained stats while the deferred record
  already treated the retired subset as detached, and statement
  rollback then resurrected that subset a second time through
  resurrectRetiredTransferEntriesLocked, duplicating the tombstone
  publication. The path now builds the retained batch FIRST (with
  failure leaving source entries byte-identical), and swaps
  stash/journal/entry atomically only after every byte landed.

  RED /tmp/e21_red_ut_f3.log RC=1 -> GREEN
  /tmp/e21_green_ut_f3.log RC=0) injects an allocation failure at
  the first shrink (nothing mutates, rollback adds nothing) and at

  the real statement-rollback path, and asserts the original

- D117 (r27, review F4, refines D113): TransferFlow.Close owns the
  leftover batch across every error path. D113's pass-through
  checkouts a separately owned leftover batch from the pool; the

  reader, rekey, sorter, or sinker error between checkout and

  flow's pool reference, and orphanLeftover nils the field after a
