  accounting keeps retained+inflight+reserved <= hardCapacity
  for in-contract producers); a registration whose names
  outnumber the outstanding reservations still registers —
  ownership first — while an ERROR log fires once the
  retained+inflight+reserved total crosses the hard ceiling,
  a violation only out-of-contract production can cause.
  Deterministic proof:
  TestPkMoveOrphanGCHardBoundBackpressureProof (at pinned
  capacity 2 / hard ceiling 4 / 2 reclaim rounds: reserved
  books fill to the ceiling; under sustained delete failure
  every reservation past the ceiling runs exactly its
  bounded rounds over the oldest batch and fails with the
  stable exhaustion error, three further failed attempts
  leave retained pinned and book nothing, and every owned
  file stays on disk; healed, one reclaim round deletes and
  deregisters the whole inventory oldest-registration-first
  before the reservation books, filesystem inventory
  byte-identical) and
  TestPkMoveBoundaryFailsBeforePersistWhenOrphanOwnershipExhausted
  (a real pk-move boundary against the saturated registry
  under sustained failure errors pre-persist, filesystem
  inventory byte-identical to the pre-statement state,
  rollback clean, retry after healing reclaims the garbage
  through its reservation's first round and commits the
  exact surviving rows).
- D134 (r32, review F3, refines D131): the terminal close
  pass is a single bounded flight over a finite snapshot,
  coordinated with the storage's active sweep. D131's
  retireEngineDurableOrphanGC re-snapshotted the shared
  inventory until empty or no progress — another live engine
  registering one name per successful deletion kept
  Engine.Close inside the loop indefinitely — and it cleared
  sweepActive/sweepPending belonging to the other engine's
  in-flight sweep, bypassing D130's single-flight rule and
  duplicating submissions over names already being deleted.
  The pass now snapshots the retained names EXCLUDING the
  active sweep's in-flight set (that sweep owns them), takes
  the storage flight when idle and none when another engine
  holds it, issues each GC-sized chunk exactly once,
  deregisters only confirmed deletions, retains still-failing
  names for the next sweep, and never clears another
  engine's flight state and never loops — registrations
  landing during the pass simply remain owned at return;
  when the pass held the flight itself it clears its own
  flag at the end, and leftover names stay retained under
  the storage key for the next trigger. Deterministic
  proof: TestPkMoveOrphanGCCloseSkipsActiveSweep (a second
  engine's barrier-held sweep owns two in-flight names
  while the closing engine's pass runs: the pass deletes
  around them, confirms and deregisters only the late
  non-inflight name, returns while the pair is still gated,
  leaves the second sweep's sweepActive/inflight state
  untouched, and the completing peer sweep then deletes its
  pair exactly once each) and
  TestPkMoveOrphanGCCloseLeavesLateRegistrationsOwned (the
  pass's barrier-held four-name snapshot succeeded while
  six late registrations from a live peer engine landed
  mid-flight: Close returns after exactly one delete
  attempt with the late names still owned and never
  attempted — the r31 loop re-snapshotted and absorbed
  them in a following pass — and the peer's later sweep
  reclaims them all).
- D135 (r33, review F1, refines D133): every reservation
  transferred into registerDurableOrphanGC settles exactly
  once, whether direct reclamation succeeds or retention
  adopts the name. D133's terminal settlement converted
  outstanding reservations only for names retained past the
  synchronous overflow reclaim (and both close drains hand
  their names over with reservations still booked and no
  subsequent refund); an overflow name whose immediate
  deletion succeeded consumed nothing, leaving a phantom
  reserved slot that pinned the registry entry against
  maybeReleaseEntryLocked and counted into every later
  reservation's used total — a fully recovered registry
  could keep refusing valid producers with the exhaustion
  error forever. The admission's terminal settlement now
  counts the confirm-deleted overflow names together with
  the newly retained failures in the same anonymous
  conversion (min(settled+added, reserved), clamped like
  every other conversion), and the all-success terminal
  settles min(confirmed, reserved) before releasing the
  shell. Deterministic regression:
  TestPkMoveOrphanGCOverflowSuccessSettlesTransferredReservations
  (both overflow reservations booked, one name retained
  under the pinned soft capacity, the overflow name's
  direct reclaim confirmed: reserved settles to zero, the
  confirmed file is gone, the healed sweep releasing the
  retained name frees the whole entry, and a fresh
  reservation books the full hard-ceiling headroom — on
  r32 semantics the phantom slot pins the entry alive and
  the same reservation exhausts) and
  TestPkMoveOrphanGCOverflowMixedResultSettlesExactlyOnce
  (relief batching pinned to one name per attempt by the
  new test-pinnable reliefBatchSize registry field, which
  carries the production default GCBatchOfFileCount: the
  first chunk's delete fails injected, the other two
  confirm; the failed name re-registers past the bound
  while the two confirmed names settle — reserved drops
  from three booked to exactly zero, not the r32 residual
  one, the failed name's file survives for the healed
  sweep, and the drained entry frees for a full-ceiling
  reservation again).
- D136 (r33, review F2, refines D133): a rollback
  resurrection releases the reservations of the retired
  files it returns to publishing workspace ownership.
  retireTransferredTombstoneStatsLocked books one
  reservation per unique retired file name (len(inputs)
  minus slack), and before r33 only gcRetiredTransferFiles
  settled them at close; RollbackLastStatement's
  resurrectRetiredTransferEntriesLocked restored the
  entries' files to workspace ownership and dropped their
  retirement records without releasing those slots, so
  repeated retirement/rollback cycles grew reserved past
  the hard ceiling and exhausted the shared storage budget
  with perfectly healthy deletion — and the existing
  resurrection tests ran with a nil FileService that never
  exercised the accounting. The resurrection now collects
  the unique file names of every entry it fully
  re-appends to the workspace and releases exactly that
  count through releaseDurableOrphanReservation (exactly
  the retirement's unique-name discipline); entries still
  retired after a mid-walk allocation failure keep their
  reservations in the surviving records for the close
  drain, matching D133's ownership-never-dies rule. The
  resurrection loop also rides the package's established
  pkMoveVecAppendBytes seam so the partial-failure
  contract is pinned deterministically in tests.
  Deterministic regression with a real FileService:
  TestPkMoveResurrectionReturnsReservationsAcrossCycles
  (three retire/resurrect cycles under a pinned hard
  ceiling: every cycle's reservations return at
  resurrection, the third retirement books exactly like
  the first — the cycle's own post-resurrection
  assertion catches the very first leaked settlement on
  r32 semantics, where the compounding arithmetic
  (2/4/6 bookings against a 4-slot ceiling) would have
  errored "durable orphan ownership exhausted" against
  an empty retained set by the third retirement — the
  registry releases
  its shell once the last reservations return, and a
  fresh full-ceiling reservation books) and
  TestPkMoveResurrectionPartialFailurePreservesRetiredReservations
  (the seam fails the second entry's batch build inside
  the resurrection: the first entry's file settled its
  reservation exactly once while the still-retired second
  record keeps its own, and the close drain then
  registers and sweeps that file to a byte-identical
  filesystem inventory with the registry released).
- D137 (r34, review F1, refines D129+D103): the boundary
  dump's provenance translation is owned and restored by the
  maintenance window itself, independently of any dirty-object
  wave. D103 (as windowed by D129) translates the
  durable-origin ledger from workspace identities onto spill
  identities the moment a boundary dump's object lands
  (translatePkMoveOriginDumpShadowLocked swaps in a freshly
  rebuilt map), but before r34 the only pre-maintenance
  restore was the wave's pending snapshot — and with no
  diverted deletions the wave never runs, so no
  pendingBoundaryFinalization exists and its discard is a
  no-op. The rollback's tail cut then deletes the spill files
  while the raw batches they re-minted survive in place, the
  statement undo was legitimately cleared once the finished
  statement became irrevocable (D120), and nothing inside the
  window journals origin writes (only the pk-move edit path
  does, unreachable during maintenance) — so a boundary that
  failed after the dump (the RC snapshot/transfer legs) left
  the ledger keyed by dead spill identities, and a later key
  move missed its origin and replayed DELETE+INSERT. The
  window now stages the pre-translation ledger header at the
  first dump translation it hosts and
  RollbackLastStatement restores it at the window's death
  point, after the tail cut and before the wave's pending
  discard — the only ordering under which the three
  window-visible transformations compose: the merge fold
  keeps its re-minted batch cells AND every provenance map
  consistent through the cut on its own (its transformation
  targets state that survives the cut), a completed transfer
  carries provenance onto identities its own pending-transfer
  rollback and retirement resurrection unwind, and the wave's
  pending snapshot, when a wave did run, restores the
  even-earlier pre-carry ledger over the staged one. Restore
  is exact: the translate publishes a fresh map and never
  mutates the staged one in place, in-window map writes are
  all fresh swaps (merge fold, transfer carry, dump
  translate), and in-place origin writes can only come from
  statement execution, which cannot interleave the
  lock-held boundary. The mid-statement WriteBatch spill
  never opens a window and keeps its statement-undo
  restoration (the translate's undo re-key exists for it);
  the commit dump never translates. Deterministic regression:
  TestPkMoveDumpOriginLedgerRestoredOnBoundaryRollback (no
  dirty-object wave: payload-update origin staged on a raw
  workspace insert, thresholds ungated so the boundary dump
  runs, the RC snapshot injection aborts the boundary after
  the translation ran; rollback restores the pre-translation
  ledger exactly — on r33 semantics the ledger stays keyed by
  the dead spill identity — the retried boundary re-spills
  and re-translates, and a later same-key probe resolves the
  durable origin; live: the payload-updated, dump-spilled
  row's key move cascades through both MERGE and PICK).
- D138 (r34, review F2, refines D129+D125): the dump path
  holds cleanup ownership of its persisted output from a
  successful Sync until the workspace registration takes it.
  Before r34, any failure inside that interval — the
  provenance shadow's post-Sync read-back storage error,
  FillBlockInfoBat, or writeFileLockedWithAutoIncrEpochKnown
  — exited with only CNS3Writer.Close scheduled, which
  releases memory and never deletes the persisted files;
  unregistered files entered neither the rollback tail-cut
  GC (no entry was appended), nor failedWaveOrphans
  (wave-only inventory), nor the durable orphan registry:
  persistent files without a cleanup owner.
  reclaimUnregisteredDumpLocked now owns every such exit:
  mirroring cleanFailedWave, a cancellation-independent
  DeleteUnpublishedObjects against the same filesystem the
  writer persisted through attempts immediate reclamation;
  when it cannot reconcile the whole inventory, the leftover
  names are retained in txn.failedWaveOrphans with a
  reserveDurableOrphanOwnership booking for exactly the
  retained count, so the transaction close's GC drain
  converts them name-for-name under D133/D135's exactly-once
  settlement — and when the registry itself refuses the
  booking, the names are still retained under the
  ownership-never-dies rule and the drain's anonymous
  clamped conversion logs and registers them. The healthy
  dump books nothing: reservation traffic appears only on
  the failure path, keeping D133's backpressure semantics out
  of the boundary's success shape. Deterministic regressions:
  TestPkMoveDumpRegistrationFailureReclaimsPersistedOutput
  (a gated read failure hits the shadow's post-Sync
  read-back: the immediate reclaim deletes the persisted
  object through the armed filesystem, the filesystem
  inventory is byte-identical to the pre-boundary state,
  failedWaveOrphans stays empty, and no reservation booked)
  and
  TestPkMoveDumpRegistrationFailureRetainsThenDrainsOrphans
  (the same read failure with the reclaim's delete itself

  and the file survives; healed, the close-drain conversion

- D139 (r35, review F1, refines D137+D110): dump-rollback
  restoration composes with completed in-window transfer
  rekeys instead of replacing them. D110's carry re-mints
  retained delete tombstones IN PLACE (the transfer resolves
  each pending tombstone's pre-transfer row id onto the
  storage generation the commit will publish and rewrites
  that batch cell through SetFixed) and re-keys the
  provenance bookkeeping onto the same identity in one shot.
  D137's restore replaced the whole ledger with the staged
  pre-translation snapshot — correct only while no other
  in-window transform had touched it. The r35 reviewer's
  sequence is the counterexample it could not survive:
  {W:O} dumps to {S:O}, the boundary's in-memory transfer
  leg then completes O -> N (the tombstone cell takes N and
  the carry produces {S:N}), and the object-transfer leg
  fails. RollbackLastStatement rewinds only the transfer
  timestamps and placeholders — the mutated batch cells and
  the carried ledger contributions are its retained state —
  yet D137's restore pitched the ledger back to {W:O}: the
  tombstone names its committed identity N, the ledger names
  the bygone O, and the retried transfer skips the
  already-minted N, so a later key move of that row anchors
  its old side to an identity the committed stream never
  shows departing and the apply replays DELETE/INSERT. The
  window now JOURNALS the dump waves' translation maps (one
  appended per shadow swap) instead of snapshotting the
  ledger header, and RollbackLastStatement — at the same
  window-death point, ahead of any pending wave discard —
  applies the inverse translations in reverse wave order to
  the CURRENT ledger with the same fresh-map rebuild
  discipline the translate itself uses: the dump's key and
  value remaps unwind exactly (spill identity back to the
  raw identity that outlives the cut) while every other
  in-window contribution — the completed carry's value
  rekeys above all — survives untouched. No in-window
  transfer is the degenerate case: the inverse application
  then reproduces D137's snapshot restore byte-for-byte.
  r35 left the dirty-object wave composition to the pending
  discard's unchanged wholesale pre-carry restore — the r36
  review proved that composite pitch: a completed in-window
  transfer carry's {W:N} is restored back to {W:O} while the
  retained tombstone keeps N, re-opening this defect whenever
  a dirty-object wave shares the boundary window. D141 (r36)
  retires the staged snapshot and unwinds the wave's own
  journaled migration pairs against the current maps instead,
  preserving exactly the rekeys this entry guarantees. The
  mid-statement WriteBatch spill still opens no window,
  journals nothing, and keeps its statement-undo
  restoration; the commit dump still never translates.
  Deterministic regression:
  TestPkMoveDumpRollbackPreservesCompletedTransferRekeys
  (payload-update-shaped acknowledged region — tombstone O
  plus raw insert W with ledger {W:O}; thresholds ungated;
  latest-partition state seeded so the boundary's real
  in-memory leg re-mints the tombstone O -> N against
  genuinely persisted created objects; the new injection
  fj/cn/incr_stmt_rc_transfer_objects_fails aborts the
  object leg and rolls the boundary back; on r34 semantics
  the ledger returns {W:O} while the tombstone holds N —
  the restore instead yields {W:N} exactly, the retained
  tombstone batch stays byte-identical naming N, the dead
  spill drains, and the retried boundary re-dumps and
  adopts with the ledger resolving N under its re-minted
  identity; live: payload-update of rows 2,4 -> forced
  flush armed -> the pk move OF PAYLOAD ROW 2 (2->22)
  carries ledger {W22:W2p} and tombstone W2p (the payload
  insert's committed identity) into its closing boundary,
  which dumps {W22:W2p} -> {S22:W2p} and completes the
  in-memory leg W2p -> N before the one-shot object-leg
  injection aborts the transfer -> boundary rollback
  unwinds the failed window's dump wave against the
  carried ledger, restoring {W22:N} while the retained
  tombstone keeps N -> a healthy retry boundary re-dumps
  and adopts {S22':N} -> the same payload-updated rows'
  moves (2->22, 4->44) cascade through both MERGE and
  PICK keys(2,4) byte-identical to the native control
  (2 link rows per flavor).

- D140 (r35, review F2, refines D138+D133): bounded
  producer admission moves to the persistence choke point.
  D133's contract — reserve cleanup ownership BEFORE any
  file exists, release or convert on every terminal —
  exempted the boundary dump: D138 booked only after a
  failed reclaim and retained the names even when that
  booking was refused, so repeated post-Sync read failures
  compounded with delete failures grew retained inventory
  past hardCapacity across boundary retries and closes, and
  the close drain's anonymous conversion settled those
  unbooked registrations against whatever reservations
  other producers held. The boundary dump's CNS3 writer
  now installs the sinker's unpublished-name observer: it
  runs after the object name is reserved and before its
  first byte reaches storage — including the
  threshold-driven flushes inside Write that predate Sync —
  and a rejection aborts that sync with nothing persisted.
  The hook books reserveDurableOrphanOwnership(fs, 1) per
  object, so the admission count never needs estimation:
  the observer fires exactly once per object the writer
  will persist, generalizing the wave's pre-computed
  len(dirtyObject) bound to events at the same choke point
  multi_update already uses for its spill markers.
  Exhaustion fails the boundary BEFORE any byte exists —
  sustained reclamation failure backpressures the producing
  statement, repeated retries never grow retained state,
  and because every registering name arrives with its own
  booking, the close drain's conversion is always
  reconciled: no settlement can consume a peer producer's
  reservations. Every terminal reconciles exactly: the
  healthy dump releases each booking when its registration
  succeeds; the three D138 post-Sync exits keep their
  reclaim-then-retain semantics with the bookings already
  in place, releasing on a reconciled reclaim and carrying
  the bookings into failedWaveOrphans on retention; the
  writer-error exits (a Sync or mid-Write flush failure)
  reclaim the persisted-or-ambiguous output through the
  writer's own DeletePersisted snapshot on a
  cancellation-free context and release the bookings when
  it reconciles, retaining the snapshot's names with their
  bookings when it cannot. The healthy dump's admission
  cost is reservation arithmetic only — no I/O is added to
  the success shape. Deterministic regressions: the two
  r34 D138 tests keep their observable terminals with the
  booking moved earlier, plus
  TestPkMoveDumpAdmissionRefusesBeforePersistenceAtSaturation
  (the registry pinned to exhaustion with a peer producer's
  reservation held and a stuck retained name failing
  sustained deletes: the dump's first object is refused at
  the observer — the boundary fails with the D133
  exhaustion error, the filesystem is byte-identical
  because no file was written, and zero reclaim deletes
  ran; repeated retries fail identically before any
  persistence; the peer's reservation remains exact
  throughout; healed, the retry produces its output and the
  healthy terminal releases every booking) and
  TestPkMoveDumpRetentionConvertsOnlyItsOwnBookings
  (headroom exactly one beyond the peer's booking: the
  dump's object books the last slot, the sustained
  read-back failure plus sustained delete failures retain
  the unreclaimable object with its own booking in place — the
  registry's reserved total stays at peer-1 plus ours-1
  through repeated boundary retries and a transaction
  close, the close drain converts our name against our
  booking, the healed sweep settles the conversion exactly
  once, and the peer's reservation survives every terminal
  byte-exact until the peer itself releases it).

- D141 (r36, review F1, refines D123): rollback ownership
  of the compaction wave's provenance re-key moves from a
  wholesale staged-snapshot restore to an exact inverse
  application against the current maps, so the discard
  composes with D139 instead of overwriting it. D123 staged
  the pre-carry origins/heals/lineage headers into
  boundaryFinalization and had the discard replace the maps
  outright — total only while the wave's carry was the LAST
  in-window provenance transform. The r36 reviewer's
  composition violates exactly that: a payload-updated row
  dumps {W:O} -> {S:O} (D139 journal), the RC in-memory
  transfer leg completes O -> N (D110 carry, mutating the
  retained tombstone cell in place), the object leg fails,
  the D139 unwind correctly yields {W:N} — and the discard
  then pitches the ledger back to the staged {W:O} while the
  retained tombstone keeps N. The retried transfer skips the
  already-minted N, so a later key move of that row anchors
  its old side to an identity the committed stream never
  shows departing: the D139 defect re-opened by an unrelated
  dirty-object rewrite. The repair replaces capture with
  inversion. Every provenance carry — the wave's migration
  and the transfer's re-mint alike — runs through
  remapPkMoveLinkRowIDsLocked with dead=nil: an injective
  re-key whose fresh-map four-case rebuild retires nothing,
  so each is exactly invertible from its own pair list and no
  snapshot is ever needed. boundaryFinalization now JOURNALS
  the wave's migration pairs (old/new, already computed at
  wave publication) in place of the staged headers, and
  discardPendingBoundaryFinalizationLocked — still after the
  D139 dump unwind and before the statement-undo replay —
  applies the pairs' inverse to the CURRENT maps through the
  same fresh-map four-case rebuild (origin keys and values,
  null-heal targets, lineage origins), then restores the
  drained deletion ledger exactly as before (D124 untouched).
  Rollback therefore walks the window's provenance transforms
  in exact reverse order, omitting only the deliberately
  preserved one: the completed IN-MEMORY transfer carry
  survives (D110/D139) — its re-minted cells live in retained
  workspace tombstone batches that outlast the rollback; the
  object-route carry shares no such shelter (its identities
  live only in the sinker's output files, whose publications
  the tail cut removes and whose retirements the
  resurrection restores) and is wound by D142 (r37) — the
  dump swaps unwind against the preserved carry (D139), and
  the wave carry unwinds against that result (D141) —
  ending at the pre-window view carried through the
  completed in-memory transfer. When no transfer carry intervened the composite
  reproduces D123's snapshot restore byte-for-byte (the nib
  case: the wave contributed the only transform), so every
  r29-r34 wave terminal is preserved unchanged; with an
  intervening completed carry the result differs exactly on
  the carry's re-minted identities, which the retained
  tombstones still name — ledger and tombstone agree on N,
  the retried boundary re-runs the wave on byte-identical
  inputs, re-dumps, skips N and adopts, and a later move of
  that row anchors its old side to N. Invariants: (i) no
  rollback path ever snapshots or replaces provenance map
  headers again — the complete in-window re-key history is
  reconstructible from the rewind journals (dump swaps in
  maintWindow.dumpTranslations, the wave's pairs in the
  pending finalization, object-route transfer carries
  journaled in the window at carry time by D142, r37); (ii)
  one staged wave per boundary
  window keeps the wave journal single-shot (the existing
  single-slot contract, unchanged); (iii) the statement-undo
  replay's preconditions are unchanged — for a wave-only
  rollback the maps it sees are byte-identical to D123's
  restored snapshot. Deterministic regression (planned,
  executes with the implementation turn): extend the D139
  regression with an unrelated dirty-object rewrite
  co-windowing the payload-row dump — tombstone O plus raw
  insert W with ledger {W:O}, an unrelated object held dirty
  under the diverted-deletion ledger so
  compactDeletionOnObjsLocked publishes a wave whose carry
  re-mints A -> C BEFORE the dump translates W -> S; the
  in-memory leg completes O -> N and the
  fj/cn/incr_stmt_rc_transfer_objects_fails injection aborts
  the object leg. r35 semantics restore {W:O} against the
  N-naming tombstone (the RED discriminant); the design's
  rollback yields exactly {W:N} with the wave's re-minted
  rows restored to A, the retained tombstone byte-identical
  naming N, the retry re-running the wave on the restored
  ledger, re-dumping, skipping N and adopting, and a later
  move of that row anchoring to N. The live battery adds the
  same dirty-object shape to the r35 F1-cascade SQL and
  re-proves MERGE and PICK keys(2,4) cascades byte-identical
  to native; a complementary unit test round-trips composed
  forward carries through the inverse (value-only, key-only,
  both, chained across wave/dump/transfer phases), proving
  the inverse total.

- D142 (r37, review F1, refines D110+D113): retained
  in-memory rekeys and discarded object-result rekeys get
  different rollback owners, and the object-route carry gets
  one at last. D110 carries provenance through BOTH transfer
  legs' re-keys, but the legs shelter their identities
  differently: the IN-MEMORY leg rewrites retained workspace
  tombstone cells in place (transfer.go:519-537), and those
  batches outlast the boundary rollback naming the new
  identity — the transfer resolved it against real
  generations, so the retry skips it as already-minted; the
  OBJECT leg re-mints identities whose only residence is the
  sinker's output files (transferStaged,
  transfer_util.go:410-471), and a rolled boundary tail-cuts
  those publications while
  resurrectRetiredTransferEntriesLocked restores the retired
  originals (types.go:1897-1903; r26/D113) — the durable
  side returns to O. The object leg carries the maps and
  staged link cells O -> N BEFORE its fallible persistence
  (carry at transfer_util.go:463 ahead of Write :471 and
  Sync :310), the statement-undo ledgers that could
  compensate expire at the boundary establishment
  (types.go:1178-1181), and nothing rewound it: a Write/Sync
  failure leaves provenance naming N over a file that never
  published; a later table's failure leaves an earlier
  table's retirement resurrected over provenance still
  naming N (retireTransfers stamps txn.statementID at
  transfer.go:165, resurrected for statementSeq >=
  rolledStmt). The wound-up state then poisons the retry:
  the retried flow re-reads O and mints P (unequal to N
  whenever storage compacted between attempts), carries
  O -> P — which touches nothing, because every reference
  was already re-minted to N — and commits a tombstone P
  that no update link names (N), so the apply replays
  DELETE/INSERT. The r35/r36 planned injection at
  txn.go:3744 fires before the object leg begins and cannot
  expose either terminal. The repair extends D139/D141's
  journal discipline to the last unowned class: every
  object-route transfer round journals its re-key pairs (the
  pkMoveTransferRekeyPairs output, copied before
  orphanStaged recycles the pairing batches) into the
  maintenance window AT CARRY TIME — before the round's
  fallible Write — and RollbackLastStatement applies the
  window's rewind journals in strict reverse chronological
  order, object rounds first (they are the last transforms
  of the window), then dump swaps (D139), then the wave
  pairs (D141), preserving only the sheltered in-memory
  carry. The inverse rides the SAME engine that minted the
  forward transform:
  carryPkMoveProvenanceThroughRekeyLocked(new, old) replays
  the round backwards through remapPkMoveLinkRowIDsLocked's
  dead=nil four-case rebuild, so origin keys and values,
  null-heal targets, lineage origins, AND staged link cells
  invert with exactly the totality they were minted — no
  snapshot, no residual map. Failure before publication
  unwinds to the pre-attempt state exactly; rollback after
  an in-window retirement unwinds every journaled round
  whose region died while the resurrection returns the
  files, so provenance and tombstone agree on O again; the
  retry's O -> P carry then finds live references and
  re-mints to P, keeping the committed tombstone and its
  update link on one identity. Out-of-window transfers journal
  nothing UNDER R37: a commit failure dies with the transaction
  and its provenance (D113's seq discipline already owns those
  outcomes), and r37 claimed an out-of-window carry never meets
  a same-region rollback — r38 review F1 verified that half
  false for the AdvanceSnapshot route (types.go:1487-1509 runs
  transferTombstones with no maintenance window, reachable via
  CALL mo_cdc_target_identity inside an explicit pessimistic-RC
  transaction): D143 retracts it and gives that route the same
  journal owner on the statement clock. The byCommit half
  stands untouched.
  Invariants: (i) owner per re-key class — every in-window
  provenance re-key is either journaled-and-wound (wave,
  dump, object transfer) or preserved by shelter (the
  in-memory leg alone, whose shelter contract D110 and
  r28/D120 document; a future change letting retained
  tombstone cells lose their re-mints during rollback must
  reclassify it as journaled); (ii) rewinds apply strictly
  reverse-chronologically, object rounds appended per
  transferStaged round under the same txn.Lock the carry
  takes; (iii) the inverse uses the forward engine with
  swapped pair lists, keeping mint/undo discipline identical
  by construction; (iv) pair lists are copied into the
  journal before the round's staged batches return to the
  pool, so the rewind never reads recycled memory; r38 review
  F2 (D144) bounds what gets copied — effective pairs only,
  coalesced per statement — and charges it to the coordinator
  budget with admission before mutation.
  Deterministic regressions (planned, execute with the
  implementation turn): UT primary — a seeded partition's
  persisted tombstone OBJECT carries provenance (origin
  ledger value O, staged link old_row_id O); the real object
  flow runs with a deterministic post-carry write failure
  (new test-only fault point at the sinker write), the
  boundary rolls back, and every map plus the staged link
  cells must read exactly O again while the resurrection
  restores the file set; the retry — run once immediately
  and once after a compaction-shaped generation churn that
  forces P != N — carries O -> P with tombstone P and link
  P agreeing, and the multi-round shape (one table
  retired+published, a second table's write failing)
  exercises rollback-after-retirement. r36 semantics keep
  provenance at N across both — the RED discriminant. A
  complementary round-trip UT interleaves wave/dump/object
  journal entries with a sheltered in-memory carry and
  proves the composite rewind reproduces the pre-window
  maps carried through the in-memory leg for every entry
  shape. The live battery adds the same flushed-tombstone
  route with a post-rekey object failure, churn, and retry,
  re-proving MERGE and PICK keys(2,4) cascades
  byte-identical to the native control.
  r38 review (F1+F2) refines this entry by D143+D144: the journal
  leaves the maintenance window for a transaction-level,
  statement-tagged chronological ledger that owns carries on every
  rollback-reachable route (D143), and its retention becomes
  effective-only, coalesced per statement per identity,
  budget-charged, and admitted before mutation with loud refusal
  (D144). The sentences above that retain every round's full pair
  list (the pkMoveTransferRekeyPairs copy at carry time and
  invariant (iv)) and the maintenance-window-only storage are
  thereby bounded and re-homed; the engine contract, the shelter
  classification, both failure terminals, and the churned-retry
  repair argument stand unchanged.

- D143 (r38, review F1, refines D142): the rollback owner for
  carried provenance leaves the maintenance window for a
  transaction-level, statement-tagged chronological carry journal,
  because the window scope has a reachable hole. AdvanceSnapshot
  (types.go:1487-1509) runs advanceSnapshot plus
  transferTombstones WITHOUT opening a maintenance window, and it
  is publicly reachable inside an explicit pessimistic-RC
  transaction through CALL mo_cdc_target_identity: the guard
  demands OPTION_BEGIN, an active operator, and pessimistic RC
  (pkg/frontend/cdc_target_guard.go:129's AdvanceSnapshot call
  behind the transaction-shape check at :143-153). Window or no
  window, the object leg carries provenance O -> N at
  transfer_util.go:463 ahead of the fallible Write :471 and Sync
  :310, and retirements stamp txn.statementID (transfer.go:165 ->
  pk_move_link_fixup.go:3136-3163). When such a write fails inside
  an explicit transaction, the ordinary-error path
  (pkg/frontend/txn.go:1157-1174, Case2) rolls back the STATEMENT
  and preserves the transaction: the positional tail cut removes
  the replacement publications and
  resurrectRetiredTransferEntriesLocked(rolledStmt) returns the
  retired originals (types.go:1831-1845, 1903; statementSeq >=
  rolledStmt at pk_move_link_fixup.go:3304-3360) — the durable
  side reads O again while D142, its journal scoped to a window
  that never opened, rewinds nothing. Provenance N over tombstone
  O reproduces the churned-retry poison of the r37 review: the
  retry re-reads O, mints P after a compaction-shaped churn,
  carries O -> P over every-reference-already-N, commits tombstone
  P while the update link names N, and the data-branch apply
  replays DELETE/INSERT. Every clause verified VALID at the cited
  loci on the md5-pinned era-29 tree (logs /tmp/e32_vf1a.log
  through /tmp/e32_vf1c.log).

  The repair keeps D142's engine, order, and totality and changes
  the journal's scope and clock. (1) One chronological journal per
  transaction records every carried re-key class — the wave pairs
  (D141), the dump swaps (D139), and the object-route rounds
  (D142) — appended at carry time under txn.Lock on EVERY
  rollback-reachable route: boundary windows and AdvanceSnapshot
  alike. D139's implemented window field and D141's
  pending-finalization journal fold in as kind-tagged entries of
  the one ledger (the whole stack ships in this PR, so the fold
  moves no released interface); dump-swap and wave entries exist
  only inside windows, object entries exist on either route, and
  the in-memory transfer leg journals nothing anywhere — preserved
  by shelter exactly as D142 classified. (2) Every entry stamps
  the txn.statementID of the statement whose carry it records —
  the same clock the retirement ledger stamps at transfer.go:165
  and the resurrection replays at types.go:1903 (D113) — so one
  statement-seq discipline owns publications, retirements, and
  provenance carries alike. (3) byCommit transfers still journal
  nothing: a commit failure aborts the transaction wholesale
  (frontend Case1/rollbackUnsafe), there is no statement-level
  rollback to own its carries, and the journal dies with the
  transaction.

  RollbackLastStatement(rolledStmt) unwinds journal entries with
  seq >= rolledStmt in strict reverse chronological order through
  the forward engine with swapped pair lists
  (remapPkMoveLinkRowIDsLocked, dead=nil, total and exactly
  invertible per D142's argument). Placement: immediately after
  the positional tail cut, in the splice region the r34-r37 window
  unwinds already occupy, and BEFORE rollbackPkMoveStmtStateLocked
  — the undo records a statement wrote before its carry name
  pre-carry identities, so the carry inverse must restore the
  state those records describe before they replay (in-window
  ledgers are already cleared at types.go:1178-1181, so the
  wave/discard composition inherits D139/D141's reviewed ordering
  unchanged; the pending finalization then drops its own inverse
  application — the walker already ran it — and discards only the
  staged finalization state). Resurrection keeps its current place
  after the undo replay; it owns files, the journal owns maps and
  link cells, and the two never touch the same state. Release is
  explicit at three points: (a) boundary adoption — entries
  stamped by the adopted, now-irrevocable statement are dropped
  (adoption drops them because the widened cut
  — types.go:1280-1292 — guarantees no later rollback's cut end
  can reach their identities; r39 review F1 (D145) proved the
  seq-uniqueness premise false — types.go:1206-1208 increments
  statementID BEFORE maintenance, so the ensuing statement rolls
  back with rolledStmt EQUAL to the adopted stamps — and aligns
  the retirement ledger with the same adoption settlement);
  (b) statement rollback — each selected entry is
  removed as it unwinds; (c) transaction close
  or rollback — the ledger dies with the transaction.

  Invariants: (i) every rollback-reachable provenance re-key is
  either journaled under its carrying statement's seq or preserved
  by shelter — the in-memory leg alone (D110 + r28/D120 contract;
  a future change letting retained tombstone cells lose their
  re-mints during rollback must reclassify it as journaled); (ii)
  rewinds apply strictly reverse-chronologically by append order
  within and across seqs, one walker for all kinds, never partial
  within a round; (iii) the inverse uses the forward engine with
  swapped pair lists, keeping mint/undo discipline identical by
  construction; (iv) provenance journals and the retirement ledger
  stamp the same statement clock — any future rollback-reachable
  transfer route must journal under it or hold a recorded
  exemption as strong as byCommit's transaction-wide death; (v)
  admission asserts pair-list integrity (equal lengths, old side
  injective) before any mutation, failing the enclosing statement
  loudly rather than risking a mis-unwind.

  Deterministic regressions (planned, execute with the
  implementation turn) EXTEND D142's ladder with the
  maintWindow=nil battery this review required, all asserting
  agreement among restored files, the three maps, staged link
  cells, and MERGE/PICK cascade results: (a) post-carry failure —
  an explicit pessimistic-RC transaction advances its snapshot
  through the workspace AdvanceSnapshot path; a seeded partition's
  persisted tombstone OBJECT round carries provenance (origin
  ledger value O, staged link old_row_id O); a deterministic
  post-carry object-write failure (the same test-only sinker fault
  point D142 plans, fired on the no-window route) fails the
  statement; RollbackLastStatement must restore exactly O
  everywhere while the resurrection returns the file set; (b)
  earlier-table retirement followed by later-table failure outside
  any window — t1 completes publication plus retirement under
  AdvanceSnapshot, t2's round fails; both tables' journaled
  carries unwind while t1's resurrection returns its originals;
  (c) statement rollback after a SUCCESSFUL AdvanceSnapshot
  transfer unwinds nothing it should not — entries stamped by
  earlier, retained statements survive byte-exact and only the
  rolled statement's own entries unwind; (d) the churned retry on
  the no-window route (P != N after generation churn) carries O ->
  P with tombstone P and link P agreeing; the live battery re-runs
  the f1cascade fixture through a CDC-style AdvanceSnapshot
  between move and commit and re-proves MERGE and PICK keys(2,4)
  cascades byte-identical to the native control. r37 semantics
  keep provenance at N in (a), (b), and (d) — the RED
  discriminant.

- D144 (r38, review F2, refines D142): journal retention becomes
  effective-only, coalesced, budget-charged, and admitted before
  mutation. r37 retains every round's full
  pkMoveTransferRekeyPairs output until window completion; that
  function returns pairs for EVERY tombstone whose rowid changed
  in the batch with no provenance filter
  (pk_move_link_fixup.go:3043-3069), and the carry gate is
  transaction-wide (transfer_util.go:458-464:
  holdsPkMoveProvenanceLocked) — so a transaction holding one row
  of provenance for table A journals table B's entire spilled
  DELETE workload round after round, 2 x RowidSize(24) = 48 bytes
  plus slice overhead per pair, aggregated across rounds past the
  8 MiB per-batch staging limit (transferBatchSizeLimit,
  transfer_util.go:44-46) with no bound, while the coordinator
  measure that already budgets lineage stacks, statement ledgers,
  origins, heals, and retirements (pkMoveBookkeepBytesLocked,
  pk_move_link_fixup.go:109-140) never sees these copies. A pair
  whose OLD identity references no provenance artifact is a
  definitional no-op in remapPkMoveLinkRowIDsLocked — nothing
  re-keys — so retaining it is pure growth with zero undo value.
  Verified VALID at every cited locus (logs /tmp/e32_vf2a.log
  through /tmp/e32_vf2c.log).

  The repair has four parts. (1) EFFECTIVE-ONLY FILTER: a shared
  helper computes the round's provenance reference set — the keys
  and values of pkMoveRowidOrigins, the null-heal rowids, the
  lineage origins, and the old identities present as staged link
  old_row_id cells — and the journal retains exactly the carried
  pairs whose old id is in that set; the same helper backs both
  the journal admission and the mutation's cost accounting, so the
  filter cannot drift from the engine's actual effect (the
  mutation itself still receives the full pair list — a no-op pair
  is one map probe, and the engine's contract is unchanged; only
  retention filters). (2) PER-STATEMENT COALESCING: within one
  statement's segment, an identity re-keyed by several rounds
  (chained mints O -> N then N -> M) keeps ONE composed entry,
  earliest old to latest new; the composed inverse lands exactly
  where the stepwise inverse would, because intermediate
  identities are minted and re-minted inside the segment with no
  observer between rounds (txn.Lock is held) — retention per
  statement becomes O(distinct provenance-referenced identities it
  re-keyed), independent of round count and of unrelated
  transferred DELETE volume. — composition SUPERSEDED by r43 review F2 (D150):
  the composed inverse is exact only when every round completes;
  a partial mid-carry failure splits current cells across
  both identities, and the in-place tip overwrite keeps the
  earlier statement's seq, so per-round undo preservation is
  mandatory. (3) BUDGET CHARGE AND
  ADMISSION-BEFORE-MUTATION: coalesced journal bytes (2 x
  RowidSize + map overhead per entry) charge into the existing
  coordinator umbrella (pkMoveLinkCoordinatorBudget against staged
  + bookkeep + pin bytes) in the style and with the error
  convention of checkPkMoveBookkeepBudgetLocked
  (pk_move_link_fixup.go:143-175); every carry computes its
  effective pairs, estimates its segment's post-merge charge, and
  checks BEFORE mutating any map, staged cell, or lineage stack —
  r39 review F2 (D146) widens that charge to the COMPLETE retained
  growth: the staged-link area appends the carry's SetBytesAt
  rewrites mint (24-byte rowids never inline, vector.go:4235-4253
  and :12150-12178) plus one inverse generation held as rollback
  reserve — overflow refuses loudly and statement-atomically, the
  transfer fails before half-carrying, and the statement rolls
  back clean;
  a zero budget disables the check (existing convention). (4)
  EXACT RELEASE: D143's three release points apply, and because
  the measure is computed on demand from the live journal in
  pkMoveBookkeepBytesLocked's style, the charge shrinks
  automatically at adoption, rollback, and close with no release
  bookkeeping of its own.

  Invariants: (i) journaled iff mutated — a round's journal equals
  the set of pairs the engine actually moved for provenance, by
  construction of the shared filter; (ii) retention bound —
  journal bytes stay O(provenance-visible identities re-keyed by
  unclosed statements) x (2 x RowidSize + overhead), itself inside
  the coordinator budget (composition bound superseded by
  D150's per-round retention bound); (iii) admission completes before
  mutation — refusal leaves zero residue on any map, staged cell,
  or lineage stack; (iv) refusal is loud and statement-atomic — a
  saturated budget fails the statement rather than silently
  skipping pairs, because a silent skip would break D143's
  total-inverse premise.

  Deterministic regressions (planned, execute with the
  implementation turn): the lowered-budget multi-round case this
  review required — a deterministically lowered coordinator
  budget; small provenance on table A; unrelated table B's
  transferred deletes sized so r37's full-pair retention would
  cross the budget across rounds. Assert (a) under D144, B's
  rounds — every pair unreferenced — journal ZERO bytes and never
  trip the check (the tiny-provenance plus huge-unrelated-workload
  repro resolves); (b) a provenance-heavy A workload that
  genuinely crosses the lowered budget refuses BEFORE mutation:
  all three maps, staged link cells, and the ledger byte-identical
  to their pre-attempt state, the loud error surfaced, the
  statement rolled back atomically, and a retry under a raised
  budget completes; (c) chaining — superseded by D150's stepwise battery
  — coalescing — N chained rounds re-keying M
  identities retain M entries, and the composed rewind reproduces
  the stepwise-rewound state byte-for-byte; (d) release — boundary
  adoption and statement rollback each return the measured charge
  to its pre-round baseline; (e) r37 semantics retain every pair
  with no charge and no refusal — the RED discriminant (retention
  growth visible directly in the measure).

- D145 (r39, review F1, refines D143+D113): adoption becomes a
  recorded eligibility transition applied uniformly to both
  roll-forward ledgers, because the seq arithmetic r38 assumed
  does not exist. IncrStatementID appends the offsets entry and
  increments statementID BEFORE maintenance (types.go:1206-1208),
  runs the window's transforms under the NEW seq, and adopts by
  widening that offsets entry (types.go:1280-1292:
  applyPendingBoundaryFinalizationLocked +
  adoptMaintenanceWindowLocked, then offsets[established] =
  len(txn.writes)) with NO further increment — so the window's
  retirements (stamped txn.statementID,
  pk_move_link_fixup.go:3156) and the ENTIRE ensuing statement
  share one numeric seq. Its ordinary error rolls back with
  rolledStmt EQUAL to those stamps (types.go:1826 region:
  rolledStmt := txn.statementID captured before the decrement);
  the positional cut end — offsets[statementID after decrement] —
  retains everything the adoption widened in, including the
  adopted window's replacement tombstone N; and the resurrection
  selects purely by statementSeq >= rolledStmt
  (pk_move_link_fixup.go:3304-3309), re-appending originals O
  beside the surviving adopted N — the exact duplicate-tombstone
  failure D113's ledger exists to prevent. Verified end to end on
  the era-29 tree (logs /tmp/e33_vf1a.log, /tmp/e33_vf1b.log).
  D143's r38 premise that seqs never revisit a completed statement
  (r38 design:4394-4398) is false; its drop-at-adoption rule
  stands only because the widened cut — not seq uniqueness — makes
  adopted identities un-cuttable, and the retirement ledger must
  get the SAME settlement.

  The repair sets one rule for both ledgers. (1) SETTLEMENT AT
  ADOPTION: when the boundary's adoption widens the cut via
  offsets[established] = len(txn.writes), every ACTIVE record
  whose statementSeq is at most the boundary's seq settles —
  retirement records become the settled PREFIX of the ONE
  collection they already live in (txn.retiredTransfers; the
  adoption walk advances a recorded boundary inside it — r40
  review F1 (D147): a separate audit list would disconnect
  adopted retirements from the close drain
  gcRetiredTransferFiles, pk_move_link_fixup.go:3363-3410,
  which enumerates ONLY that collection, leaking files and
  D133 reservations on every close outcome), and the D143
  carry journal drops the same
  rounds' entries in the same walk. Settlement is justified by the
  widening itself: the cut end of EVERY later rollback is an
  offsets entry at or above the adopted region's end, so
  identities and replacements the adoption retained can never die
  in a later tail cut — unwinding or resurrecting them would
  corrupt live state with exactly the duplicate D113 prohibits.
  (2) FRESH SAME-SEQ WORK STAYS ACTIVE: retirements and carries
  minted AFTER adoption by the ensuing statement under the SAME
  numeric seq (its AdvanceSnapshot/transfer rounds) enter the
  active structures normally, because their replacements append
  above the widened entry and die in that statement's tail cut;
  seq >= rolledStmt selects exactly them. Eligibility is ledger
  MEMBERSHIP at rollback time, never numeric seq alone — two
  records sharing one seq are distinguished by which side of the
  adoption event they stand. (3) NO SEQ ARITHMETIC CHANGES:
  stamps, the >= test, and the positional cuts keep their r26-r38
  semantics; the only new mechanics are the settlement walk at
  adoption and the active-set discipline in resurrection and
  unwind. (4) PRE-EXISTING HOLE OWNED: the mismatch exists in the
  era-29 tree independent of D143 (a window-stamped retirement
  meets a same-seq ensuing-statement rollback today); the
  implementation turn fixes it in retire and resurrect per this
  entry, and the D143 journal and the retirement ledger settle in
  ONE adoption walk.

  Invariants: (i) one adoption event settles exactly one round's
  records from BOTH ledgers — no record class may outlive adoption
  while its sibling class drops; (ii) resurrection and carry
  unwind read ONLY the active tail beyond the settled prefix
  defined by D147 — passing over settled prefix records is
  normal, because they stay in the drained collection; a
  settled record found INSIDE the active tail, or an ordering
  inversion across the settled boundary, fails loudly, never
  silently skips;
  (iii) settlement is irrevocable and idempotent — a settled
  record never re-activates, and double settlement reports a bug;
  (iv) the settled/active boundary is the adoption EVENT, not the
  seq value — any future code stamping records enters the active
  set and settles by the same walk; (v) settlement changes no
  stamp, no >= test, no cut arithmetic — it is a membership
  transition only.

  Deterministic regressions (planned, execute with the
  implementation turn), covering the shapes this review required:
  (a) ADOPT-THEN-SAME-STATEMENT-ERROR — a window object transfer
  completes with retirement, the boundary adopts, and the ENSUING
  statement (same numeric seq) hits an ordinary error: after the
  rollback, EXACTLY ONE parent tombstone survives (the adopted N),
  no resurrected O appears beside it, provenance and staged link
  cells name N, the retirement record is settled, and the
  statement's retry re-runs cleanly; (b) SAME-SEQ FRESH CARRY
  FAILURE — the ensuing statement performs an AdvanceSnapshot
  transfer (no window) whose post-carry write fails: its fresh
  carry and fresh retirement DO unwind and resurrect (active, seq
  == rolledStmt) while the adopted window's records stay settled
  and the adopted N untouched — one surviving identity per row;
  (c) composition — (a), then (b), then a churned retry minting P:
  tombstone P and update link P agree, and MERGE and PICK
  keys(2,4) cascades stay byte-identical to the native control at
  the live level; (d) settlement totality — after adoption the
  ACTIVE resurrection ledger holds no record with seq <= the
  adopted seq, and a deliberately re-inserted settled record trips
  the loud selection assertion; (e) the adoption-then-close
  drain batteries across commit, rollback, and unknown-result
  close are owned by D147 on a real file service. RED
  discriminants: era-29/r38 semantics resurrect the adopted O
  beside N in (a) — the duplicate tombstone, observed directly
  in the workspace — and fail (b)'s active/settled separation.

- D146 (r39, review F2, refines D144): admission charges the
  COMPLETE retained growth of the carry plus its potential
  inverse, because the staged mutation is not free. The carry
  rewrites staged link old_row_id AND new_row_id cells through
  pkMoveVecSetBytesAt -> vector.SetBytesAt
  (pk_move_link_fixup.go:3690-3724 — both columns, every matched
  24-byte cell, already riding the workspace reaccount helpers); a
  24-byte Rowid payload can never inline (VarlenaInlineSize = 23,
  types/bytes.go:26), so BuildVarlenaFromByteSlice dispatches it
  to buildVarlenaNoInline (vector.go:12245-12254), which APPENDS
  the payload to the vector area (vector.go:12150-12178) without
  reclaiming the displaced range until batch recycle —
  SetBytesAt's own comment states it 'appends a fresh area range
  before replacing the descriptor' (vector.go:4235-4253). The
  inverse rewrite performs a SECOND generation of the same
  appends. r38's admission (design:4491-4498) preflights only the
  journal's post-coalescing charge: a budget that fits existing
  staged + bookkeep + pin plus the journal estimate but not the
  ensuing area growth ADMITS the carry, which then grows the
  measured staged bytes past the budget with no refusal. Verified
  clause by clause (logs /tmp/e33_vf2a.log through
  /tmp/e33_vf2c.log).

  The repair: (1) COMPLETE CHARGE — admission computes G = J (the
  D144 journal post-coalescing charge) + A (staged-area append
  bytes for every cell the effective pair set will rewrite in BOTH
  row-id columns, at 24 bytes per cell under the CURRENT vector
  API's append behavior) + R (one full inverse generation of A,
  held as rollback reserve), all derived from the SAME effective
  set and the SAME reference-set helper, BEFORE any mutation;
  refusal when footprint + G crosses the budget, byte-identical
  pre-attempt state, loud statement-atomic error exactly as D144
  specified. (2) PRE-AUTHORIZED INVERSE — the inverse never
  re-admits: its bytes were reserved by R at forward admission, so
  a rollback under a saturated budget still unwinds completely
  (mirroring the resurrection walk's own never-fail discipline); R
  discharges when the entry settles at adoption or is consumed by
  the unwind. (3) BOUNDED SAME-LENGTH OVERWRITE — r40 review
  F2 (D148) makes the storage-neutral mechanics MANDATORY for
  replacing an EXISTING measured 24-byte link cell: both
  payloads are types.RowidSize varlenas that can never inline,
  so a local pk_move_link_fixup.go helper materializes
  ownership transactionally (MaterializeOwned,
  buffer_lease.go:274-291), takes the mutable area-backed
  window from GetBytesAt (vector.go:3800-3806), and copies
  the replacement over it in place — no append, no displaced
  range, measured delta ZERO forward and inverse — every
  precondition violation loud, no appending fallback. The
  APPEND mechanics r39 permitted is REJECTED for retained-
  cell replacement: the reaccount records but never reclaims
  and Vector.Size includes len(v.area) (vector.go:543-552),
  so append made the (b) baseline restoration unpassable;
  initial writes into vectors under construction keep
  SetBytesAt, and vector.go stays untouched (out of scope).
  (4) RELEASE — J discharges per D144's
  points, A discharges on batch recycle/reaccount via the
  on-demand measure, R per (2).

  Invariants: (i) charge completeness — the admitted charge covers
  every retained byte the forward carry or its inverse can add to
  ANY measured class (journal, staged area, reaccounted batch
  sizes); no class is admitted by estimate and grown in fact; (ii)
  refusal precedes mutation — the pre-attempt state is
  byte-identical when the loud error surfaces; (iii) the inverse
  is pre-authorized at forward admission and never re-admits — an
  unwind cannot trip the budget mid-rollback; (iv) the growth
  measure is derived on demand from live vectors and batches, so
  recycling and settlement shrink the charge with no release
  ledger of its own; (v) the measured post-carry staged bytes
  never exceed the admitted charge — under D148's mandated
  overwrite the retained-cell delta is exactly zero and the
  admitted growth reduces to J — enforced by the growth-
  equality UT, not by convention.

  Deterministic regressions (planned, execute with the
  implementation turn), including the case this review required:
  (a) JOURNAL-OVERFLOW REFUSAL — a deterministically lowered
  budget sized to fit the existing footprint but NOT the
  journal charge J itself (D148 collapses A and R to measured
  zero, so the complete charge IS the journal charge); the
  carry must refuse BEFORE mutation: all three maps, staged link cells and batch sizes, and
  the ledger byte-identical to pre-attempt, the loud error
  surfaced, the statement rolled back atomically, and a retry
  under a complete-sized budget completes; (b) ROLLBACK UNDER
  SATURATION — the pre-authorized inverse keeps its never-fail
  discipline (its reserve measures zero once D148 makes the
  overwrite byte-neutral), with the post-carry failure forced
  after admission (the r38-planned sinker fault point):
  the inverse unwinds fully under the saturated budget with no
  refusal, and the measure returns to the pre-round baseline; (c)
  GROWTH EQUALITY — the measured staged-area delta after a
  round (forward, and forward-plus-inverse) is exactly ZERO on
  retained link cells under D148's mandated overwrite, never
  exceeding the admitted charge; (d) the r38 F2 composition
  re-run (tiny provenance on
  table A, huge unrelated transferred deletes on table B): B's
  unreferenced rounds still journal zero AND rewrite zero cells —
  admission charges nothing for them; (e) REPEATED-ATTEMPT
  FOOTPRINT — the regression r40 review F2 required: one
  retained object link batch suffers k forced post-carry
  failures and retries; after EACH inverse the measured
  footprint returns to the pre-round baseline byte-for-byte,
  headroom never tightens across attempts, and the final
  retry completes under the UNCHANGED budget with cells
  naming the final identities; (f) RED — r38's journal-only
  admission passes the same lowered budget and the carry
  then pushes the measured staged bytes past it with no
  refusal, observed directly in the measure; r39's append-
  permitted mechanics makes (b) and (e) unpassable; the
  measure cannot return to baseline.

- D147 (r40, review F1, refines D145): settlement must never move
  a record OUT of the collection the close drain owns. r39 kept
  settled retirements 'in a settled audit list for assertion'; the
  reviewer proved that list has no cleanup terminal:
  gcRetiredTransferFiles (pk_move_link_fixup.go:3363-3410, full
  body log /tmp/e34_hyg_vf1a.log) returns immediately when
  txn.retiredTransfers is empty, gathers file names ONLY from that
  collection's records, then nils the collection and drains — the
  main path registerDurableOrphanGC + retryDurableOrphanGC
  transfers ownership to the durable orphan registry BEFORE the
  fallible reclamation and releases D133 reservations only on
  confirmed deletion, with the CCPR and clone branches releasing
  reservations by count — because retired files are unpublished
  garbage in EVERY close outcome: committed, rolled back, or
  unknown-result alike. A record sitting outside that collection
  leaks its unpublished files, and its outstanding reservation
  outlives the transaction against the shared hard ceiling.

  The repair: settled records stay INSIDE txn.retiredTransfers as
  a SETTLED PREFIX whose boundary the adoption walk advances.
  Retirements deposit in append order and one boundary settles at
  most one round, so the settled records sit consecutively at the
  head; the adoption walk asserts that totality loudly and records
  the boundary position — never a seq watermark, because a
  rolled-back statement's seq is re-issued to its retry under
  D145's fresh-work discipline and a value-based mark would settle
  newborn records at birth. Resurrection walks ONLY the active
  tail beyond the boundary, keeping stamps, the statementSeq >=
  rolledStmt test, and its name-for-name reservation settlement;
  the settled prefix is skipped by CONSTRUCTION — this corrects
  r39 invariant (ii): passing over settled prefix records is
  normal; a settled record found INSIDE the active tail, or any
  ordering inversion across the boundary, reports a bug.
  gcRetiredTransferFiles is UNCHANGED: it enumerates the WHOLE
  collection — settled prefix plus active tail — on every close
  outcome, so files and reservations drain through the existing
  protocol exactly once; registry ownership precedes reclamation,
  so a deletion failure retains ownership and a later piggyback
  retry completes deletion and release. Settlement creates no
  second owner, no second drain, no skipped name.

  Invariants: (i) settlement changes eligibility ONLY — cleanup
  ownership, drain membership, and reservation settlement are
  invariant across the active/settled transition; (ii)
  EXACTLY-ONCE across outcomes — commit, rollback, and
  unknown-result close each enumerate every record's files and
  reservations exactly once; (iii) boundary totality — after
  adoption every settled record precedes the recorded boundary and
  every active record follows it, asserted loudly by the walk;
  (iv) no drain fork — one code path over one collection, no
  audit-list-only records; (v) D145 semantics preserved verbatim
  on the active tail — no stamp, >= test, or cut arithmetic
  changes.

  Deterministic regressions (planned, execute with the
  implementation turn) on a REAL file service so deletion and
  reservation settlement are observable: (a) ADOPTION-THEN-COMMIT
  — window transfer retires and adopts, commit closes: the drain
  enumerates the settled record exactly once, its files reach the
  durable orphan registry, reservations release only on confirmed
  deletion; (b) ADOPTION-THEN-ROLLBACK — same drain shape (retired
  files are unpublished garbage in every close outcome), no
  resurrection of the settled prefix during the rollbacks, no
  double-release; (c) ADOPTION-THEN-UNKNOWN-RESULT — an unresolved
  commit outcome drains identically; (d) DELETION FAILURE AND
  RECOVERY — inject a deletion failure: registry ownership
  persists, the reservation stays outstanding, a later piggyback
  sweep confirms deletion and releases, converging to the
  file-free fully-released terminal; (e) r39-audit-list RED —
  under the reviewed audit-list shape the settled record never
  reaches the drain, observed as surviving files plus outstanding
  reservations after close. The D145 batteries (a)-(d) stand, with
  (a)'s assertion 'the retirement record is settled' now meaning
  prefix membership.

- D148 (r40, review F2, refines D146): rollback reclamation is
  CHOSEN — the retained-cell rewrite is a bounded SAME-LENGTH
  IN-PLACE OVERWRITE; the append mechanics r39 permitted is
  REJECTED, because it made D146's own baseline-restoration
  acceptance unpassable. The carry's staged loop
  (pk_move_link_fixup.go:3690-3724, helper alias
  pkMoveVecSetBytesAt = vector.SetBytesAt at :215) replaces
  EXISTING 24-byte cells in ALREADY-MEASURED retained link
  batches: SetBytesAt appends a fresh area range without
  reclaiming the displaced range (vector.go:4235-4253),
  Vector.Size includes len(v.area) (vector.go:543-552), and the
  unaccount/account reaccount records the growth without
  reclaiming it (logs /tmp/e34_vf2a.log, /tmp/e34_vf2b.log,
  /tmp/e34_vf2c.log) — a round trip leaves 48 measured bytes per
  cell, so repeated failed attempts consume the coordinator budget
  even though the logical row IDs restore.

  The mechanics: a LOCAL helper in pk_move_link_fixup.go —
  vector.go stays untouched (out of scope) — overwrites in place.
  Preconditions, all loud on violation: cell non-null, vector
  non-const, BOTH displaced and replacement payloads exactly
  types.RowidSize (24 > VarlenaInlineSize 23, so the displaced
  payload is always area-backed). Steps: MaterializeOwned
  (buffer_lease.go:274-291) performs transactional copy-on-write —
  allocation failure leaves the vector unchanged and readable;
  GetBytesAt (vector.go:3800-3806) returns the mutable window
  bs[i].GetByteSlice(v.area); copy the replacement bytes over the
  window. Result: len(v.area), the descriptor, and the batch's
  measured size are ALL unchanged — forward and inverse alike — so
  the inverse restores the row ID AND the footprint and D146's
  baseline assertion holds by construction. There is NO appending
  fallback on this path: a precondition that cannot hold fails the
  statement loudly, because an appending fallback would mint
  uncharged retained growth.

  Scope and accounting: (1) the helper governs replacement of
  EXISTING MEASURED cells — the carry loop and every identity
  rewrite of a retained batch; the implementation turn audits the
  other pkMoveVecSetBytesAt call sites (pk_move_link_fixup.go:332,
  :960, :1346, :2312) and switches exactly those that replace
  measured cells, while initial writes into vectors under
  construction keep the appending API whose growth IS the batch's
  measured construction; (2) D146's charge reduces — A and R are
  MEASURED DELTAS, both zero under the overwrite, so G = J:
  journal admission IS the complete admission, the D144/D146
  preflight shape (compute from the effective set, refuse before
  mutation, statement-atomic loud failure) is preserved, and the
  inverse's pre-authorization degenerates to the never-fail
  discipline with a zero reserve; (3) the unaccount/account
  reaccount pair stays around the loop so mid-loop bookkeeping
  stays legal, but observes zero net delta across a round; (4)
  append remains rejected for retained-cell replacement even under
  budget headroom — the invariant is measured-delta-zero, not
  'growth fits'.

  Invariants: (i) measured-delta-zero — a forward carry and its
  inverse each leave len(v.area) and every descriptor of a
  retained link batch untouched; only cell PAYLOAD bytes change;
  (ii) precondition totality — length, null, const, and ownership
  checks are exhaustive and loud, no silent append fallback; (iii)
  charge adequacy — admission charges G = J + A + R with A = R = 0
  measured by the same helper from the same effective set BEFORE
  mutation; (iv) baseline restoration — a round trip returns the
  batch's measured footprint to pre-round bytes exactly, meeting
  D146's acceptance; (v) construction semantics preserved —
  initial writes into growing vectors keep SetBytesAt and their
  growth is measured at staging.

  Deterministic regressions (planned, execute with the
  implementation turn), including the regression this review
  required: (a) REPEATED-ATTEMPT FOOTPRINT — one retained object
  link batch suffers k forced post-carry failures and retries
  through the sinker fault point: after EACH inverse the measured
  footprint returns to the pre-round baseline byte-for-byte across
  all k attempts, the effective headroom never tightens, and the
  final retry completes under the UNCHANGED budget with the
  batch's cells naming the final identities; (b) GROWTH EQUALITY
  (ZERO) — forward alone and forward-plus-inverse measure exactly
  zero staged-area delta on retained cells; (c) PRECONDITION GUARD
  — a wrong payload length or const vector surfaces a loud
  internal error with no mutation and no appending fallback; (d)
  the D146 battery stands with its A = R = 0 alignment; (e) RED —
  r39's permitted append mechanics leaves 48 bytes per cell per
  round trip and fails (a) on the second attempt, observed
  directly in the measure.

- D149 (r41, review F1, refines §7's upgrade placement): the
  link-table catalog migration moves to a FORWARD tenant-upgrade
  version NEWER than the target branch's final registered version,
  because upgrade selection is strictly greater-than. The reviewed
  placement (r40 design:625) put table creation in v4.0.15; the
  resolved target origin/main
  6cbe375b49696021d72778baa292a66287f080bd — of which this
  worktree's base 8795f3699b40504376343fa1acda8b4619f0c76e is a
  verified ANCESTOR (/tmp/e35_vf1b.log) — registers v4_0_15,
  v4_0_16, v4_0_17 as its final handlers
  (pkg/bootstrap/upgrade.go:81-83 at the target; the base
  registers only through v4_0_14, /tmp/e35_vf1a.log); the target's
  v4_0_15 tenant list creates the database-default metadata table
  (catalog.MODatabaseDefaults) and a whole-tree git grep finds NO
  mo_data_branch_update_link definition (/tmp/e35_vf1b.log); and
  selection executes a handler only when versions.Compare(handler,
  tenant) > 0 chains through the ordered handle list
  (service_upgrade.go:277-281; service_upgrade_tenant.go:123-126 —
  identical on base and target, /tmp/e35_vf1c.log). So on the true
  target a tenant already at 4.0.17 never executes a newly added
  4.0.15 handler — provenance recording stays disabled — and the
  era-29 untracked pkg/bootstrap/versions/v4_0_15 package would
  collide with the target's existing package path byte-for-name.
  Every clause verified VALID at the cited loci (/tmp/e35_vf1a.log
  through /tmp/e35_vf1d.log).

  The repair: (1) FORWARD PLACEMENT — a new tenant-upgrade version
  registered AFTER the target's final registered version: v4.0.8
  on the landing target origin/main
  3cf38889bca2d183e973e78b1288f8c704727542 (final 4.0.7 — upstream
  #31497 consolidated the unpublished 4.0.8-4.0.17 steps into the
  frozen 4.0.7 handler and removed those packages, so the derived
  predecessor-final-plus-one number recomputes to the now-free
  4.0.8; MinUpgradeVersion is 4.0.7). The version NUMBER is a
  derived value, re-computed as predecessor-final-plus-one and
  re-verified against the then-current origin/main at landing
  time, never hardcoded below the target's last registration; (2)
  EXISTING MIGRATIONS PRESERVED — the consolidated, frozen 4.0.7
  handler (which now owns the former v4_0_15 database-defaults
  entries and the v4_0_16/v4_0_17 steps byte- and order-identical
  per #31497) stays byte- and order-identical;
  the new package's tenant list carries ONLY the update-link entry
  (frontend.MoCatalogDataBranchUpdateLinkDDL, CREATE_NEW_TABLE,
  CheckTableDefinition guard — the reviewed handler shape from the
  era-29 v4_0_15 package, idempotence semantics unchanged),
  MinUpgradeVersion set to the predecessor final version,
  registration appended last in upgrade.go, and the
  statistics-refresh test gains the same hop-guard extension the
  current diff demonstrates; (3) CONTROLLED BASE UPDATE — the era-35
  turn integrated the then-current origin/main owning
  v4.0.15-4.0.17 as a controlled base update (a verified
  prerequisite, not mere staleness), preserving the current diff,
  relocating the era-29 package to the new version path, and
  re-running the affected bootstrap/version gates and the upgrade
  battery — no unrelated repair rides along; the 2026-10-29 landing
  rebase integrated 3cf3888 whose #31497 folded and removed the
  unpublished 4.0.8-4.0.17 handlers, and the package relocated to
  v4_0_8 with the same entries; (4) TENANT SEMANTICS UNCHANGED —
  new accounts keep receiving the table from predefined DDL; fresh
  clusters initialize the system tenant AT the final version through
  predefined DDL — bootstrap runs initPreprocessSQL and
  frontend.InitSysTenant at GetFinalVersion()
  (pkg/bootstrap/service.go:396-399) — so no upgrade handler
  executes for them and the table arrives with the predefined catalog
  (pkg/frontend/authenticate.go's predefined DDL); fresh-cluster
  schema validation is the predefined-DDL/plan-TableDef/writer-batch
  agreement battery, distinct from the existing-tenant
  upgrade-selection tests below; the §7 mixed-version and downgrade
  degradations
  are untouched (a fixed CN facing a tenant whose table is missing
  still degrades to legacy replay — including a tenant
  pre-upgrade).

  Invariants: (i) REACHABILITY — for every tenant version V below
  the new version, the greater-than selection chain from V through
  the ordered handle list reaches the new handler: existing 4.0.7
  tenants and every older recorded version alike — fresh clusters are
  recorded at the final version at bootstrap and receive the table
  through predefined DDL, so no handler reachability is owed to them;
  (ii)
  PRESERVATION — no existing handler's entries, order, or metadata
  change; (iii) IDEMPOTENCE — the CheckTableDefinition guard makes
  a repeated upgrade run a no-op and keeps fresh predefined-DDL
  accounts safe; (iv) NUMBER FRESHNESS — the handler version at
  landing is always greater than the target's final registered
  version, re-verified at implementation and landing; (v) NO
  HISTORY REWRITE — the superseded placement never shipped, so no
  tenant carries state from it and no rescue migration is needed.

  Deterministic regressions (planned, execute in the
  implementation turn, extending §10's upgrade row): (a) UPGRADE
  PATH — a tenant fixture recorded at the target's final
  registered version (4.0.7) lacking the table runs the new
  handler and gains mo_data_branch_update_link with the §3 schema
  exactly as predefined.go, the plan TableDef, and the writer
  batch agree; (b) REPEATED UPGRADE — a second run performs no DDL
  and no error (CheckFunc short-circuit); (c) SELECTION WITNESSES
  — a tenant at 4.0.7 selects exactly the new handler; a tenant
  already at the new version selects none; RED discriminant: a
  handler registered at or below the tenant version is never
  selected — the r40 placement's exact failure shape; (d) SCHEMA
  AGREEMENT stays, moved to the new version's package; (e)
  POST-UPGRADE LIVE — a cluster pre-seeded at 4.0.7 and upgraded
  runs the f1cascade battery: MERGE and PICK keys(2,4) pk moves
  cascade byte-identical to the native control; (f) gates and
  restart batteries re-run on the updated base (bootstrap tree
  incl. the new version suite); era-29 R17-R19 restart evidence
  stays valid for the no-upgrade fresh-cluster path and is
  re-cited.

- D150 (r43, review F2, refines D144 part (2), invariant (ii), and
  planned test (c)): the carry journal preserves every round's undo
  until that round completes — no composition, ever. r38's
  premise for composition was that intermediate identities have no
  observer between rounds because txn.Lock is held; the false half
  is observing after FAILURE: the staged-cell rewrite loop
  (pk_move_link_fixup.go:4010-4039) can break mid-round with cells
  split across both identities, and the real observers of the
  intermediate state are the unwind walk itself and the next
  statement's rollback boundary, not a map reader under the lock.
  The implemented overwrite additionally kept the EARLIER entry's
  seq, so a chain crossing the statement boundary aliased into the
  earlier statement's entry and unwindPkMoveCarryJournalLocked's
  rolledStmt selection never touched it. The journal therefore
  journals each round as its own entry — appended in order,
  stamped with the CURRENT statement's seq, entries immutable once
  written (no in-place newIds rewrite, no tip-directed
  composition). Chained pairs (the round's old side minted by an
  earlier journaled round) start a new chronological entry
  referencing the intermediate identity exactly; the journal tips
  map survives only as the admission projection aid, never as an
  edit channel. Admission charges EVERY effective pair at (2 x
  RowidSize + 16) plus per-entry overhead — the projected
  charge stays exactly the real growth, satisfying D144's
  admission-before-mutation and loud-refusal clauses (i), (iii),
  (iv) unchanged; D146/D148's measured-area argument is untouched
  because the charge here is the journal bytes themselves (D148
  already made the staged-cell mutation byte-neutral, so journal
  growth is the only growth). D145/D147's settled-prefix adoption
  walk is untouched: settlement freezes both ledgers against the
  adopted cut, and the walk keys on entries, not on composition.
  Unwind semantics gain their missing guarantee: the strict
  reverse-chronological walk over per-round entries restores any
  chained sequence stepwise — a failed N->P round's own entry
  is inverted (current-cell P -> N, including every cell the
  partial failure already rewrote and no cell it missed), then the
  completed O->N round's entry is inverted (N -> O) — exact
  restoration when the second round fails mid-carry, exact
  restoration when the two rounds belong to different statements
  (the rolled statement selects only its own stamped entries and
  restores its own round's partial writes; the completed earlier
  statement's state is by definition not rolled). Statement-abort
  release still walks every carried pair of the rolled region with
  zero residue; the inverse never re-admits (D146/D148 unchanged).
  Deterministic regressions (planned, execute with the
  implementation turn): (a) completed O->N round, then an
  injected PARTIAL overwrite failure on the chained N->P round in
  the SAME statement — both rounds carry the rolled
  statement's seq (D150 stamps every entry with the CURRENT
  statement's seq), so the retained walker
  (pk_move_link_fixup.go:3218-3226) selects both and the
  stepwise unwind applies BOTH inverses: the failed round's
  entry first (every partial P write back to N exactly, the
  intermediate checkpoint), then the completed round's entry
  (N back to O); assert the unwind passes through a byte-exact
  intermediate N checkpoint and ends with every provenance map
  and staged cell byte-identical to the PRE-CHAIN O state,
  BOTH entries consumed, the chained tip forgotten, and a
  healthy retry of the WHOLE chain (O->N, then N->P)
  completing — accepting N as the final state would
  preserve identities belonging to the rolled-back statement
  and is a failure, not acceptance; RED discriminant: the
  r42 composition leaves N/P-split cells after rollback; (b) the same chain where the failed round belongs to
  the NEXT statement — assert RollbackLastStatement restores
  the failed statement's partial writes and leaves statement k's
  completed O->N state untouched (RED: the r42 composition is
  invisible to the rolled statement and leaves P cells
  unrestored); (c) N completed chained rounds unwind stepwise
  byte-exactly; (d) charge accounting: a chain of N rounds charges
