  N effective pairs (charge == growth) and refusal still aborts
  before any mutation.

- D151 (r43, review F1, refines D144 as clause (v)): EVERY carry
  admission boundary — the boundary-dump origin translation
  (pk_move_link_fixup.go:2855) and the object-transfer re-key
  (transfer_util.go:475) alike — applies the shared
  participation rule: with no live staged link rows
  (pkMoveHasLiveStagedLinksLocked), the pair-list integrity checks
  and the effective-pair computation STILL run, the journal
  append STILL happens (rollback journaling preserved — the
  carried remaps mutate origin-heal maps that die with the
  transaction, but a rolled statement must still unwind them),
  and the budget refusal is SKIPPED, because a transaction
  without staged links commits no provenance and its marker
  bookkeeping dies with it — the exact r22/r23 contract the
  fill-end, diverted-delete, swallowed-delete, and pre-dump
  boundaries already honor (:704-710). With staged links the
  admission enforces unchanged, including the first-link
  full-measure admission at fill/first-link time
  (checkPkMoveBookkeepBudgetLocked), so an update-then-move
  transaction still stops statement-atomically at the move and a
  provenance-heavy transaction never commits unbounded durable
  growth. Deterministic regressions (planned, execute with the
  implementation turn): (a) marker-only bulk payload UPDATE under
  a deterministically LOWERED coordinator budget crossing every
  charged byte class (origins, lineage, heals) through a boundary
  dump (maintenance window open) commits with no
  provenance-budget error; (b) the same marker-only shape through
  a tombstone object-transfer round (holdsPkMoveProvenanceLocked
  true on marker presence alone, :3397-3402) also commits; (c)
  rollback of a later statement in each shape restores the
  carried maps byte-identically (journaling was preserved, only
  the refusal skipped) and a retry round succeeds; (d) the
  paired control: adding one staged link batch re-enables the
  refusal with the full measure, refused before mutation,
  statement-atomic; (e) RED discriminant: on the r42 tree the
  same (a)/(b) shapes fail with the coordinator-budget error.

- r43 review F3 hardening note (no new decision): D143's
  surface-failure premise (the unwind comments at
  types.go:1896-1899 and the restore comments at :1914-1916:
  ‘a failure to unwind / a restore failure must surface, not
  vanish into a silently dangling identity’) requires the
  RollbackLastStatement error aggregate to JOIN
  unwindPkMoveCarryJournalLocked's result, the positional
  restoration's result, and the resurrection's result through
  errors.Join with no overwrite; the regression injects an
  unwind failure while the later restoration succeeds and
  asserts RollbackLastStatement returns an error containing the
  unwind failure (RED: r42 reports success).

- D152 (r45, implementation review P1, refines D47/D83/D86+D98): the
  historical-retention gate that every link-reclaim probe consults
  covers ACTIVE PITR scopes exactly like user snapshots, through ONE
  shared check. D98 grounds a lineage on LIVE user snapshots only
  (branchSnapshotCoversTable's mo_snapshots query,
  compile/ddl.go:5249), but a timestamp-sourced DATA BRANCH over the
  unchanged incarnation needs no snapshot
  (validateTimestampDataBranchSourceIDs keeps same-incarnation
  clones, pkg/frontend/clone.go:170) and the frontend's own
  historical-lineage model already treats every ACTIVE mo_pitr row
  (pitr_status = 1) as a historical owner with a rolling lower bound
  (historicalPitrSourceSQL, pkg/frontend/data_branch_snapshot.go:70;
  databranchutils HistoricalSource + PitrRetentionLowerBound,
  branch_protect_snapshot.go:116-126). Verified-reachable residual
  (P1): retain P through an active PITR, note a pre-move timestamp,
  branch B from P, move a key on P, drop B — the retirement reclaim
  sees no live descendant, the snapshot-only probe reports
  uncovered, and P's links retire (compile/ddl.go:5127-5139) — then
  a PITR-retained clone H of P at the pre-move timestamp diffs
  link-bearing history whose links are gone, and MERGE/PICK replay
  the move as DELETE+INSERT (the provider probe degrades to
  proven-none, data_branch_pk_move_link.go:1444-1451), deleting
  destination children under ON DELETE CASCADE instead of cascading
  their keys. The shared check extends the existing coverage
  predicate with the active-PITR scope rule, reusing the clone
  flow's ownership vocabulary (cluster grounds everything; account,
  database, and table by scope; table additionally by the recorded
  obj_id so pre-rename retention survives, r24 review F2): a mo_pitr
  probe over pitr_status = 1 rows resolves through the sys account
  with the owning account's id, per the established
  granularity-query convention (compile/ddl.go:8715/8810-8820), and
  joins the existing mo_snapshots result under ONE coverage
  predicate, so the member-retire (compile/ddl.go:5089), orphan-
  parent (:5127), and unbranched-drop (:5366/:5368) probes all
  inherit it with no per-site drift. Any active owner grounds ALL
  current links at table granularity — the conservative union over
  every timestamp a future clone may still name; per-link
  rolling-horizon filtering is deliberately declined (over-retention
  ends with the PITR's own lifetime while under-retention silently
  destroys destination rows). Fail-ALIVE is unchanged: any probe
  error keeps the links, and a catalog image without mo_pitr yields
  no additional coverage exactly like the mo_snapshots-absence rule.
  Regressions (planned, execute with the implementation turn): (a)
  compile-package UTs on the drop-lifecycle executor fabric — active
  table/database/account/cluster-level PITR keeps the reclaimed
  member's and the orphan parent's links, obj_id coverage survives
  a rename, pitr_status = 0 and foreign-account rows do not cover,
  a probe failure keeps with the WARN, and an absent catalog keeps
  the pre-r45 behavior; RED on the pre-fix tree because no mo_pitr
  probe exists and the covered links retire; (b) live MERGE and
  PICK batteries on the issue harness: retain P via an active
  database-level PITR, record the pre-move timestamp, branch B from
  P, move P's key, drop B (the last-descendant reclaim runs), clone
  H from P{MO_TS=<pre-move>}, then MERGE P INTO H WHEN CONFLICT
  ACCEPT yields the exact parent (3,'two') and cascaded child
  (1,3) rows with the link rows kept across the drop (link-count
  probes before and after), PICK keys(2) twins it, and the RESTRICT
  flavor fails the apply with the destination byte-unchanged
  (failure atomicity) — the r23/D98 live battery shapes with the
  PITR owner substituted for the named snapshot; (c) evidence
  reuse: the amendment only WIDENS retention — every pre-r45
  covered case keeps identically and every uncovered case deletes
  identically — so the r23-r44 UT/live/BVT banks remain valid with
  unchanged inputs and are re-cited by mode and terminal result;
  the BVT fixtures stay deterministic with the snapshot-grounded
  etkf2_/etkf2p_ shapes pinning the consumer, because a wall-clock
  {MO_TS=...} literal has no deterministic BVT form and the PITR
  reachability is exercised live, matching how the D98 analog was
  established.

- r45 review P2 hardening note (no new decision): D130/D132 already
  place every registry read under durableOrphanGC.mu;
  retryDurableOrphanGC's two rejection logs evaluated len(ent.set)
  AFTER mu.Unlock (engine_orphan_gc.go:526-536), racing the
  registration write at :226 and the sweep-completion deletion at
  :436 on the same FileService with a concurrent map access, and
  the closed-engine early-return path overlaps exactly the other
  engine population D131 permits. Capture the count under the lock
  in both branches. Focused race regression (planned): overlap
  retryDurableOrphanGC on a closed engine with a
  register/sweep-completion loop on one FileService under `-race`;
  pre-fix the run is fatal with a concurrent-map-access diagnostic,
  post-fix clean, and the sequential r22-r42 registry batteries keep
  passing unchanged.

- D153 (r46, design review r45 P2, refines D152/D98/D83/D86/D47): links
  retained under the D152 union for a table that then disappears gain a
  terminal lifecycle. D152 defines KEEP only at table/subtree
  retirement, and owner-removal flows invoke only the ALTER-lineage
  compactor (pkg/frontend/pitr.go:858), which selects ALTER generations
  and deletes their snapshot/metadata rows
  (pkg/frontend/data_branch_snapshot.go:299-307;
  databranchutils/branch_protect_snapshot.go:401-403) - it never
  rediscovers ordinary dropped tables, so a retained dead table's
  links would outlive every owner forever and repeated retain-then-
  drop-owner cycles grow the catalog without bound (verified: the link
  catalog's only DELETE runs from the three retire funnels,
  pkg/sql/compile/ddl.go:4871 with call sites :5100/:5139/:5380 plus
  the ALTER-generation stream-death path, and mo_branch_metadata
  stores no table names, pkg/frontend/predefined.go:413-423, so
  dead-table identity is otherwise unrecoverable post-drop). Terminal
  reclamation therefore has three parts.

  (a) Retention ledger. A new account-scoped catalog
  mo_catalog.mo_data_branch_link_retention (table_id primary key,
  database_name, table_name, obj_id, created_ts) joins through the
  same tenant-upgrade pattern that introduced the link catalog
  (v4_0_8). Every funnel KEEP verdict writes one keyed, retry-
  idempotent ledger row inside the SAME dropping transaction as the
  keep: reclaimUnbranchedDropPkMoveLinks' grounded and probe-failure
  returns (pkg/sql/compile/ddl.go:5358-5381) with the caller-supplied
  identity (empty names preserve the fallback probe's by-id-only
  parity exactly), and deletePkMoveUpdateLinksForReclaimedSubtrees'
  grounded and identity-unresolved keeps (:5084-5099) with the
  admission-captured identity. The live orphan parent (:5137) takes
  no row: its own eventual drop flows through the unbranched funnel.
  Ledger writes mirror the funnel's POST-mutation KEEP verdict - they
  never re-derive coverage, so ordering inside the retire flow is
  preserved by construction - and ledger rows die only with their
  links or the account. r55 amendment (D159): admission generalizes
  from KEEP-verdict-only to link-record GENESIS - every link address
  gains its keyed ledger row inside the recording transaction itself,
  and the funnel writes above become insert-or-refresh upsert
  contacts over that row (created_ts immutable; they remain the
  fallback admission for the capability-gated eras D159(C) defines).
  The live-orphan-parent no-row rule is superseded: its genesis row
  exists from its own first recorded move. 'Ledger rows die only
  with their links or the account' keeps force under the rebounded
  invariant D159(E) pins: the row set equals the distinct link
  addresses with surviving rows, gone with the last link or the
  account.

  (b) Reap at owner disappearance. doDropPitr at every level
  (pkg/frontend/pitr.go:779-862, after every owner-row mutation
  including the internal sys-catalog row cascade) and doDropSnapshot
  for user rows (pkg/frontend/snapshot.go:679-760) run a reap pass
  INSIDE the same pessimistic txn that already holds the lineage-owner
  lifecycle gate (pitr.go:803, snapshot.go:699): scan the account's
  ledger rows, re-evaluate the SAME shared coverage predicate D152
  defines (user snapshots + ACTIVE PITR scopes, obj_id rename
  robustness, by-id fallback for empty-name rows) against the
  surviving owner set; uncovered -> deleteDataBranchUpdateLinks plus
  the ledger row; covered -> keep both; probe failure -> keep both
  with the WARN (fail-ALIVE mirrors the funnels). Owner-set mutation,
  link deletion, and ledger deletion commit atomically, so no
  committed state ever shows the final owner gone with links kept -
  the r45 finding's missing terminal transition is exactly this
  event. The candidate set is the ledger itself: complete by (a),
  bounded by retained-dead-table count. r55 amendment (D159): with
  genesis admission the candidate set is bounded by the count of
  distinct link addresses with surviving rows (live plus retained-
  dead), and the reap orders one batched, chunk-bounded SELF-LIVE
  probe after the coverage miss and before the descendant walk
  (D159(D)), so a live producer is a KEEP, never a candidate for
  deletion. ALTER-PITR shrink is no reap
  trigger - the D152 union deliberately grounds ALL links while any
  active owner exists, so shrink retains until the owner dies -
  and account drop wipes the whole account namespace.

  (c) Synchronization with owner creation. The reap holds the
  lifecycle gate that drop-PITR (all levels), drop-SNAPshot and
  SNAPshot creation already hold (pkg/frontend/snapshot.go:389) and
  that account/cluster CREATE PITR holds (pitr.go:330).
  Database/table CREATE PITR already orders against the gate:
  pitr.go:325-327 routes through admitLocalLifecycleRC, whose
  beginLifecycleRCAdmission locks the SNAPSHOT feature-registry row
  in SHARED mode before the exclusive database-name target lock
  (lifecycle_admission_rc.go:43-55,175-179) - the same registry key
  the drop-side gate holds exclusively
  (catalog.SnapshotLifecycleGateSQL via
  databranchutils.LineageOwnerLifecyclePessimisticLockSQL),
  transaction-owned under enforced pessimistic RC (:150-153). r49
  corrects the r46 premise that this path lacked gate ownership
  (r48-approval P3): NO additional gate acquisition is introduced
  anywhere, because shared-creation vs exclusive-reap ordering on
  one transaction-owned key already puts every owner-set transition
  in one total order with reaps; the validation asserts the
  existing ordering rather than adding a lock. The
  independent second net is admission clamping: RESTORE PITR rejects
  ts <= create_time (pkg/frontend/pitr.go:2216), a snapshot pins
  state at its own creation ts so a dead table is simply absent, and
  timestamp clones consult no owner - they ride on physical
  readability, whose contractual guarantee comes from exactly the
  mo_snapshots + mo_pitr rows the GC waterline consumes
  (checkpointCleaner window,
  pkg/vm/engine/tae/db/gc/v3/checkpoint.go:1164/:1277-1279). Every
  link a reap deletes committed before the reap's txn, so an owner
  created after its read admits none of it.

  Candidate-discovery summary: the ledger is the complete candidate
  set; the coverage re-evaluation is the one D152 predicate shared
  with the funnels (no per-site drift); the ALTER compactor stays
  scoped to ALTER generations, whose links die via
  deletePkMoveUpdateLinksForIDs at physical-stream death (unchanged);
  pre-r46 retained links predating the ledger have no rows to reap
  and remain the benign orphanage the D98 family already accepts
  under O1's long-lived-table scope.

  Regressions (planned, execute with the implementation turn): (a)
  compile-fabric UTs on the drop-lifecycle executor - unbranched-drop
  and covered member-retire KEEP paths emit one ledger INSERT with
  the retained identity and a retried drop keeps it single-rowed;
  RED on the pre-fix tree because the catalog and INSERT do not
  exist; (b) frontend-fabric UTs on the mock background exec -
  doDropPitr at each level and doDropSnapshot emit the ledger scan,
  the coverage re-probes, and the paired link+ledger DELETEs only in
  the final-owner case; a surviving user snapshot or a surviving
  PITR keeps both, and a probe failure keeps both; RED pre-fix; (c)
  CREATE PITR database/table levels emit the lifecycle-gate SQL
  before the mo_pitr insert (existing pitr fabric, RED pre-fix); (d)
  live retain-then-remove-final-owner battery on the issue harness:
  create a database-level PITR, run the issue's pk-move, drop the
  table (link AND ledger counts non-zero), drop the PITR (both
  zero); the surviving-snapshot twin keeps both through drop-PITR
  and loses both only at drop SNAPshot; deterministic owner-event
  boundaries, no wall-clock MO_TS named. (e) evidence reuse: the
  ledger adds one INSERT at KEEP verdicts and a gated reap at owner
  drops; an empty ledger leaves every pre-r46 reclaim byte-
  identical, so the r23-r45 UT/live/BVT banks stay valid with
  unchanged inputs.

- D154 (r47, design review r46 findings P1 + four P2, refines D153):
  the retained-dead-table lifecycle gets its ownership, discovery,
  exceptional-path, and restore contracts corrected. The r46 review
  verified five gaps at exact loci (/tmp/e43_vf.log): the reap
  inherited the owner predicate, whose query deliberately excludes
  kind='branch' protect snapshots (pkg/sql/compile/ddl.go:5248 -
  "Rows with kind='branch' are filtered by the caller's query:
  branch-protect snapshots retire with the branch metadata rows the
  descendant probe already covers", :5165-5168), yet D153(b) never
  ran that descendant probe, so a user-snapshot drop ordered between
  a historical clone's creation (clone.go:1758-1775 +
  data_branch_snapshot.go:461-505, atomic descendant row + protect
  snapshot) and its MERGE would erase the dropped member's provenance
  under a live descendant and replay DELETE (proven-none,
  data_branch_pk_move_link.go:1444-1451) instead of the issue's
  native UPDATE; a row-less root can die physically while a child
  stays live - its drop skips the unbranched funnel because
  tableHasBranchLineage matches either side (ddl.go:4909-4927,
  :5792-5801), the reclaim closure returns for metadata-less ids
  (lifecycle_branch_reclaim.go:65-76, its own comment accepting
  "benign orphans"), and the later child retire fails closed KEEP
  (ddl.go:5224-5228) with no ledger row ever written; mo_pitr is
  sys-scoped (authenticate.go:963-970) with cluster rows at
  account_id=0 (pitr.go:395-410) and sys-created account rows for
  other tenants (:446-474), which a session-local reap scan cannot
  see; probe-failure keeps at a final-owner removal had no retry
  owner (DROP PITR IF EXISTS on an absent name returns before
  maintenance, pitr.go:813-820) and empty-name rows inherit a probe
  that keeps them forever; and restore semantics were unspecified
  even though the link catalog is registry-skipped
  (snapshot.go:180-184) while an unregistered sys-account catalog
  bulk-restores (snapshot.go:2194-2216). The five corrections, lettered
  to the findings:

  (A) Live-descendant recheck and ownership transfer. The reap
  deletes a ledger row's links only when BOTH predicates hold: no
  historical owner under the shared D152 predicate AND no live
  lineage descendant under the same DAG walk the orphan-parent
  funnel uses (branchHasLiveLineageDescendant, ddl.go:5298-5348),
  evaluated on the reap txn's current image. This restores the
  :5165-5168 pairing the owner predicate assumes: protect snapshots
  are excluded from owners exactly because live descendants gate
  separately. Ownership transfers cleanly: a historical clone that
  creates a descendant over ledger-kept links keeps them via the
  liveness half at every later reap, and when that final branch
  retires, the funnels - which already re-evaluate the same two
  gates at :5114-5139 - discharge links AND the matching ledger
  row(s) in their delete path, and refresh/keep the row in their
  covered path; ledger maintenance thus mirrors link reality at
  every funnel verdict. The D153(b) text is refined accordingly:
  "covered -> keep" becomes "covered by owner(s) OR by liveness ->
  keep"; "uncovered -> delete" requires the conjunction.

  (B) Early root capture and ledger-consult identity. The
  lineage-referenced drop skip (ddl.go:5792-5801) now persists a
  ledger row for the DROPPED table with the drop flow's own plan
  identity - (dbName, tblName, tblID) is in exact scope there,
  unlike every later point - when a cheap link-presence probe finds
  rows or errors (fail into retention); this is the one place the
  row-less root's identity outlives its physical retirement. Every
  fail-closed funnel path consults the ledger before falling back:
  the orphan-parent funnel (ddl.go:5114-5141) and the by-id probe's
  mo_tables miss (:5220-5230) evaluate coverage with the ledgered
  identity when present, so a root dropped while a child lived is
  reapable at the child's retire and at later owner events; the
  fail-closed KEEP survives only for the ledger-missed defensive
  residue defined in (D). Members whose admission names are missing
  likewise resolve from the ledger (their own earlier capture);
  member covered/kept paths keep mirroring the row. The D153(a)
  phrase "the live orphan parent takes no row" is superseded: a
  parent already physically gone takes its row at ITS drop, through
  the skip-site capture.

  (C) Affected-account discovery for global owners. The ledger
  stays per-account (predefinedTables sibling of the link catalog),
  and the reap's account set is the set the REMOVED owner rows
  covered: cluster-level rows (account_id=0) select every tenant
  account; sys-created account-level rows select exactly their
  recorded target account (pitr.go:446-474); account-self,
  database- and table-level rows and every user snapshot select the
  owning account only. doDropSnapshot's publication resolution
  (snapshot.go:710-718) yields the owning account the same way.
  Execution enumerates mo_account under the sys account and runs
  each selected account's scan with that account attached
  (defines.AttachAccountId) - the drop-account flow's own precedent
  for sys-scoped per-account cleanup by account id
  (authenticate.go:4420-4475). An account whose catalog cannot be
  attached (mid-creation/suspension transitions) keeps its rows
  with WARN, the funnel-side fail-ALIVE symmetry; drop account
  wipes the whole namespace as today.

  (D) Exceptional-path terminal lifecycle. Inside an owner-removal
  reap, a coverage or liveness probe ERROR now fails the drop
  statement: the pessimistic txn rolls back, so the owner row, all
  links, and all ledger rows persist atomically and the identical
  retry runs the reap again - the finding's "keep owner removal
  retryable through transaction failure" alternative. Funnel-side
  probe errors stay fail-ALIVE (table drops must not wedge) with
  the ledger row carrying the best-known identity, reachable at the
  next owner event. Identity-unresolved paths resolve through the
  ledger first (B); a true ledger miss - reachable only outside the
  production capture chain (pre-ledger legacy, corruption repair) -
  keeps the links AND an empty-name row, which the reap NEVER
  auto-deletes: it is an explicit operator-visible residue class
  owned by O1, surfaced by WARN at every reap, so the eventual-
  reclamation claim covers the complete identity-bearing class and
  nothing else. An empty ledger skips probe traffic entirely, so
  owner drops without retained dead tables see no new failure mode.

  (E) Restore semantics. The ledger registers in
  systemCatalogRestorePolicies with systemCatalogRestoreSkip
  beside MO_DATA_BRANCH_UPDATE_LINK (snapshot.go:104-184); the
  shared classifier needSkipTable (snapshot.go:2194-2216) governs
  snapshot AND PITR restore (pitr.go:2442), and its tenant rule
  already skips unregistered mo_catalog tables while the sys rule
  would restore them - the registration is what makes the skip
  coherent in every account. Ledger and link catalogs are therefore
  always skipped TOGETHER; restoring a snapshot or PITR never
  imports historical ledger rows (their table ids belong to
  incarnations the restore invalidates, exactly the link catalog's
  registry comment), older snapshots predating the upgrade have no
  table to restore and skip silently, and post-restore both
  catalogs start empty with live tables re-ledgerizing at their own
  later drops. Section 7's restore discipline for the link catalog
  gains the sibling row verbatim.

  Regressions (planned, execute with the implementation turn): (1)
  etkf2-family MERGE/PICK twins with the user snapshot dropped
  BETWEEN historical-clone creation and apply - links and ledger
  survive the reap (liveness half), the fold yields the exact
  parent (3,'two') and cascaded child (1,3), the RESTRICT twin
  fails atomically with the destination byte-unchanged, and
  retiring the final branch discharges links and ledger with no
  owner left; RED on the pre-fix tree where the coverage-only reap
  deletes. (2) Root-drop -> last-child-drop -> final-owner-drop:
  skip-site INSERT, orphan consult, and zero counts only at the
  final event; compile-fabric UTs RED pre-fix (no skip write, no
  ledger). (3) Multi-tenant live battery: cluster-PITR removal from
  sys reaps a non-system tenant's rows, a surviving tenant snapshot
  preserves them, sys-created account PITR removal reaps exactly its
  tenant, and tenant-local drops leave foreign tenants untouched.
  (4) Fabric UTs for the exceptional paths: injected reap-probe
  failure aborts drop with owner+links+ledger intact and retry
  completes; admission-miss with ledger hit evaluates and
  discharges; ledger-miss empty-name survives with WARN, no DELETE.
  (5) Live restore battery over snapshot and PITR restore plus a
  registry UT asserting needSkipTable verdicts for sys and tenant
  accounts; RED pre-fix for the sys catalog. (6) Evidence reuse:
  refinements touch only ledger/reap heuristics, one registry entry,
  and one gate join; with empty ledger and registry deltas the
  r23-r46 UT/live/BVT banks stay valid with unchanged inputs.

- D155 (r48, design review r47 findings P1 + two P2, refines D152
  and D154(C)/(D)/(E)): the retained-dead-table lifecycle closes
  the sys-owned owner topology, hardens the owner-removal error
  contract, and splits the restore contract. The r47 review
  verified three gaps at exact loci (/tmp/e44_vf.log): cross-tenant
  and cluster snapshot rows publish into SYS's mo_snapshots
  (snapshot.go:420-440,481-508 under the :662-674 priv gate, the
  INSERT riding the creator session's executor :648-652), so a
  tenant whose only surviving owner is such a row fails D152's
  account-local coverage probe (ddl.go:5246-5251); D154(C) admitted
  commit-with-WARN when an affected account's catalog could not be
  attached, after which the owner is gone and DROP PITR/SNAPSHOT
  IF EXISTS early-returns before maintenance (pitr.go:813-820;
  snapshot.go:722-729), stranding discoverable rows outside O1's
  scope; and D154(E)'s "post-restore both catalogs start empty"
  oracle contradicts the skip policy, which excludes historical
  imports only and leaves current contents untouched
  (snapshot.go:180-184,:1710-1715; pitr.go:2055-2059).

  (A) Sys-owned snapshot coverage (refines D152's owner predicate).
  The shared coverage probe gains a second half resolved under the
  sys account with the probing tenant attached: cluster-level rows
  (level='cluster', obj_id=MaxUint64) cover every account, and
  account-level rows whose recorded target (account_name/obj_id)
  matches the tenant cover that tenant. Sys-scoped database/table
  rows are NOT extended: they resolve inside the creator's own
  namespace (snapshot.go:512-527,603-607) and are owner-local by
  construction, so the account-local half already sees them. The
  sys half joins the account-local rows and the mo_pitr probe under
  D152's ONE coverage predicate, so the member-retire, orphan-
  parent, and unbranched-drop probes inherit it with no per-site
  drift. Fail-ALIVE is symmetric: a sys-half probe error keeps the
  links with WARN, and an absent catalog image yields no coverage
  from that half, exactly the existing rule. The coverage is real
  retention: logtail appends cluster snapshot timestamps to every
  tenant's tables (logtail/snapshot.go:2159-2163) and a timestamp
  clone of an unchanged incarnation stays admissible
  (clone.go:198-200), which is what makes the missing probe
  destructively reachable today.

  (B) Affected-account discovery for snapshot owners (refines
  D154(C)'s discovery). doDropSnapshot already reads the removed
  row's kind before the DELETE (snapshot.go:735-738); for
  non-branch kinds that read also takes level, account_name, and
  obj_id, and the reap's account set derives from the removed row
  exactly like the PITR rule: a cluster row selects every tenant in
  mo_account; an account-level row selects its recorded target
  tenant; sys-local rows select sys only; tenant-local drops remain
  account-local; publication drops keep the publishing-account
  resolution (snapshot.go:705-714). The read rides the same
  pessimistic transaction as the DELETE and the reap, so
  classification cannot race the removal; IF EXISTS early-returns
  before the read (snapshot.go:722-729), so a missing owner fires
  no reap, as today. With (A) in place, a non-system tenant's
  retained links now disappear only when their last owner -
  including a sys-owned one - actually disappears.

  (C) Fail-atomic owner-removal reaps (refines D154(C)/(D)). EVERY
  error inside an owner-removal reap fails the drop statement
  atomically: mo_account enumeration, per-account attach/open/scan,
  and the coverage/liveness probes D154(D) already named. The
  pessimistic transaction rolls back, so the owner row and every
  already-processed account's links and ledger persist
  byte-identically and the identical retry re-runs the complete
  reap. The r47 commit-with-WARN clause for inaccessible accounts
  is DELETED: an unverifiable account keeps the drop failing until
  it is attachable again, a truly dropped account's namespace is
  wiped by the drop-account flow as today
  (authenticate.go:4420-4475), and no stranded discoverable-row
  class is created, so O1's scope is unchanged. Funnel-side table
  drops stay fail-ALIVE (drops must not wedge) with ledgerized
  identity; the empty-name O1 residue is unchanged; an empty ledger
  still skips reap traffic entirely, so owner drops without
  retained dead tables see no new failure mode.

  (D) Restore semantics split (refines D154(E)). The single
  "post-restore empty catalogs" oracle becomes two separately
  validated properties. Historical-import exclusion (the r47 half,
  unchanged): the ledger registers systemCatalogRestoreSkip beside
  MO_DATA_BRANCH_UPDATE_LINK; the shared classifier needSkipTable
  skips both in every account for snapshot AND PITR restore
  (snapshot.go:2194-2216; pitr.go:2442); snapshots predating the
  upgrade have no rows to import and skip silently.
  Current-pair preservation (new): the skip policy leaves current
  contents untouched by construction, so pre-existing link and
  ledger rows SURVIVE any restore byte-for-byte. Survivors stay
  correct: consumption keys on exact table ids resolved as-of the
  named timestamp, so a historical clone grounded by a surviving
  pre-restore owner still names the retained incarnation; owners
  themselves are skip-registered (snapshot.go:167-168) and survive
  restore, keeping the retention topology intact; rows whose owners
  were already gone are the ordinary reclaim-eligible class the
  next owner drop reaps. No bulk clear ever runs: clearing a
  restored account's catalogs would under-retain rows whose owners
  still ground them - the F1 class of bug - and a database-scoped
  restore has no mandate over the account's other tables. Lifecycle
  liveness across restore is asserted: a moved table dropped after
  restore re-ledgerizes beside the survivors, and a subsequent
  final-owner drop reaps the pre-existing rows normally.

  Regressions (planned, execute with the implementation turn): (1)
  compile-fabric UTs for (A) - sys-owned cluster/account rows keep
  the reclaimed member's and orphan parent's links, foreign-target
  rows do not, sys-half probe failure keeps with WARN; RED pre-fix
  because no sys half exists. (2) Live multi-tenant MERGE/PICK
  battery for (A)+(B) - a tenant protected solely by a sys-owned
  cluster snapshot keeps links+ledger across its last branch
  retire, the surviving-owner session folds MERGE/PICK to the
  exact (3,'two')/(1,3) rows, sys dropping that snapshot reaps
  exactly the unprotected tenant set, and a sys-created account
  snapshot for U reaps U while leaving T untouched. (3) Fabric UTs
  for (C) - a second-of-three attach failure aborts the drop after
  the first account was processed, rollback preserves the owner row
  and every account's links/ledger byte-identically, and the retry
  completes all three; RED pre-fix where the commit-with-WARN class
  exists. (4) Restore battery for (D) - classifier UTs (RED pre-fix
  for the sys instance), snapshot AND PITR restore leaving
  link+ledger byte-identical (content-pinned, not empty), the
  predating-snapshot skip, consumption-after-restore through a
  snapshot-named historical clone with the exact issue rows, and
  post-restore lifecycle liveness. (5) Evidence reuse: with empty
  ledger and registry deltas, and no sys-owned snapshot rows in any
  pre-r48 scenario, every r23-r47 path stays byte-identical, so
  those banks stand re-cited by mode and terminal result.

- D156 (r50, design answer to r60 review F1 (P1), refines D87's
  unrecorded-replacement boundary, executes D2/D15's pre-authorized
  commit-exact direction without a catalog shape change): failed-scope
  attribution is derived from the link catalog's OWN committed change
  stream, not from approximations over the data stream. Background:
  D2/D15 record write_ts as the move transaction's CREATE ts, a strict
  lower bound of its commit, while anchor-tie and same-key-tail queries
  are commit-shaped; an arrival-attribution failure must therefore name
  feasible COMMIT instants of the failed chain. The code-level
  committed-stream approximations (channel 1: tombstones at keys the
  chain's links depart from; channel 2: arrival-key collision deaths
  paired by the departed-birth index to a birth before the chain's
  creation) cover only deaths whose victim's birth insert lies inside
  the observed window. The r60 counterexample sits exactly outside
  that cover: with the chain's commit evidence carried by a death
  whose victim was born BEFORE the window, stream evidence alone is
  non-discriminating - 'the chain committed in-window and vacuumed the
  pre-existing committed occupant' (must fail closed) and 'a pre-window
  chain's landed image was replaced by a later in-window edit' (must
  stay silent, the D87 pre-fork long-chain merge control) attach to the
  same re-born instant with the same unpaired shape. Answering None
  there converts unresolved attribution into absence: the truncated
  foreign arrival folds onto a destination lineage and cascades its
  children (F1), violating I1's rule that unresolved provenance
  degrades to the legacy path. Poisoning the instant anyway would
  falsely abort the D87 control. The only sound discriminator is the
  chain's actual commit instant.

  (A) Capture mechanism. At arrival-build time the provider streams
  the mo_catalog.mo_data_branch_update_link relation's committed
  changes over the apply window's exact collected bounds ((F))
  through engine Relation.CollectChanges - the generic relation path
  exercised by the
  table_changes table function (pkg/sql/colexec/table_function/
  table_changes.go:202) and proven on catalog tables by the
  table_func_table_changes fixture (mo_catalog.mo_database/mo_tables
  stream with commit_ts rows). The SQL projection path is NOT usable
  for this table (its `table_id` column conflicts with the reserved
  table_changes metadata names; live-verified rejection), so the
  capture is engine-level and calls Relation.CollectChanges on the
  resolved link relation directly under the (E) policy context - the
  databranchutils.CollectChanges helper is expressly unsuitable for
  it per (E). The capture streams rows into an index keyed by
  transaction scope (txn_id/write_ts) naming each in-window-committed
  scope's exact commit ts, folding batches incrementally under the
  (G) bounds and admission filter rather than queueing the full
  stream. Every link row committed in-window appears exactly once
  in the stream; the retained index is bounded by admitted relevant
  scopes, not by the relation-wide row count.

  (B) Semantics. failedArrivalCommitsLocked becomes: memo per scope
  (unchanged) over index lookup (replaces the scan). Scope present in
  the index => the chain committed in-window at exactly the recorded
  instant; the failed attribution names exactly that instant, so any
  fold query touching it answers Incomplete and the verdict fails
  closed (I1). Scope absent => the chain committed outside the apply
  window (its link rows can still be probe-visible history, e.g. the
  D87 pre-fork chain); it names nothing and the fold proceeds. Exact
  commit evidence removes BOTH failure directions at once: the
  approximation channels' over-poisoning risk (an unrelated same-window
  removal could be mistaken for the chain's commit) and the
  r60 under-poisoning hole (absence mistaken for resolution). The
  index feeds ONLY failed-scope attribution; it never enters byPK
  occupancy matching, so D15's straddler lane (write_ts >= fork
  implies commit in-window; straddlers fail closed) and D87's
  predMissing lane keep their current semantics and fixtures.

  (C) Capture integrity. The capture must be COMPLETE for the window
  or the affected build fails closed: an engine error or a truncated
  capture poisons every unfailed attribution query of that build per
  the file's established arrivalWindowsComplete posture - never a
  silent downgrade to absence. A pre-upgrade cluster without the link
  table deactivates provenance wholesale, exactly as today (D5 and the
  upgrade gate). Resolvable chains never consult the index, so the
  success path carries no new failure mode; cancellation is D157.
  r51 sharpens the incomplete producers to an explicit list: an engine
  error (including the checkpoint-replay recovery classes surfacing an
  unservable or compacted window per (E)), a substituted or synthetic
  timestamp detection (which the (E) policy context makes impossible
  by construction and the ctx guards reject up front), and certified
  truncation; capacity exhaustion is NOT silent either - it takes the
  (G) NF8/I6 provider-disable lane rather than the statement-failure
  lane.

  (D) What this supersedes. Channels 1/2 and the unpaired-names-nothing
  lane were code-level approximations added under r49 without a design
  decision; D156 replaces them with exactness. Their proof obligations
  are strict subsets: the r59 paired-occupant PICK regression (chain
  committed in-window at a recorded instant) still fails closed because
  the scope IS present; the hpo merge control (chain committed
  pre-fork) still folds because the scope is absent; the e58/era-26
  resolvable-chain cells never reach failed attribution. The
  walk-level stub whose fixture OMITS the stream feed models an
  outside-window commit and keeps asserting None; its contract is
  restated as absence-is-silence, not unpaired-is-silence.

  (E) r51 amendment (r50 design-review F1): capture policy and
  timestamp fidelity. The capture is served with recorded commit
  timestamps end to end; synthetic stamp substitution of any kind
  disqualifies the output. Mechanically: the capture context carries
  NO snapshot-policy override, so policy resolution falls to the
  default SnapshotReadPolicyCheckpointReplay (engine/
  change_handle_policy.go:29-33,50-64), and carries NO
  VisibleStateRecoveryResources; the databranchutils.CollectChanges
  helper is expressly unsuitable here because it forces
  SnapshotReadPolicyVisibleState on every call (branch_change_handle
  .go:78,81). The hazard is concrete, not hypothetical: with the
  visible-state policy and recovery resources, the disttae dispatcher
  substitutes VisibleStateChangesHandle for the replay handle on the
  recovery error classes (disttae/change_handle.go:273-296), and that
  handle's appendDataRow stamps every emitted row with h.end
  (change_handle_visible_state.go:554) - a SUCCESSFUL capture whose
  timestamps are the window end, not the commits. Such output breaks
  both directions of (B): a pre-window hpo chain's rows still visible
  in state would surface as committed AT end (false fail-closed), and
  an in-window chain committed at T<end would surface at end, leaving
  the fold query at T unanswered (false absence). Under the default
  policy the same recovery classes are NOT substituted - the swaps
  are guarded on the policy and the resources (change_handle.go:189,
  391) - and surface to the caller as errors, which (C) fails closed
  on. Defense in depth: the capture constructor REJECTS a context
  carrying a visible-state policy or recovery resources, so a future
  caller-side policy change cannot silently reintroduce substitution;
  the fabric guard UT pins the rejection.

  r52 amendment (r51-review F1): zero-start windows. A whole-history
  collection generates a types.MinTs() lower bound (data_branch.go:
  3137-3138), and an EMPTY lower bound routes Relation.CollectChanges
  to NewCheckpointChangesHandle (disttae/change_handle.go:91-92),
  whose Next stamps every row's commit-ts column with h.end (:833) -
  synthetic output under the DEFAULT policy, invisible to the guards
  above because no policy override, resources, or error is involved.
  The capture therefore NEVER passes an IsEmpty lower bound: a
  whole-history collector window [MinTs(), end] is normalized to
  [MinTs().Next(), end] before capture. MinTs() = TS{} (types/
  txnts.go:117) is the reserved zero instant and can never be a real
  transaction commit (HLC commit timestamps have physical > 0), and
  Next() (txnts.go:130) yields (0,1), so the normalized window
  contains exactly the same real commits; the idiom matches the
  codebase's own boundary handling (windowFrom = nodeCTS.Next(),
  data_branch.go:3139; betweenFrom.Next(), :2223). Routing off the
  CheckpointChangesHandle shortcut selects the per-version changes
  progression (in-memory logtail with recorded commit ts, then the
  checkpoint RANGE recovery constructor for older persisted
  history), never the end-stamping state reader. Two obligations
  follow: the capture consumes the commit-ts values the engine's
  change currency reports per read phase, and D156(B) is a
  CONSISTENCY contract - the stream instant naming a chain's commit
  must equal the instant the same transaction's data rows carry in
  the apply's own collection, which holds by construction (one
  engine implementation serves both) and is pinned by planned case
  (9); and any window whose exact history is unservable - stale-read
  horizon (NewChangesHandler :3326-3328), recovery classes, GC-ed or
  compacted history - surfaces as an error that is classified
  INCOMPLETE before any evidence is adopted, feeding (C)'s fail-
  closed lane exactly as the r51 amendment demanded.

  r53 amendment (r52-review F1): the SHARED timestamp contract
  across BOTH readers. The fidelity rule binds every stream whose
  per-row commit instants feed PROVENANCE binding - the D156 capture
  and the apply's own data collection windows that supply the walk's
  birth/death instants (pkMoveStreamView tombstonesAt, departedBirth,
  prevDeath, the chainTS seed at data_branch_pk_move_link.go:2619)
  and the anchorArrivalVerdict tie instant. The apply reads through
  databranchutils.CollectChanges (branch_change_handle.go:76-85)
  with VisibleStateRecoveryResources attached (data_branch.go:
  2263-2266), and that reader still carries TWO synthetic-stamping
  modes the zero-start normalization does not reach: an EMPTY lower
  bound - the whole-history first window generated at
  data_branch.go:3137-3138 when buildSideCollectRange runs with
  wholeHistory=true (the no-LCA call at :2842-2856) - selects
  NewCheckpointChangesHandle (disttae/change_handle.go:91-92;
  useBoundedVisibleStateRange stays false because the apply
  attaches no ChangeRangeLimit, :105-112) whose Next const-stamps
  every row's commit-ts with h.end (:833) under the
  ChangesHandle_Snapshot hint (:798, engine/types.go:1037-1041);
  and a NONZERO window hitting a recovery class substitutes
  VisibleStateChangesHandle (nextWithSnapshotRecovery gated at
  :188-190, swaps at :273-296) whose
  appendDataRow/appendTombstoneRow stamp data AND tombstones with
  h.end (change_handle_visible_state.go:554,578) under the
  ordinary tail hint. Both modes keep their APPROVED net-effect
  replay role unchanged - output semantics, stamps, and ordering
  are not modified. The contract: a transaction's commit instant
  reported by the capture must equal the instant the same
  transaction's rows carry in every provenance-consumed window of
  the apply's data collection, and a window served by either
  synthetic mode CERTIFIES NO such instants. Mechanically the
  collector certifies each window's serving mode at three
  observable points - the empty-bound dispatch it itself performs
  (its own bounds), the Snapshot hint on received batches, and
  the recovery substitution surfaced through the apply-side
  governance this PR owns (the dataBranchVisibleStateRecovery-
  Resources attachment at data_branch.go:2263-2266; the recovery
  swap is observable at the dispatcher) - and TAINTS every
  instant-bearing extract from a synthetic window (birth instant,
  death instant, tie instant) at extraction time. Any provenance
  verdict whose binding touches tainted evidence is classified
  INCOMPLETE before adoption - never bound to h.end, never
  compared against the capture's exact T - feeding the approved
  D51/D56 unresolved lane exactly like every other incomplete
  producer in (C). Equivalently: synthetic data ranges answer
  net-effect replay only; they never answer instant queries.
  The r52 phrasing 'consistency holds by construction' is
  narrowed: it holds by construction ONLY among certified-exact
  readers (one engine implementation serves the per-version
  changes path for both), and the two synthetic modes are
  excluded by classification, not assumed away. Planned case
  (11) pins all three serving modes through the real apply and
  capture readers together.

  (F) r51 amendment (r50 design-review F2): window bounds and
  combined absence. CollectChanges serves INCLUSIVE collection
  bounds - the replay row filter accepts ts with ts.LE(end) &&
  ts.GE(start) (logtailreplay/change_handle.go:4050-4051) - and the
  apply's data collection runs per generation over the lineage
  ranges, with PICK's BETWEEN additionally intersecting each
  generation range with [betweenFrom.Next(), betweenTo]
  (data_branch.go:2218-2238). The capture therefore mirrors the EXACT
  bounds the data collection used for every relevant generation: the
  per-generation full-types.TS from/end as the collector computed
  them, inclusive at both ends, BETWEEN intersections included. A
  scope is "absent" under (B) only when its link rows appear in NONE
  of those windows AND every window's capture is certified complete
  under (C); adjacent generations may share a boundary instant, so a
  boundary commit appearing in two windows dedupes to the one true
  commit (a scope names at most one commit instant - one transaction
  commits once). Two consequences the r50 text had wrong or unwritten:
  first, a closed-open reading of the window treats a commit exactly
  AT end - which the data stream includes - as outside the capture
  and answers "absent", silently folding a chain the data stream will
  replay; second, the provider's existing pkMoveLinkTableWindow
  retains only physical timestamps (data_branch.go:2447-2452), which
  cannot express these bounds: two timestamps with equal physical and
  different logical parts are distinct commit instants with different
  boundary membership. The capture consumes the collector's
  full-type bounds directly; the physical-truncated view is never
  used to derive capture bounds (its existing probe-budget role is
  unchanged). r52: a whole-history window enters this contract in
  its normalized form per (E) - [MinTs().Next(), end] replaces
  [MinTs(), end] everywhere the capture consumes bounds, never the
  empty bound. r53: a window's instant-bearing provenance extracts
  enter every contract in this section only in certified-exact form
  per (E)'s shared rule - synthetic windows contribute net-effect
  rows to replay and never instant evidence to capture comparison,
  tie resolution, or absence certification.

  (G) r51 amendment (r50 design-review F3): enforceable resource
  bounds, admission, and cleanup ownership. A zero ChangeRangeLimit
  explicitly means UNLIMITED memory (engine/change_handle_range_limit
  .go:22-29) and the cited helper attaches none, so the r50 contract
  had no enforceable bound past "the window's link rows" - and that
  count is relation-wide, growing with unrelated tables' moves
  independently of the link-cache cap. The corrected contract: (i)
  the capture context attaches an explicit
  WithChangeRangeLimit({MaxInMemoryRows, MaxInMemoryBytes}) caller
  bound - both fields, because persisted replay rejects
  MaxInMemoryRows without MaxInMemoryBytes for variable-width columns
  - sized off the provenance cache budget (I6's budget family), so
  the capture cannot exceed the memory class the provider already
  operates under; (ii) ADMISSION to the retained index is filtered
  to the apply's own table-id set and to scopes represented in the
  provider's link cache - unrelated tables' link rows stream through
  the bounded engine materialization but are never retained, so
  retained state is bounded by RELEVANT scopes, not by K relation-
  wide; (iii) the fold is INCREMENTAL: the capture streams batches
  straight into the index and frees them, never queueing the full
  stream; (iv) ownership: the capture handle and the index belong to
  the arrival build and are released with it - a failed or cancelled
  build releases both before its lane runs, and nothing survives into
  the next generation; (v) exhausted capacity is ATOMIC and takes
  the approved D51/D56 unresolved-evidence lane: no
  partially-filled index is ever
  adopted; the provider closes the capture handle, releases capture
  and index, and disables itself with the capacity reason via the
  established NF8/I6 mechanism (disableLocked releases all caches).
  Post-disable behavior is the approved fail-closed taxonomy
  unchanged: a disabled provider cannot disprove update intent
  (byRowProbeVerdict reports complete=false,
  data_branch_pk_move_link.go:1125-1126; anyPkMoveLinkInWindow
  answers as though links exist, :970-980), so every provenance
  verdict the affected apply needs resolves UNRESOLVED and aborts
  the apply statement-atomically with parent and child rows
  unchanged - the ERROR 20101 behavior pinned today at
  data_branch_pk_move_link_test.go:2801-2806 and :3184-3195, which
  the capacity lane reuses rather than redefines, under ON UPDATE
  CASCADE and ON DELETE CASCADE alike. Legacy DELETE+INSERT replay
  remains reserved EXACTLY where D51/D56 reserve it: an
  independently proven QUIET window - fully scanned generation
  windows or the bounded existence probe answering no links in any
  provider window (D56). Capacity exhaustion never constitutes
  quiet certification: the capture blew the budget precisely
  because its content overflowed, and replaying that content as
  DELETE/INSERT would destroy destination children of genuine
  moves under ON DELETE CASCADE (the r60 F1 class). Engine ERRORS
  remain statement-fail-closed per (C)/(E). Block-level pruning by
  the link PK's leading table_id stays a possible optimization; it is
  NOT part of the correctness contract.

  r52 amendment (r51-review F2): engine-path completion for
  enforceable limits. Verified this turn: under the (E) policy the
  selected capture path reaches logtailreplay.NewChangesHandler via
  the NewPartitionStateChangesHandler alias (disttae/change_handle
  .go:44-46) for in-memory partition reads and
  NewChangesHandlerWithCheckpointRangeRecovery (:2918, delegating to
  newChangesHandlerWithCheckpointEntries) for checkpoint recovery;
  both constructors leave maxInMemoryRows/maxInMemoryBytes ZERO
  (:3323-3353 and :3102-3118), persisted prefetch consumes the
  zeros (:1320-1338 and :1554-1555), and only the partition-state-
  range family reads the ctx limit (:2988-2992 rows-requires-bytes
  validation, :3021-3022 assignment) - a family of the visible/
  snapshot camp whose synthetic stamps (E) disqualify, so no
  existing engine path satisfies exact-ts + enforced-bounds on the
  selected policy. This PR therefore completes the plumbing: the
  two selected constructors read engine.ChangeRangeLimitFromContext
  (ctx) with the IDENTICAL validation and assignment contract as
  (:2988-2992, :3021-3022). The change is pure opt-in: an
  unattached context leaves both fields zero, which the engine API
  defines as unbounded-preserving-existing-callers
  (engine/change_handle_range_limit.go:22-29), so every
  pre-existing caller's behavior is byte-identical and only the
  D156 capture attaches a non-zero bound. Alternatives weighed and
  rejected: consumer-side accounting alone (bounds must act at the
  engine read, BEFORE the provider's admission filter, which is
  exactly where persisted prefetch materializes variable-width
  rows); routing through the visible-state range constructor
  (synthetic net-effect stamps, (E)); attaching spill ownership
  (the index is tiny relative to data and spill adds a cleanup
  surface with no correctness gain). Capacity classification: an
  exhausted bound surfaces a CAPACITY-class error (cf. the bounded
  range replay's memory-limit error, logtailreplay/change_handle
  .go:2322-2325), the provider closes the capture handle BEFORE the
  NF8/I6 atomic provider-disable lane runs, and no partial index
  state is adopted; a limit-misconfiguration (rows without bytes)
  fails at construction under the shared validation - a programming
  error, statement-fail-closed. Cleanup ownership is otherwise as
  (iv): capture handle and index released with the arrival build.
  Post-disable apply behavior is defined by (v) as corrected in
  r53 - the D51/D56 unresolved-abort lane, never legacy replay of a
  possible move.

  r53 amendment (r52-review F2): bound enforcement through
  RESULT-BATCH ASSEMBLY and the combined live working set. Verified
  this turn: the reads above bound only PERSISTED PREFETCH windows;
  the assembled output is unbounded by the attached fields alone -
  CNObjectHandle.Next unions each prefetched window whole into the
  caller's destination batch (:1450-1463), quickNext iterates
  windows until EOF or coarseMaxRow (:3453-3493; quick mode holds
  whenever either handle is empty, decideMode :3407-3420), and the
  non-quick Next terminates only against coarseMaxRow*2 and
  coarseMaxRow (:3743-3764, with coarseMaxRow = objectio.
  BlockMaxRows on both selected dispatch arms,
  disttae/change_handle.go:433-434/:518-519). A 20-row persisted
  insert window under an attached MaxInMemoryRows=8 assembles one
  20-row result batch, and wide windows pass the byte budget the
  same way - before any provider admission. The completed
  constructors therefore charge the attached row AND byte budgets
  through assembly: every union append into the accumulating
  data/tombstone destination and every batch the Next loops emit
  is accounted against the attached fields, covering the combined
  live working set - the prefetch window cache, the in-memory
  aobj/in-memory buffers, and both destination batches together.
  Exceeding the attached budget at ANY accounting point surfaces
  the same capacity-class error classified by (v) - never an
  over-budget result batch, never silent spill (no spill ownership
  is attached, unchanged), never truncation of the stream. The
  Close path on that error releases the prefetch cache and both
  handles before the provider's (v) lane runs (CNObjectHandle.
  Close :1471-1478, ChangeHandler.Close per constructor guard),
  so bounded peak and full release are the same event. Timestamp
  semantics are preserved by construction: enforcement is pure
  memory accounting - emitted rows, order, hint progression, and
  recorded commit stamps are byte-identical to the unbudgeted
  read - and unattached contexts (both fields zero) keep every
  existing caller byte-identical. Alternatives weighed and
  rejected: assembly-time spilling under this PR's ownership (the
  provenance capture must fail loudly; adding a disk surface buys
  cleanup surface for no correctness gain - the bounded family's
  spill remains that family's own opt-in), consumer-side
  accounting alone (persisted prefetch materializes variable-
  width rows before admission, which is exactly the memory the
  limit exists to bound), and bounded-batch emission without a
  total cap (it would let an unbounded relation-wide stream
  through the completed constructors, defeating (i)'s memory-
  class promise; retained state is bounded by admission but the
  engine materialization itself is what the attached bound
  governs). Planned case (12) exercises the multi-window and
  wide-row shapes through the COMPLETE default-policy handles.

  Planned validation (execute with the implementation turn, cheapest
  first): (1) feed fabric UTs - scope present names exactly the
  recorded commit instant; scope absent names nothing; corrupt or
  truncated feed poisons the build's unfailed queries (RED pre-fix: no
  feed exists). (2) Walk-level UT pair - the r60 counterexample at
  walk level (truncated foreign arrival, in-window commit evidenced
  only by a pre-window-born victim's death, origin outside the PICK
  closure) answers Unresolved, while its hpo twin (identical unpaired
  shape, scope absent from the feed) answers Recorded/fold; the r59
  tail mirror stays green. (3) Live RED->GREEN at the review's exact
  rows: current binary folds (child 10 cascaded onto B, no ERROR
  20101); fixed binary aborts PICK KEYS(1) statement-atomically with
  parents (1,'A'),(3,'B') and children (10,1),(30,3) unchanged, and
  the hpo merge control cascades to (42,'edited')/(900,42). (4) PICK
  regression cell appended to pick_foreign_key_pk_move.sql/.result
  asserting atomic rejection and unchanged rows. (5) Full frontend
  bank, rebuild, six-fixture run-mode replay to catch any
  over-poisoning regression. (6) Producer-to-provider timestamp
  fidelity (r50 review F1): a chain committed at T strictly inside
  the capture window surfaces with ts EXACTLY T (never end, never
  substituted); a window whose needed history is compacted away
  surfaces the recovery class as a capture ERROR and the build
  fails closed; a restart between production and capture preserves
  exact timestamps; the constructor guards reject a ctx carrying a
  visible-state policy or recovery resources. (7) Boundary cases
  (r50 review F2): commits exactly AT from and exactly AT end are
  captured (inclusive); for PICK BETWEEN a commit at
  betweenFrom.Next()-1 is outside the capture while betweenTo
  itself is inside; a pair with equal physical and different
  logical parts straddling the bound resolves by full-types.TS
  comparison; each case is authored RED against the physical-only
  closed-open reading where that reading would answer differently.
  (8) Resource cases (r50 review F3): with row and byte limits
  lowered to expose exhaustion, a window carrying more link
  rows/bytes - variable-width pk payloads and unrelated-table move
  history included - drives the atomic I6-lane provider-disable
  with zero partial index adoption and full release of capture and
  index memory; retained state stays bounded by admitted scopes in
  every case. (9) Zero-start fidelity (r51 review F1): a REAL
  whole-history case - the collector window is literally
  [MinTs(), end] and a producer chain commits at T<end; assert the
  capture (normalized to [MinTs().Next(), end]) reports the same
  commit instant the apply's own data collection records for rows
  of the SAME transaction, and never h.end or any substituted
  stamp; plus an unservable exact window (stale-read horizon)
  classified incomplete before evidence adoption. (10) Engine
  bound enforcement on the selected path (r51 review F2): real
  persisted reads through the completed default-policy
  constructors - checkpoint recovery and in-memory, variable-width
  rows, unrelated-table history flushed to persisted objects -
  under a tiny attached limit assert a capacity-class error at the
  ENGINE read before any provider admission; a retry with a one
  notch larger limit captures the same window; an unattached ctx
  keeps the pre-existing unbounded behavior pinned; and rows-
  without-bytes fails at construction. (11) Shared-timestamp
  joint-reader cases (r52-review F1): a chain commits at T inside
  a per-version window - assert the D156 capture AND the apply's
  own data collection report the SAME recorded instant T for
  rows of the SAME transaction (never end); a whole-history
  no-LCA window - the capture runs normalized [MinTs().Next(),
  end] while the apply's first window rides the checkpoint state
  reader - asserts a recorded move inside the state window fails
  its needed verdict closed (statement-atomic abort, unchanged
  rows) while the certified-quiet control replays green; a
  visible-state recovery window asserts recovered end-stamps
  never bind a provenance verdict (synthetic extracts tainted,
  verdict incomplete, abort lane; replay rows unaffected).
  (12) Assembly-bound and abort-lane cases (r52-review F2/F3):
  multi-window variable-width reads through the COMPLETE
  default-policy handles (both constructors, in-memory plus
  checkpoint RANGE recovery with persisted objects) - the 20
  persisted insert rows under an attached rows=8 limit surface
  the capacity-class error DURING ASSEMBLY (never a 20-row
  result batch), live prefetch windows stay bounded, Close
  releases everything; wide rows under a byte budget likewise;
  a one-notch-larger retry captures all rows with exact stamps;
  and lowered-limit live MERGE and PICK with a genuine recorded
  move in-window assert statement rejection (ERROR 20101 family)
  with parent AND child rows unchanged - under a destination
  child declaring ON UPDATE CASCADE and again under a child
  declaring ON DELETE CASCADE - while the certified-quiet
  control (no recorded moves under the same lowered limits)
  replays green, pinning the D56 lane.
- D157 (r50, design answer to r60 review F2 (P2), refines the
  evidence-construction cost contract accompanying D156): arrival-build
  evidence construction is one pass per provider generation, and every
  evidence loop observes cancellation. F2's blowup was structural:
  failedArrivalCommitsLocked memoizes per scope, but the code-level
  scan re-walked every cached link per DISTINCT scope - M failed scopes
  times N cached links, all under p.mu with no ctx check. D156's
  scope->commit index is built ONCE per arrival build by a single
  streaming pass over the window's link rows (O(K)); each failed-scope
  query is a hash lookup. The matching lanes the review asked to
  preserve are preserved by exactness: the index names the exact
  superset of what both approximation channels named, with the same
  accept/reject outcomes on every previously-proven fixture.
  ensureArrivalIndexLocked's per-cached-landing attribution stays a
  single per-build pass (per-build O(N) once, not per scope). (A)
  Cancellation: the stream capture checks ctx at batch boundaries and
  every arrival-build loop (per-key walk, index fold, failed-scope
  attribution) checks ctx at iteration boundaries; a cancelled build
  aborts the apply statement fail-safe and adopts NO partial verdict
  state - the provider generation boundary already guarantees a later
  retry rebuilds wholesale. (B) Deterministic operation-count
  coverage: the provider's existing probe counter (arrivalScans, the
  walk instrumentation F2 cited) is asserted in a fabric UT with M
  distinct failed scopes over N links - post-fix the failed-scope
  attribution performs M index lookups and ZERO per-scope link walks,
  so the counter is constant in M (RED pre-fix: the counter scales
  MxN). A cancellation UT cancels mid-capture and mid-walk and
  asserts error-not-hang plus no partial index adoption.

  Planned validation (execute with the implementation turn): the
  operation-count UT, the cancellation UT, and reuse of D156's live
  and replay evidence for behavior identity.

  r51 amendment: the cost contract now has two bounded terms -
  engine replay materialization under the explicit ChangeRangeLimit
  (D156(G)(i)) and retained index state bounded by ADMITTED scopes
  (D156(G)(ii)) - and the deterministic coverage extends to
  admission and release: the op-count UT additionally asserts
  retained rows/state stay within lowered limits with unrelated-
  table history present, and the cancellation UT asserts capture
  and index memory are released on cancel before the fail-safe
  return.

Open questions (non-blocking, owned):


- D158 (r54, round-4 review F1 (P1), refines D102): one member,
  two identities - the coverage contract matches the OWNER's logical
  identity, never the link's physical address. The round-4 premise
  was verified at every cited locus and reproduced live on the
  era-70 binary (/tmp/e71_probe_identity.log,
  /tmp/e71_probe_funnel2.log): table-level CREATE SNAPSHOT and PITR
  record obj_id from getSqlForCheckDatabaseTable, which selects
  rel_logical_id (authenticate.go:2169; snapshot.go's
  SNAPSHOTLEVELTABLE getTableIdFunc; pitr.go:583), and copy ALTER
  creates a new physical relation while WithKeepLogicalId carries
  the old logical id (alter.go:1196 -> sql_executor.go:457 ->
  disttae/txn_database.go:394-404). (A) Identities. The PHYSICAL
  LINK-ADDRESS identity is the producing/absorbing incarnation's
  rel_id; it stays the address key across the link catalog
  (pkMoveLinkID embeds it), closure windows, arrival/capture state,
  and the retention-ledger keyspace, because it names the physical
  relation whose committed change stream produced the moves - the
  correlation the engine-side readers require. The LOGICAL OWNER
  identity is rel_logical_id, durable across copy ALTER and RENAME;
  it is the base's only table-object identity for snapshots, PITR,
  and grants (authenticate.go:1449/:1508 joins), so it is the one
  identity the OWNERSHIP question (does any owner still ground this
  member's provenance?) can be answered in. (B) Persist-before-
  disappearance: every retention-ledger identity record carries the
  owner's logical id from the moment the ledger row exists,
  captured at link-row genesis from the writer relation's catalog
  definition and refreshed whenever a funnel touches a live
  relation's ledger row while its catalog row is still readable -
  after DROP the mapping is unrecoverable (the coverage layer
  receives a row set, not a catalog). The link catalog's own
  10-column shape is unchanged: the durable mapping lives in the
  retention ledger, the single store all funnels already consult.
  r55 amendment: D159 pins the genesis-admission protocol, the
  failure/concurrency policy, the live-row lifecycle, and the
  reachable refresh sites that make this capture durable
  end-to-end; D160 pins the storage column, encoding, marker,
  and schema compatibility boundary. (C) One shared coverage
  contract: PkMoveLocalSnapshotCoversTable,
  PkMovePitrCoversTable and every funnel caller (branch-DAG reclaim
  ddl.go:5116, drop-lifecycle ddl.go:5281/:5604, owner-removal reap
  data_branch_link_retention.go:311) feed one row shape (physical
  id, logical id, names) into one predicate whose table-level match
  is obj_id == the member's LOGICAL id, with the name predicate kept
  as fallback; rows whose logical id was never persisted (pre-r54
  in-build rows or identity-unresolved writes) fall back to the
  legacy physical compare plus name and stay fail-ALIVE (kept) on
  any ambiguity - the established MemberIdentityUnresolved lane -
  and the int64 defensive fallback for pre-v4_0_8 decoders is
  retained. (D) Reclamation after the final owner disappears keeps
  its approved effect and gains the correct identity: a member's
  links retire when no live relation, snapshot, or PITR grounds its
  logical identity - post-ALTER and renamed members stay covered
  while any owner exists and retire exactly when the last owner
  retires, never merely because an incarnation changed. (E)
  Untouched: link addressing, producer/apply recording semantics,
  folding, admission and cancellation (D156/D157), and the §9.2
  privilege surface; the change is confined to the retention-ledger
  record, the coverage predicate, and its callers.
- D159 (r55, round-5 review F1 (P2), refines D153/D158(B)): the
  genesis-admission lifecycle of the retention ledger. D158(B)
  demands the owner identity persisted from the moment the address
  exists; D153 admitted rows only at funnel KEEP verdicts, bounded
  candidates by retained-dead-table count, and protected uncovered
  rows only through the descendant walk - none of which answers
  how a LIVE link address registers, survives an unrelated owner
  removal, or fails.
  (A) Writer site and atomicity: genesis rides the producer
  transaction itself. The multi_update link recorder stages one link
  row per moved row inside the recording transaction
  (pkg/sql/colexec/multi_update/pk_move_link.go:250
  insertUpdatePkMoveLinkRows, flushed through the actionPkMoveLink
  tail UpdateFlushS3Info); the same staging path attaches at most
  one identity row per distinct address per transaction, keyed by
  table_id, carrying database/table names and rel_logical_id from
  the writer relation's catalog definition (the update pipeline
  already names that relation; where the logical id is absent from
  its descriptor, one keyed mo_tables read inside the same
  transaction supplies it, and that read is charged in (F)). One
  transaction carries both writes, so genesis is atomic and
  rollback-symmetric BY CONSTRUCTION: a rolled-back move leaves no
  link row and no ledger row; a crash mid-statement leaves no
  uncommitted residue (staging dies with the transaction), and a
  committed pair is durable across restart - the F1 restart case. r97 amendment (D218(A.8)):
  genesis admission gains the ACTUAL-MOVE gate - the staging
  path attaches the identity row ONLY when the triggering link
  batch carries a real moved-address link row (old pk bytes
  != new pk bytes); continuity-only batches (the r26-F5
  markers, whose emission, carriage and txn-local consumption
  stand unchanged) stage nothing; the identity-row-first
  ordering above and the positional-cut rollback symmetry
  apply to move-carrying statements.
  (B) Idempotency and concurrent first writers: the recorder's
  txn-private map dedups within the transaction; on first touch of
  an address it runs one keyed probe and inserts only when absent,
  so exactly one row per (account, table_id) ever exists under the
  primary key. Two concurrent first writers on one address build
  IDENTICAL content - names and logical id derive from the same
  catalog definition, so the writes are commutative - and the
  race resolves by the platform's ordinary duplicate-key /
  write-write conflict rule: the loser aborts statement-
  atomically, its client retries, and the retry's probe finds the
  committed row and skips the insert. Outcome: exactly one row,
  stable identity, no wedge, behavior identical to any duplicate-
  key race on an ordinary table. r56 amendment (D161(B)): the
  dedup map is OWNED by the transaction's pk-move staged state,
  PUBLISHED nowhere beyond the owning transaction (consulted only
  by the same transaction's recorder; discarded at commit or
  rollback), and JOURNALED per statement: a statement rollback
  truncates the staged identity row with the positional writes
  cut (pkg/vm/engine/disttae/types.go:1887-1894) and undoes that
  statement's map entries through the same pass that restores the
  other provenance side effects the cut cannot reach

  pkg/vm/engine/disttae/pk_move_link_fixup.go:2055-2082), so a
  registering statement that rolls back leaves no trace and a

  both link and ledger rows. r57 amendment (D163(A)/(B)):
  first touch means first touch of a registration EPOCH - a
  prune cancellation (D161(A.1)) ends the epoch by destroying
  the staged row AND this map entry in one journaled step, so
  the map never outlives its staged row and a later
  same-transaction move on that address takes this ordinary
  first-touch path again; statement rollback of the cancelling
  statement resurrects both halves from the same journal
  segment. r58 amendment (D165(A)): the first-touch probe
  resolves into one of TWO map states - OWNED (probe absent:

  registration already covers the address; nothing is
  inserted, and the entry stands as a READ-ONLY memo of that
  committed row's existence). Both states dedup repeat
  touches within the epoch; D165 defines their cancellation,
  rollback, and cost rules.
  (C) Failure policy: genesis registration is MANDATORY, so a
  genuine write error (anything beyond the two capability gates)

  r56 amendment (D161(A)): the
  invariant now reads exactly - SURVIVING-LINK TRACKING with ONE
  named residue class (probe-error writes and pre-r56 admitted

- D161 (r56, round-6 review F1+F2 (P2), refines D159(A)/(B)/
  (E)/(F)): ledger lifetime and registration-state correctness.
  (A) Contract: the ledger tracks SURVIVING LINKS exactly -
  never a broader address history - with ONE named residue
  class (probe-error writes and pre-r56 admitted link-free rows;
  the owner-removal reap retires residue with their possibly
  empty link sets, uncovered -> paired delete, so residue dies
  at the first owner removal that does not ground it). Two
  enforcement rules:
  (A.1) Genesis pruning: pruneDeadPkMoveLinkRowsLocked
  (pkg/vm/engine/disttae/pk_move_link_fixup.go:4056-4074) runs
  at the top of every IncrStatementID and once at commit
  (txn.go:3790-3796) and can retire every staged link of a
  first-touch address when the moving transaction deletes the
  replacement before commit. The staged identity row shadows
  the staged links: when the prune drops the LAST staged link
  of an address whose registration was staged by THIS
  transaction AND no committed link row for that address
  exists, the prune also cancels the staged registration.
  Addresses holding committed links keep the registration (the
  invariant WANTS a row for an address that still has surviving
  links), and a registration staged by another transaction is
  never touched (txn-private staging is unforgeable while
  uncommitted; a concurrent first writer's own registration
  carries the same commutative identity). The cancellation is
  journaled like the link-cell deaths it shadows and is
  reversed by the same statement-rollback undo if the
  cancelling statement rolls back; commit discards the journal.
  The at-staging probe records the two facts the cancellation
  needs - committed ledger row absent, committed link presence
  (one keyed read mirroring pkMoveLinkPresenceProbe,
  pkg/sql/compile/pk_move_link_retention.go:166-169) - charged
  to D159(F). r57 amendments: D163(A) makes the cancellation a
  transition of ONE registration state that also destroys the
  dedup-map entry in the same journaled step (re-admission is
  a new epoch's ordinary first touch; rollback symmetry holds
  for both halves), and D164(A) keeps the staged identity row
  in memory through every mid-transaction boundary dump by
  BOUNDED RETENTION UNTIL FINAL PRUNING - the prune is an
  in-memory shrink that skips nil-batch entries
  (pk_move_link_fixup.go:4056-4074), so the row this rule
  cancels must never spill on a !dumpAll pass; the commit dump
  (dumpAll) flushes only rows that survive the final prune.
  (A.2) Funnel presence gating: EVERY KEEP-lane ledger upsert
  is gated on link presence, reusing the lineage lane's rule
  (pkg/sql/compile/ddl.go:6051-6057): probe present -> upsert
  per D159(E); probe ERROR -> upsert as the bounded residue
  class (fail-ALIVE; the lineage lane's rationale is adopted
  verbatim - a false miss strands the one record reaps can
  trust, a false extra row is bounded residue the same reaps
  retire); probe ABSENT -> NO ledger action: a table retiring
  with zero links leaves no ledger row. This closes the
  unbranched KEEP lanes' unconditional admission
  (reclaimUnbranchedDropPkMoveLinks, ddl.go:5590-5619 with its
  :5612/:5616 writes, invoked for every non-lineage drop at
  ddl.go:6041).
  (A.3) Restated invariant and bound: |ledger| = |distinct
  addresses with surviving link rows| + |bounded probe-error
  residue|; D159(F)'s candidate/cost bound gains the
  presence/committed-link keyed reads (per first-touch staging
  and per funnel contact, never per row), amortized as
  (A.1)/(A.2) state.
  (A.4) Validation - case (14) additions: move-then-delete in
  one transaction on a fresh address commits ZERO links and

  probe-error twin writes bounded residue a later owner removal
  retires; a covered member whose last links retire loses its
  row in the same transaction (paired delete, D159(E)).
  (B) Registration dedup-map correctness (round-6 F2): the
  map's OWNER is the transaction's pk-move staged state; its

- D162 (r56, round-6 review F3 (P2), refines D160(B)/(E)/(F)):

  its verdict never outlives the read. (B) Writers derive the
  shape per contact the same way: the genesis keyed dedup probe
  runs wide-first and its success-or-signal doubles as the
  recording transaction's capability verdict FOR THAT
  TRANSACTION ONLY (a memo ending at the transaction boundary);
  funnel contacts probe per invocation; nothing else is cached.
  (C) Account-scopedness is by construction: every probe
  executes under the target account's attached context, so

- D167 (r59, round-9 review F1 (P2), refines D165(C) and

  and inherits the enclosing statement's attribution
  (WithDisableIncrStatement, compile.go:11316-11317). So ONE
  transaction can hold an EXTERNAL memo or an OWNED

  deletes X's committed or staged ledger row, and no

  conflicts with itself. D165(B)'s memo dedup then skips
  re-registration, committing a later surviving link without
  its mandatory ledger identity - the review's
  counterexample, confirmed shape-valid at every cited
  locus.
  (B) The RETIRE transition: every paired-delete caller
  listed in D159(E) - ddl.go:5130/:5192/:5619/:5635 and the
  frontend owner-removal reap
  (data_branch_link_retention.go:359-362) - performs, for
  each retired address X and in the SAME journaled step as
  its paired deletes: OWNED -> ABSENT (the paired delete
  already kills the staged row it can see in the caller's
  workspace; the map entry AND the D166 genesis-batch
  membership die in the retiring statement's journal
  segment) and EXTERNAL -> ABSENT (the memo is invalidated;
  the committed row's deletion is the paired delete's own
  same-statement work). ABSENT stays ABSENT. Because the
  deletes run under WithDisableIncrStatement inside the
  enclosing user statement, the journal segment belongs to
  that statement exactly like the D163 cancellation
  segments; background reap transactions carry no
  registration state, so the transition is a uniform no-op
  there (map miss) and the caller rule stays total.
  (C) Subsequent moves = NEW EPOCH: the next touch of X is
  an ordinary first touch: the keyed probe, executed inside
  the same transaction, observes the ledger row DELETED
  (own-transaction deletes are visible to own-transaction
  reads), resolves ABSENT -> OWNED, and re-stages the
  registration and membership. The D165(E)/D163(C) bounds
