  transaction's statements; at most one live staged row per
  address exists at any instant; the mandatory-identity
  invariant is restored at the re-registration, so no
  surviving link can commit without its ledger row.
  (D) Rollback symmetry: statement rollback of the retiring
  statement restores everything in ONE locked pass from the

  next touch after the rollback dedups against the restored

- D168 (r60, round-10 review F1 (P2), refines D165(A)/(B)/
  (C)/(E) and the D159(E) paired-delete callers):
  registration use and retirement share one serialization
  protocol, so the link/ledger identity invariant holds for
  every successful interleaving of a registration-using
  transaction and a retiring transaction.
  (A) The gap (verified r60 at the cited loci): r59's
  D165(C) and D167(H) assumed another transaction's
  retirement necessarily write-write conflicts with this
  transaction's staged links. It does not: the link
  producer writes with a raw engine.Relation.Write
  (pk_move_link.go:271-272, the source resolved by
  resolvePkMoveLinkSource, pk_move_link.go:61-64); the
  retirement sweep selects and deletes SNAPSHOT-VISIBLE
  committed rows (ddl.go:5150-5192), which need not include
  the other transaction's new link keys; the delete's lock
  acquisition covers only the returned keys for small
  batches (lockop/fetch.go:768-774 and :810-819, per-key
  lock.Granularity_Row); and an EXTERNAL memo neither
  writes nor locks the memoized ledger row. With no shared
  key ever locked on both sides, T1 (probe HIT -> EXTERNAL,
  stages links) and T2 (retires the address's committed
  links and ledger row) can both commit, leaving T1's
  surviving links without their mandatory ledger identity
  row - the review's two-session counterexample.
  (B) The protocol - two serialized sides over ONE shared
  resource, the ledger row's primary key.
  EXTERNAL-resolution side: the D165(A) probe that HITS is
  a LOCKING probe - it acquires a SHARED-mode row lock
  (pb.LockMode_Shared; the lock service implements shared
  and exclusive modes, verified at
  pkg/lockservice/lock_table_local.go and its remote/proxy
  test family) on the hit row's key, held until the
  transaction ends (commit or rollback releases it).
  Registration readers neither write nor delete the row, so
  shared mode suffices and concurrent EXTERNAL resolutions
  of one address do not serialize against each other.
  Retirement side: every D159(E) paired-delete caller
  performs each address's retirement as ONE serialized
  critical section - (i) acquire the EXCLUSIVE row lock
  (pb.LockMode_Exclusive) on the address's ledger-row key
  FIRST; (ii) under that lock re-probe the address's link
  presence at the locked/current committed view (observing
  everything committed up to the lock grant); (iii) compute
  the final delete set from THAT view - every link row the
  locked view shows, plus the ledger row; (iv) execute the
  paired delete of exactly that set. Recomputing the delete
  set at the serialized view is what closes the hole: links
  committed by a just-released EXTERNAL lock-holder are
  visible to the retirer's locked re-probe and die together
  with the ledger row - no surviving link ever loses its
  identity row. r61 amendment (D170), refined r62 (D172),
  refined r63 (D173), refined r64 (D174): the
  'locked/current committed view'
  obligation above is DELIVERED by D173(B)'s
  causal-frontier advance (the exclusive grant's own
  result.Timestamp as the fence, WaitLogTailAppliedAt,
  UpdateSnapshot - never a local clock sample) with the
  fence first passing D174(B.2)'s generation-checked
  acceptance (a committed fencing transaction on the
  current binding makes the frontier valid across
  binding generations) followed
  by D170(B)(3)'s fresh-internal-statement re-probe, not
  by the lock op's conditional snapshot advance - verified
  r61/r62 to be absent for exactly this call shape
  (uncontended grant over an unchanged ledger row, and
  the changed-gate never covers the link table's keys);
  steps (i)-(iv) above stand with (ii) and (iii) executed
  per D173(B) + D170(B).
  (C) Schedules (deterministic two-session cases; the
  invariant = an address has surviving links <=> it has a
  ledger row):
  (C.1) retire-before-writer-commit: T1 probes (HIT, takes
  the shared lock), records EXTERNAL, stages links; T2's
  retirement reaches the address and BLOCKS on T1's shared
  lock; T1 commits - its links AND the still-present,
  never-deleted ledger row commit together (invariant holds
  at T1's commit); T2's lock grant follows, its locked
  re-probe sees T1's committed links, and the recomputed
  delete set covers them together with the ledger row -
  final state ZERO links AND ZERO ledger rows for the
  address (invariant holds at T2's commit).
  (C.2) writer-commit-before-retire: T1 commits first; T2's
  sweep selects at its own snapshot, which already contains
  T1's committed links - they enter the delete set from the
  start - final state ZERO links AND ZERO ledger rows.
  r61: this schedule places the writer's commit INSIDE the
  retirement snapshot; the complementary stale-snapshot,
  uncontended-grant schedule that an in-snapshot selection
  cannot discriminate is (C.6) in D170(H).
  (C.3) abort twin: the (C.1) shape with T1 ABORTING while
  T2 waits - the lock releases with nothing committed; T2's

  (C.4) concurrent EXTERNAL writers on one address: two

  the critical section exists pre-fix).
  (D) Conflict and retry behavior: a blocked retirement
  waits under the lock service's ordinary policy; a
  lock-wait timeout or deadlock-detect victimization
  surfaces as an ordinary statement error on the retiring
  statement, which the existing D165(D)-family statement
  retry re-runs under its fresh snapshot - the retried
  sweep re-selects and re-serializes per (B), converging to
  one of the (C) outcomes; no new error class is
  introduced, and the funnel's benign-WARN posture for
  probe ERRORS is unchanged (a lock conflict is a wait or
  abort, never a WARN swallow). A locking probe that waits
  past a retirement's commit re-reads at the grant: the row

  stages the identity row, exactly the new-epoch
  re-registration the invariant needs; an EXTERNAL memo
  never materializes against a deleted row.

  r61 amendment (D171): the second sentence of this

  (E) The OWNED lane needs no registration lock: an OWNED

  (F) Cost: folded into D165(E)'s amended bound - one
  shared row-lock acquisition per EXTERNAL resolution per
  epoch on the producer side; one exclusive row-lock
  acquisition plus one locked re-probe per retired address
  on the retiring side, amortized over the statement's
  existing per-address work; totals unchanged in order:
  O(addresses x epochs) producer-side and O(retired
  addresses) retirement-side. r64 amendment (D174(G)): add

  retired address - same order; the EXTERNAL probe's

  the proxy feature existed.
  (G) Rejected alternatives (recorded): (G.1) validation

- D169 (r60, round-10 review F2 (P2), refines D159(E),
  D166(A), and the D163(A)/D165(A) transition sets): a
  KEEP/enrichment refresh of a present ledger row whose
  address is TRACKED in the refreshing transaction PRESERVES
  ownership of the registration instead of replacing it with
  an unowned funnel batch.
  (A) The gap (verified r60 at the cited loci): D159(E)
  requires present rows to be refreshed on KEEP contacts;
  the refresh executes as a native SQL UPDATE
  (insertPkMoveLinkRetention's enrichment lane,
  pk_move_link_retention.go:99-117), which is a delete of
  the old row plus an insert of the replacement
  (multi_update.go:577-591); and D166(A) excludes EVERY
  funnel refresh batch from genesis ownership and lane
  retention. One transaction can therefore: move a p key
  (OWNED staged genesis row, cancelable in memory per
  D161/D164), DROP the last branch under a grounding
  snapshot (the KEEP refresh deletes the OWNED genesis row
  and stages its replacement as an UNOWNED funnel batch),
  force a boundary dump (the unowned batch is not
  lane-admitted and may spill beyond the in-memory
  cancellation D161/D164 require), then delete the moved
  replacement - the D161(A.1) prune cancellation destroys
  the OWNED entry's already-dead genesis batch while the
  live refreshed ledger row commits with ZERO links: a
  linkless ledger row outside the D161-named probe-error
  residue class, with the map entry and the D166 membership
  still pointing at the killed batch. D167 governs deletes
  only and explicitly left the refresh lanes untouched, so
  no ownership-transfer transition existed.
  (B) The transition: a refresh whose target address is
  TRACKED (the refreshing transaction holds an
  OWNED/EXTERNAL D165(A) entry for it) performs a journaled
  REFRESH transition in the refreshing statement's D161(B)
  journal segment, in the same step as the refresh's
  delete+insert: the killed owned batch's D166 membership
  dies; the replacement refresh batch is REGISTERED as the
  address's owned entry (ownership TRANSFER); and the map
  state is OWNED thereafter - an OWNED entry keeps its
  state with the entry rebound to the replacement batch,
  while an EXTERNAL memo converts to OWNED with the memo
  invalidated (this transaction staged the replacement row,
  so it now owns the live row and with it cancel
  authority). Cancellation, rollback, and lane admission
  all follow the transferred entry: D161(A.1) prune
  cancellation destroys the LIVE replacement batch in
  memory, and D166(A)'s conjunction admits it to the lane
  as the one transaction-owned entry for the address.
  (C) Untracked addresses are untouched: a refresh whose
  target address has no registration state in the
  refreshing transaction stays the plain unowned funnel
  upsert - nothing registers, nothing joins the lane, and
  the row's lifecycle remains the D159(E) paired delete's;
  the lane retains NO unrelated funnel batches (the D166(B)
  budget rejection stands).
  (D) Rollback symmetry: statement rollback of the
  refreshing statement undoes the refresh's delete+insert
  ordinarily and restores the prior map state and
  membership from the same journal segment in one locked
  pass - an OWNED-prior refresh restores the original
  genesis batch's membership and entry, an EXTERNAL-prior
  refresh restores the memo (valid again precisely because
  the committed row is back), and the replacement batch's
  registration dies with the segment.
  (E) Cost and bounds: O(1) journal operations per
  tracked-address refresh - one membership death plus one
  membership registration, no new probes; the lane's bound
  gains at most one batch per tracked refreshed address,
  still O(addresses the transaction tracks), so the D164(D)
  domination argument stands unchanged.
  (F) Rejected alternatives (recorded): (F.1) mutating the
  tracked row in place is rejected - workspace entries are
  append-only staged batches and the dump format has no
  in-place update, so a refresh physically IS delete plus
  insert and the metadata must move to the replacement.
  (F.2) suppressing the refresh on tracked rows is rejected
  - the D159(E) enrichment duty (an empty-named row gaining
  names and logical id) must still fire. (F.3) admitting
  ALL funnel refresh batches to the lane is rejected - it
  reopens the unbounded-retention surface D166(B) rejected;
  the transfer registers exactly one batch per tracked
  refreshed address. (F.4) registering the replacement
  WITHOUT killing the genesis membership is rejected - it
  would hold two memberships per address and leave the dead
  batch's membership forever unmatched.
  (G) Validation - case (14) additions: (G.1) the demanded
  cell - OWNED registration -> grounded KEEP refresh ->
  forced dump (fixture plus the fj/cn/workspace_force_flush

  live replacement batch stays cancelable in memory through
  the dump and the prune cancellation destroys it - COMMIT
  holds ZERO links AND ZERO ledger rows for the address.
  (G.2) the refresh-rollback twin: the (G.1) shape with
  ROLLBACK of the refreshing statement - deletes and
  membership restored and the original genesis batch live
  again; the later last-link deletion cancels it - COMMIT
  holds ZERO links AND ZERO ledger rows. (G.3) the ordinary
  unowned-funnel control: the same schedule on an address
  the refreshing transaction never touched - no transfer
  occurs and the refresh batch is never lane-admitted (the
  r57 name-only predicate WOULD have retained it - asserted
  as the control), with the invariant still resolving
  through the ordinary paths. (G.4) negative control: the
  (G.1) schedule WITHOUT the transfer - the refreshed
  ledger row commits after the last link's prune with ZERO
  links - the r59 shape; RED pre-fix by construction (no
  transfer exists pre-fix).
- D170 (r61, round-11 review F1 (P2), refines D168(B)/(C)/
  (D) and D165(B)): the post-lock visibility that the

  (A) The gap (verified r61 at the cited loci): the

  admission lock on the ADDRESS's ledger key, and (B.2) (:8425-8439)

  DROP's retirement in ONE caller transaction: the D165(B) shared
  probe lock and the OWNED insert's own row lock are held to

  WithTxn(c.proc.GetTxnOperator()) + WithDisableIncrStatement). T_f's
  exclusive request then waits behind the caller's own held lock while
  the caller waits synchronously for T_f's commit - a cross-session
  wait the lock-level deadlock detector has no edge for - so every
  caller-held-key retirement decays to a lock-wait-timeout failure and
  never to the promised success or bounded retry, and the in-place

  ordinary pessimistic RC transaction ON THAT CN. An RC commit

  logtail is armed on the grant - the planned GREEN schedule

- D187 (r77, 2026-10-26): PER-ROUND OWNER TOKEN AND
  PRE-INVOCATION TERMINAL-OWNERSHIP SELECTION FOR THE T_f1
  OWNER (round-27 design review F1+F2 (P2, both against
  D186(B.2)'s T_f1 ownership mechanics); refines
  D186(B.2)(i)/(ii)/(iii) and re-proves (C.23) ONLY;
  D186(B.1)/(B.3)/(B.4)/(B.5) and every earlier decision
  stand, noted in place; D165(C) remains absolute).
  (A) Verified gaps (each re-verified at the cited loci
  before editing):
  (A.1) F1 - THE RECORDED ROUND IDENTITY IS BINDING-SCOPED,
  NOT ROUND-SCOPED: D186(B.2)(ii) (r76 :12805-12810)
  specifies the owner identity as the address's account
  plus the generation contract Table/ServiceID/Version of
  the generation-checked grant, but that triple identifies
  the ledger BINDING, not a round: AcquireScratchGrant
  locks the scratch key on the lane's OWN LEDGER TABLE -
  pk_move_fencing_cs.go:282-293 passes l.ledgerID to
  lockop.LockRowsForAdmissionResult - and admission REQUIRES
  the locked binding's Table to equal that ledger table
  (lock_op.go:1071-1073, a mismatch raising
  NewLockTableBindChangedNoCtx), so while the binding stays
  unchanged EVERY round of the same address presents the
  identical triple; an EXPIRED predecessor round completing
  late satisfies the successor's recorded 'round-key
  guard', and (ii)'s claimed isolation - a later grant
  NEVER overwriting an in-flight predecessor, an expired
  owner NEVER publishing into a live round - does NOT
  follow from the specified identity; verified 2026-10-26
  at the cited loci exactly as the review states.
  (A.2) F2 - FIRST RETURN IS NOT TERMINAL OWNERSHIP:
  D186(B.2)(i)/(iii) (r76 :12798-12816) releases the charge
  once 'commit returned, or rollback returned' and lets the
  FIRST of those returns win after expiry, but the
  transaction operator claims terminal ownership BEFORE
  executing any terminal work: Commit claims the
  terminal-call gate first (operator.go:1098-1102,
  claimTerminalCall's Idle->Active CAS :2370-2382, gate
  contract :2365-2369 - exactly one public Commit,
  Rollback, or WriteAndCommit call owns the terminal
  transition and INTERNAL CLEANUP OWNERS BYPASS THE GATE
  through rollback), so a Rollback racing a blocked Commit
  FAILS THE SAME GATE (operator.go:1164-1168) and returns
  moerr.NewTxnClosedNoCtx WITHOUT entering
  sealAndWaitRunningSQLWithSQL or rollback - zero cleanup.
  Round expiry while the owner's Commit blocks inside its
  deferred synchronous unlock (the D186(B.1)/(H.10)(n)
  geometry) would thus record a 'rollback returned' FIRST
  RETURN and release the charge while the transaction,
  workspace, locks, and committing lane remain live -
  (C.23)'s ownership linearity gives out exactly as the
  review states; verified 2026-10-26.
  (B) Decisions:
  (B.1) F1 - FRESH PER-ROUND OWNER TOKEN (refines
  D186(B.2)(ii) in IDENTITY ONLY; the triple's binding
  FRESHNESS use, the no-overwrite/no-publish properties,
  and the (H.10)(o) merge stand):
  (i) OWNER TOKEN: the owner mints its token BEFORE grant
  dispatch - the round's OWN ScratchTableID (the fresh
  per-round DataBranchFencingScratchDraw, contract at
  pk_move_fencing.go:88-90, validated nonzero at the round
  gate pk_move_fencing.go:338-342, minted at
  pk_move_fencing_retire.go:291) PAIRED WITH a driver-local
  monotonic ROUND ORDINAL allocated under the driver mu;
  the ordinal is defense-in-depth so two live owners NEVER
  share a token even if a draw were ever duplicated.
  (ii) Token-keyed authority: the per-owner slot of
  D186(B.2)(i) is keyed by the token; EVERY publication,
  certificate write, stage-completion write, terminal
  cleanup, and sweep-visible residue marker carries the
  token and is accepted ONLY by the slot whose token
  matches - a mismatched token is a NO-OP, so an expired
  predecessor can neither publish into nor clean or
  overwrite a live successor's state even under the same
  account AND the same binding.
  (iii) BINDING FRESHNESS IS SEPARATE FROM OWNER IDENTITY:
  the account + Table/ServiceID/Version triple is retained
  EXCLUSIVELY as the generation/freshness check it actually
  is - the grant's LockedOn binding must still equal the
  ledger's current binding at admission, and a bind-changed
  generation still invalidates the round per the recorded
  contract; it is no longer part of the round owner
  identity.
  (iv) Re-derived properties over the token: a later round's
  grant can NEVER overwrite an in-flight predecessor
  (distinct tokens; the predecessor's slot lives until ITS
  OWN selected terminal action genuinely returns), an
  expired owner can NEVER publish into a live round
  (token-mismatch NO-OP), and sweep-visible residue carries
  the round's token so the witnessed sweep's reclamation
  stays round-exact - the D178(B.3)/(D) residue geometry
  is unchanged.
  (B.2) F2 - TERMINAL OWNERSHIP IS CHOSEN BEFORE INVOCATION
  (refines D186(B.2)(i)/(iii) and REPROVES (C.23) over
  selected-invocation completion instead of first return;
  the amalgamation, the ONE-charge geometry, the deadlines,
  and the D178 residue contract stand):
  (i) DECISION STATE, SELECTED ONCE: the owner carries an
  explicit terminal-decision state under its own mutex -
  ACTIVE -> COMMITTING, or ACTIVE -> ABANDONING, then DONE.
  Exactly one selector wins: the ordinary F1 completion
  path selects COMMITTING (certificate satisfied, deadline
  unexpired); the abandonment edges - F1-reservation
  REJECTION, round EXPIRY, LATE completion - select
  ABANDONING. The decision is recorded BEFORE any
  Commit/Rollback invocation, and a later selector
  observing a recorded decision NEVER invokes a second
  public terminal call, so exactly one public terminal
  invocation per operator exists BY CONSTRUCTION - the
  operator's terminal-call gate (:2365-2369) stays the
  platform belt to this decision gate's braces.
  (ii) EXPIRY DURING COMMITTING revokes RESULT ACCEPTANCE
  ONLY: no Rollback is invoked against a claimed gate, and
  a gate-rejected ErrTxnClosed return
  (operator.go:2370-2382) is NEVER treated as cleanup or as
  a charge-releasing return. The charge, the slot, and the
  owner's accounting persist UNTIL the selected Commit
  invocation GENUINELY returns - on success the pair is
  sweep-owned durable residue per D178(B.3)/(D) and the
  expired round's outcome is discarded; on commit error the
  operator's own failure path (the recorded internal
  cleanup owners that BYPASS the gate) owns the terminal
  transition, and the owner awaits only the genuine return
  of its selected invocation (r78: REFINED by
  D188(B.1)(i)/(ii) - a returning call can leave cleanup
  DEFERRED (operator.go:1169-1174/:2116-2138) or scheduled
  independently (sql_executor.go:385-392/:1090/:1115); the
  owner RETAINS and awaits the observed operator close,
  not merely the return).
  (iii) ABANDONING exactness: when no Commit was ever
  invoked (the stage lanes observe the recorded decision
  under the owner mutex before their public calls), the
  owner's single Rollback invocation seals and waits the
  running stage SQL and rolls back through the platform's
  public route; its genuine return (r78: RE-SEATED as a
  RESULT input by D188(B.1)(i) - the running-SQL wait can
  FAIL and defer the actual cleanup past the return
  (operator.go:1169-1174/:2116-2138); cleanup completes
  EXACTLY ONCE and the charge releases ONLY at the
  observed ClosedEvent boundary of D188(B.1)(i)/(iv)),
  and any later
  stage-side Commit attempt is gate-rejected, observed as
  a NO-OP, releasing nothing.
  (iv) CHARGE-RELEASE RULE (supersedes the r76 (B.2)(i)
  return list): the charge releases ONLY at the genuine
  return of the invocation the decision state selected
  (r78: SUPERSEDED by D188(B.1)(i) - release rides ONLY
  the observed operator close; even a genuine return can
  precede cleanup in the deferred and independently
  scheduled geometries of D188(A)) -
  or, for a round rejected before ANY scratch transaction
  exists, at the recorded no-transaction reap; NO other

- D188 (r78, 2026-10-26): OBSERVED-CLOSE COMPLETION

  that live state; (C.23')'s interval [open, SELECTED

  does not exist.
  (B) Decisions:
  (B.1) OBSERVED-CLOSE COMPLETION BOUNDARY (refines
  D187(B.2)(ii)/(iii)/(iv) in the RELEASE CONDITION ONLY;
  the pre-invocation selection state machine, exact-once-

  (i) RELEASE ONLY AT THE OBSERVED CLOSE: the owner
  releases the charge, the slot, and its accounting ONLY
  after observing the stage operator's ClosedEvent - the
  single terminal-completion publication closeLocked
  emits exactly once under the operator mu
  (operator.go:2037-2060, the !mu.closed guard at
  :2048). Every cleanup geometry publishes the SAME
  boundary: synchronous rollback (rollbackOwned's
  unconditional closeLocked defer :1236-1240), deferred
  scheduled rollback (the same private rollback, the
  same defer), independently scheduled fatal-error
  cleanup (the same scheduleRollbackAfterRunningSQL ->
  the same private rollback), and commit-failure
  scheduling (:1090/:1115). Registration rides the
  public AppendEventCallback surface
  (operator_events.go:54-78) AT stage-operator
  construction, while the operator is provably open
  (append panics on closed :65-67), so no terminal
  action can precede registration. A public call's
  return - selected, error-returning, or gate-rejected -

  residue-geometry decisions per D187(B.2)(ii)/(iii))
  and NEVER a release condition.
  (ii) RETAINING STATE: the decision machine becomes
  ACTIVE -> COMMITTING/ABANDONING -> RETAINING -> DONE.
  A selected invocation returning without the close
  observed - the deferred geometries - leaves the owner
  RETAINING: charge held, slot and accounting intact,
  expiry-side result acceptance already revoked per
  D187(B.2)(ii); DONE - and the single release - fires
  only when BOTH the stage lanes have exited per
  D179/D180 accounting AND the observed close has been
  consumed, retaining the charge, slot and dependent
  resources until all stages and the effective cleanup
  owner finish.
  (iii) NON-BLOCKING, PLATFORM-BOUNDED OBSERVATION: the
  ClosedEvent callback fires under the operator mu
  (closeLocked holds mu through triggerEventLocked
  :2055-2060), so it performs ONLY the recorded
  D186(B.1) non-blocking publication discipline - an
  atomic store / channel close toward the driver - and
  the driver's own observation consumes it. The
  deferred geometries' completion is bounded by the
  platform's own machinery: sealAndRunWhenDrained runs
  the cleanup once when the last SQL token exits
  (:493-525/:456-478) on a context with the recorded
  runningSQLWaitTimeout (:2127-2135), and the token
  exits are themselves capped by the lanes' D179/D180
  bounded awaits - retention adds NO new wait, NO new
  timeout constant, NO new lock. (r79: the 'capped by the lanes' D179/D180 bounded awaits' clause is WITHDRAWN and the bound RE-SEATED by D189(B.2)/(C.29') - D179/D180 cap only the retiring caller's return (:10141-10150), the timeout clock starts only AT token drain (:2126-2131), and the drained rollback's unlock tail rides the SERVICE-LIFETIME context (service.go:769-775) AHEAD of closeLocked under the LIFO defer order (:1236-1251); retention is ACCOUNTING-bounded by the saturation count and COMPLETION-bounded only at the post-stopRPCs barrier)
  (iv) EXACTLY-ONCE AT THE BOUNDARY: exactly one close

  (C) Proofs:
  (C.23'') OWNERSHIP LINEARITY, re-derived: the scratch

  (D) Residue contract: stands as D187(D); the close

  (E.49) keeping release at the selected return plus a

  (F) Untouched: every D187(F) entry stands;

- D189 (r79, 2026-10-26): SHARED STAGE-OPERATOR OWNERSHIP
  AND THE RETAINED-OWNER DRAIN CONTRACT (round-29 design
  review F1 (P2, against D186(B.2)'s T_f1-only accounting
  scope as retained by D188) and F2 (P2, against
  D188(B.1)(iii)/(C.29)'s retention bound); extends
  D186(B.2)'s amalgamation scope and refines
  D188(B.1)(iii)/(C.29) ONLY; every D187/D188 token,
  selection, boundary and exactly-once decision stands,
  noted in place; D165(C) remains absolute).
  (A) Verified gaps (re-verified at the cited loci before
  editing):
  F1 - CLEANUP-COMPLETION ACCOUNTING STOPS AT T_f1:
  D186(B.2) (:12789-12792) supersedes the per-STAGE charge
  model "for the T_f1 pair ONLY; every other stage keeps
  D176(D)/D179/D180 lane semantics", and D188 retains that
  scope - but T_f2's transaction runs stage SQL through the
  SAME borrowed executor (execInStage
  pk_move_fencing_cs.go:243-251 routing
  executor.Options{}.WithTxn(op) into the internal
  executor): a fatal DELETE error schedules the deferred
  rollback through the executor's retErr defer BEFORE the
  call returns (sql_executor.go:386-388 ->
  client.DeferredTxnRollback -> operator.go:2112-2138,
  sealing mu.terminalAction at :2117-2124 and arming
  sealAndRunWhenDrained at :2126), so T_f2's fail path
  (pk_move_fencing_cs.go:433-435, reached from the DELETE
  error at :470-471) calls the public Rollback against an
  ALREADY-SEALED terminal gate and returns ErrTxnClosed
  with cleanup ARMED-not-RUN; the lane then delivers the
  error result and exits, releasing its charge at the
  lane-exit defer (pk_move_fencing_driver.go:161-166) while
  the scheduled rollback still owns the workspace, anchors
  and locks - repeated failures accumulate resources the
  accounting no longer sees, bypassing the claimed
  aggregate bound.
  F2 - THE RECORDED RETENTION BOUND IS FALSE:
  D188(B.1)(iii) (:13462-13476) and (C.29) (:13500-13507)
  bound retention by the platform's token drain plus
  runningSQLWaitTimeout "with the token exits capped by
  the lanes' D179/D180 bounded awaits"; but (i) D179(B.1)
  (:10141-10150) bounds ONLY the retiring statement's
  driver-local await - the lane runs on past T_round; (ii)
  the deferred rollback's timeout clock starts only AT
  token drain (operator.go:2126-2131 creates the
  WithTimeout context INSIDE the drained callback); and
  (iii) in every rollback geometry the unlock runs BEFORE
  closeLocked (the closeLocked defer at :1236-1239 declared
  before the unlock defer at :1241-1251, LIFO) while the
  lockservice UNLOCK substitutes the SERVICE-LIFETIME
  context for its remote retry (pkg/lockservice/service.go:
  769-775: retries remote cleanup until completion EVEN
  WHEN the caller's request context has ended; service
  shutdown is the one terminal cancellation owner) - so a
  retained charge can outlive runningSQLWaitTimeout
  indefinitely in steady state, and the lane-only
  CloseStep/DrainBarrier joins (driver.go:339-423) neither
  classify nor drain a retaining-but-laneless owner.
  (B) Decisions:
  (B.1) F1 - SHARED OBSERVED-CLOSE OWNERSHIP FOR EVERY
  DEFERRED-CLEANUP-CAPABLE STAGE OPERATOR:
      (i) ONE OWNERSHIP COMPONENT, EVERY STAGE OPERATOR:
      the D187/D188 owner (per-round token identity,
      pre-invocation terminal selection, ACTIVE ->
      COMMITTING/ABANDONING -> RETAINING -> DONE, release
      ONLY at the observed ClosedEvent) is GENERALIZED to
      one shared ownership component instantiated for every
      stage transaction opened through newStageTxn: the
      T_f1-pair amalgamation stands as ONE owner covering
      the grant and F1 stage operators; T_f2 gets its own
      owner on the SAME component; the watermark probe's
      throwaway operator consumes the same component (its
      rollback completes in-call today, so its owner
      releases in-call) - uniform by construction, no
      per-stage ad-hoc rule, no future stage able to open a
      deferred-cleanup-capable operator outside accounting.
      r82 amendment (D192): the (i) parenthetical in-call
      premise ('its rollback completes in-call today, so
      its owner releases in-call') is REFUTED - a stalled
      remote unlock ignores the caller's ended context
      under the lockservice's service-lifetime retry
      (pkg/lockservice/service.go:754-775), so the probe's
      in-thread release hangs the retiring statement past
      cancellation; the probe consumes the SAME component
      with its terminal SELECTION recorded in-call and its
      single rollback DETACHED and accounted, the charge
      releasing at the observed ClosedEvent like every
      other D189 owner - see D192(B)/(C).
      (ii) THE T_f2 FATAL GEOMETRY OWNED: on a fatal
      stage-SQL error the executor schedules the deferred
      rollback BEFORE fail() runs; fail()'s public Rollback
      (:433-435) gate-rejects with ErrTxnClosed and cleanup
      ARMED; the lane delivers its error result and exits
      WITHOUT releasing; the T_f2 owner enters RETAINING at
      lane exit and releases its charge ONLY at the
      scheduled cleanup's observed ClosedEvent - the (o.6)
      geometry, now owned for T_f2 by construction rather
      than excluded by scope.
      (iii) SATURATION REFUSES UNCHARGED WORK: a RETAINING
      owner's charge COUNTS in the pool's reservation
      accounting exactly like a live lane's charge; when
      live lanes plus retained owners reach the recorded
      G_lane budget (LanePoolCapacity), the next reserve
      REFUSES with the recorded saturation class
      (DataBranchFencingRoundSaturated, spawn at
      driver.go:271-277) - NO uncharged work is admitted
      while any cleanup is outstanding.
      (iv) EXACTLY-ONCE: stands as D188(B.1)(iv) - the
      :2048 single close publication, the terminalAction
      gate (:2117-2124) and the tracker's single-shot drain
      (:501-504) make the FIRST cleanup arming the only
      effective one however many paths race; DONE consumes
      the single observed event exactly once.
  (B.2) F2 - THE DRAIN CONTRACT (bounded ADMISSION/
  ACCOUNTING; shutdown-bounded COMPLETION):
      (i) BOUNDED ACCOUNTING, NOT BOUNDED STEADY-STATE
      COMPLETION: at every instant live lane charges plus
      retained owner charges <= G_lane (charged at reserve
      BEFORE dispatch per driver.go:261-292, released only
      at the D188(B.1)(i) observed-close boundary), so
      retention can NEVER starve the pool silently - it
      presents as exact, counted admission pressure.
      Steady-state retention DURATION is explicitly NOT
      wall-clock bounded: the unlock tail rides the
      platform's service-lifetime retry until remote
      recovery, and capping that retry is (E.53).
      (ii) COMPLETION CONSUMER: when an owner's LAST stage
      lane exits in RETAINING, the owner hands its close
      future to the pool's RETAINED-OWNER REGISTRY - pool
      state surfaced in Dump as a Retained set keyed by
      owner with stage/step; the registry entry IS the
      completion consumer after statement-driver exit: once
      both stages have exited, the owner is no longer a
      lane matter at all, and every charge remains visible
      to every dump.
      (iii) SHUTDOWN INTEGRATION: CloseStep GAINS a
      classifier: retained registry entries are NOT lanes -
      the step records them and neither fail-stops on nor
      joins them (symmetric to the existing detached-lane
      rule at driver.go:367-374); the FINAL DRAIN BARRIER
      (driver.go:389-423) joins BOTH detached lanes AND
      retained registry entries to full close observation
      under the same BarrierTimeout, then verifies zero
      lanes, zero retained and zero charges - a loud named
      failure with owner id/stage on any expiry, never a
      silent zero (the barrier never reports a zero it did
      not verify).
      (iv) ORDER AUTHORITY: the CN drain chain ALREADY
      places the barrier AFTER stopRPCs
      (cnservice/server.go:620-625; lockService.Close at
      :858), whose service-lifetime cancel terminates the
      stalled unlock's retry (the retry's serviceCtx ends
      at service Close); the drained rollback then runs
      through closeLocked, the ClosedEvent publishes, the
      retained owner releases, and the barrier's join
      observes it within BarrierTimeout - shutdown
      completion is bounded by the EXISTING chain position:
      NO new step, NO moved step, NO cnservice change. (r80: the reachability premise is REFUTED and the authority RE-ANCHORED by D190(B.1) - txnClient.Close precedes lockService.Close (cnservice/server.go:845-858) and its stopper join can wait on an operator mutex a stalled rollback holds through the abort-marking walk; the lockservice cancellation segment is moved BEFORE the stopper-join segment by this design's ONE stopRPCs order amendment)
  (C) Proofs:
  (C.23'') and (C.27)/(C.28) stand VERBATIM (the boundary
  itself does not move).
  (C.29') BOUNDED ACCOUNTING (replaces (C.29)):
  (a) at every instant live lanes plus retained owners <=
  G_lane, with saturation refusing the recorded class, so
  every open-or-closing stage transaction is charged to
  exactly one owner and the pool's aggregate resource
  claim holds while cleanup is outstanding;
  (b) steady-state retention can outlive
  runningSQLWaitTimeout ONLY inside the platform's own
  service-lifetime unlock retry - the platform's
  pre-existing reclamation surface - while the delayed
  charge stays counted and budgeted by (a); (r80: (b) CORRECTED by D190(C.29'')(b) - beyond-timeout retention also spans PH-1 while a stage statement is in flight; D189(H.10)(u)'s token-retention premise contradicted this clause and had no production correspondence (sql_executor.go:385-393))
  (c) at CN shutdown the (B.2)(iv) ordering bounds
  completion by the barrier budget or fails the chain
  LOUD. (C.29)'s premise that D179/D180 awaits cap the
  token exits is WITHDRAWN: they cap the retiring caller's
  return only.
  (C.30) DRAIN COMPLETENESS: every charged resource is
  visible to Dump at every instant as exactly one of {live
  lane, detached lane, retained registry entry}; CloseStep
  classifies all three without fail-stopping on legal
  transients; the barrier joins all three to zero -
  the accounting has no invisible state at any point in
  the lifecycle.
  (D) Residue contract: stands as D188(D); the retained
  registry and its classification are transient owner
  bookkeeping, never durable residue shapes.
  (E) Superseded/rejected record:
  (E.52) force-releasing the charge after a NEW retention
  timeout CONSIDERED-AND-REJECTED: release while cleanup
  is live is the round-28 (A) fallacy with a timer; the

  AFTER txnClient.Close -> never reached; the DrainBarrier

  F2 - THE (u) SCHEDULE'S TOKEN GEOMETRY CANNOT OCCUR AND
  ITS DISCHARGE CANNOT FIRE: D189(H.10)(u) (:13809-13827)

      (ii) TERMINATION AFTER THE AMENDMENT IS BOUNDED:
      with serviceCtx canceled first, the stalled retry

      in-flight remote lock/unlock operation was already

      (iv) SCOPE AND D165(C) RE-SCOPED: the amendment

      stall an unlock at close - the D186 detached

  (B.2) F2 - THE TWO-PHASE RETENTION MODEL:
      (i) PHASES AND EDGES: retention has exactly two
      phases. PH-1 TOKEN-HELD: the deferred cleanup is
      ARMED (the tracker stored, operator.go:517-519) but
      cannot start; the phase ends ONLY at the
      independent TOKEN-EXIT edge - the stage statement

      cancel-then-exit (operator.go:505-523). PH-2

      service-lifetime retry (service.go:769-775),

  (B) The repair - the probe's lifecycle splits into
  IN-CALL SAMPLING and DETACHED ACCOUNTED DISPOSAL:
  (B.1) WHAT STAYS IN-CALL: the throwaway transaction's
  SHARED scratch-key acquisition and its returned watermark

  serialization the sample means): both stay synchronous on
  the statement thread. The probe's value to its caller -
  the grant-time watermark - is fully captured in the
  admission result before any disposal begins.
  (B.2) WHAT MOVES OFF THE THREAD: the throwaway operator's
  DISPOSAL. The probe owner's terminal selection records
  SYNCHRONOUSLY on the statement thread (abandon() selects
  ABANDONING under the owner mutex BEFORE the thread
  proceeds, the D187(B.2) chosen-before-invocation

  while the single public Rollback runs DETACHED under the

  The owner releases its charge ONLY at the operator's
  observed ClosedEvent (D188(B.1)(i) verbatim): a probe
  owner whose rollback tail outlives its sample enters

  (D189(B.1)(iii)): retention presents as exact counted

  probe transaction wrote nothing (zero-write throwaway by
  construction), so its detached rollback carries no data

- D207 (r88, 2026-10-28): THE RESTART-AWARE CLOCK-CHAIN
  CONTRACT - the per-generation causal freshness ground
  and the two closure channels (round-38 pre-PR review
  F2 (P2), supersedes D203(B.1)'s response-lift
  sentence and the D203(B.4) envelope pin (ii);
  D201-D206 stand).
  (A) The gap (verified r88 at the cited loci): F2 -
  D203(B.1)/(B.4), design :16902-16953, grounds post-T3
  freshness on the response codec's lift, but the codec
  stamps the responder's CURRENT clock
  (codec_header.go:105-119's Encode/Decode), never the
  conflicting MVCC timestamp; a TN's NORMAL write-mode
  open restores committed history WITHOUT advancing
  that clock (tae/db/controller.go:816-819 advances
  only the watermark via TryUpdateMaxCommittedTS; the
  explicit Clock.Update(maxCommitted) at :493-501 sits
  in the replay-to-write PROMOTION path under its own
  comment 'Replay advances the committed watermark,
  but not that clock'), so a restarted TN adjudicates a
  restored version at C (mvccnode.go:74-89) while its
  response stamp stays below C - the asserted post-T3
  request >= C fails inside the window. The review's
  skewed-restart schedule is VERIFIED VALID.
  (B) The contract:
  (B.1) THE IN-GENERATION CHAIN (grounded; every locus
  re-read): on the reference topology the adjudicating
  TN MINTS C from its own runtime clock (s.storage.
  Commit and the newTxn.CommitTS assignment,
  txn/service/service_cn_handler.go:278-285; the client
  consumes it at operator.go:1786), so at adjudication
  the responder's clock dominates C by in-process HLC
  monotony; its response stamp (codec_header.go:
  106-110) carries >= C; the refused CN's Decode lifts
  its clock (:112-119); the fresh creation's request
  = max(minTS, HLC now) >= C and blocks in the waiter
  until the applied frontier covers it
  (timestamp_waiter.go:88-101) - NO stale attempt: AT
  MOST ONE T3 per ordered pair PER TN GENERATION.
  Multi-TN note: A's commit RPC to the seal shard also
  carried a header stamp >= C (A's CN was lifted by its
  own commit response's Decode; monotony), so the
  shard's server Decode (txn/rpc/server.go:199) lifts
  the shard past C at install; the same conclusion
  holds there.
  (B.2) THE RESTART WINDOW (honest): across a TN
  (re)start the (B.1) premises reset - a fresh runtime
  clock (setup.go:73-76/:110-115's per-service clocks)
  and restored history left unaligned by the normal
  open - so for a real-time window bounded by the clock
  domain's offset relative to C's mint instant, the
  response lift may undershoot C; fresh creations
  inside the window may start stale and collide with
  the same killer. Each induced extra T3 costs at least
  one full commit round trip, and no repository
  mechanism can promise a smaller integer without
  re-adopting the skew-as-ordering fallacy - the window
  is closed by the two channels below, and ONLY by
  them.
  (B.3) CHANNEL-C (CLOCK CROSSOVER): HLC.Now returns
  max(state, local physical) plus a logical bump
  (hlc.go:241-251), so after the local physical
  component crosses C's physical component - bounded in
  real time by the clock domain's offset relative to
  the mint instant - the fresh creation's request is
  >= C FOREVER and the waiter STALLS loudly (pending
  entry, no refusal, no delivery needed).
  (B.4) CHANNEL-F (FRONTIER COVER): the waiter's
  success arms return latest.Next() - the CN's APPLIED
  FRONTIER advanced past the request
  (timestamp_waiter.go:83-85 and :100-101), NOT the
  request itself - so once logtail delivery covers C at
  the refused CN, EVERY fresh creation returns a
  snapshot >= C regardless of that CN's clock; the
  D202(B.1) chain (openTxn client.go:723-762 ->
  updateSnapshotWithClose operator.go:955-991 -> the
  waiter) keeps blocking requests above the frontier
  meanwhile. Delivery liveness closes the window
  permanently. r89 amendment (D209(B.1)): the
  honest certificate is delivered L >= r: for
  r <= C a release covering C admits and returns
  C.Next() >= C; for r > C admission PENDS until
  L >= r, then returns latest.Next() > C; in both
  regimes no STALE attempt is possible, so the

- D217 (r96, 2026-10-28): THE REAL-RETENTION NAMESPACE IN THE KEEP FIXTURE ORACLES (round-47 pre-PR design review REQUEST_CHANGES on r95, ONE P2 finding; supersedes D216(B.3)'s and D211(C.1)'s r95 amendment row_kind=1 literals, corrected IN PLACE; every other r95/r94 landing stands).
  (A) THE FINDING, VERIFIED (read-only before editing;
  /tmp/e117_verify.log):
  (A.1) THE NAMESPACE CONSTANTS -
  pkg/catalog/types.go:418-431:
  DataBranchLinkRetentionColRowKind's comment pins (row_kind,
  table_id) as the retention-table primary key with real
  retained identity rows writing 0 and fencing scratch rows
  writing 1; DataBranchLinkRetentionRowKindReal = 0 selects
  the retained dead-table identity rows the drop-lifecycle
  funnels and genesis admission write;
  DataBranchLinkRetentionRowKindFencingScratch = 1 selects the
  fencing round's scratch rows, written only by the fencing
  pair. This matches D178's namespace decision verbatim
  (design :9926-9928: every REAL row writes row_kind = 0;
  every SCRATCH row writes row_kind = 1; the key spaces
  disjoint by primary-key prefix).
  (A.2) THE FUNNEL'S KIND SCOPE -
  pkg/sql/compile/pk_move_link_retention.go: the probe SELECT
  filters row_kind = RowKindReal AND table_id (:108-115); the
  enrichment UPDATE predicates row_kind = RowKindReal AND
  table_id (:202-207); the INSERT writes RowKindReal
  (:259-271). NO funnel path reads or writes kind 1.
  (A.3) THE r95 ERROR AND ITS CONSEQUENCES: D216(B.3)(i)/(ii)
  (design :19339/:19346) and the D211(C.1) amendment (design
  :18411) asserted row_kind=1 for the INSERT and ENRICHMENT
  fixtures. TWO failure modes follow: (a) a CORRECT INSERT
  writes row_kind=0, so the r95 oracle asserting row_kind=1
  FAILS even when production is right; (b) an ENRICHMENT
  fixture seeded at kind 1 is INVISIBLE to the kind-0-scoped
  probe (:108-115), so found=false and the funnel takes the
  INSERT branch - the fixture named ENRICHMENT would silently
  exercise INSERT and its enriched-value assertions would
  never run. The finding is VALID at every cited locus.
  (B) THE CORRECTED NAMESPACE CONTRACT: (B.1) REAL-ROW
  IDENTITY - every KEEP fixture, probe and terminal assertion
  identifies retained rows by (row_kind=0, table_id), the row
  the funnels and genesis admission own; the three row_kind=1
  literals are corrected IN PLACE to the real kind
  (row_kind=0) at design :18411, :19339 and :19346. (B.2)
  SCRATCH DISTINCTNESS - kind-1 fencing scratch rows never
  appear as funnel rows; a fixture may CO-SEED a kind-1 decoy
  at the same table_id ONLY as the disjointness witness, with
  terminal assertions requiring ONE kind-0 identity row total
  and the decoy byte-untouched, PROVING the probe's kind
  scoping rather than assuming it. (B.3) THE THREE BRANCH
  WITNESSES PRESERVED, re-keyed: (i) MISSING-row INSERT
  asserts the inserted row's exact values including
  row_kind=0, ONE kind-0 identity row total, links byte-exact;
  (ii) INCOMPLETE-row ENRICHMENT seeds an incomplete KIND-0
  row (blank names and/or the stored 0 logical-id marker - the
  :149-153 backfill contract) and asserts the enriched values
  exact AND the preserved immutables (created_ts
  byte-identical; row_kind=0 and table_id stable), byte
  equality deliberately not asserted for the mutated fields;
  (iii) EXISTING-complete-row NO-OP keeps FULL byte equality
  plus the code-shaped branch witness (the :185-199 seam).
  FULL byte equality stays RESERVED for the rollback arms and
  the no-op; the race arm's finals adopt the branch the
  funnel's fresh RC probe observes. (B.4) NAMESPACE SEAM PINS
  - the catalog constants (pkg/catalog/types.go:418-431: the
  ColRowKind comment, RowKindReal, RowKindFencingScratch) and
  the funnel's three kind-scoped predicates (probe :108-115,
  enrichment UPDATE :202-207, INSERT :259-271) are pinned; ANY
  modification REOPENS D217 beside D216's and D215's pins.
  (C) Cells (revised landing): D211(C.1)'s r95 amendment and
  D216(B.3) carry the r96 amendment (D217) notes superseding
  the row_kind=1 literals with (B)'s contract - (i)/(ii)/(iii)
  re-keyed to kind 0 with the decoy discipline of (B.2); the
  split SNAPSHOT/PITR controls of D216(A), the standing
  :572-579 DROP-TABLE control, D212(C.2)/(C.3), D206's family,
  both bounded arms and every D215 landing stand UNCHANGED.
  (D) Cost: document plus cell-schedule edits ONLY; ZERO
  production delta; NO namespace, admission or funnel behavior
  change.
  (E) Rejected alternatives: (E.1) seeding kind-1 fixture rows
  and re-scoping the production probe to match - a production
  behavior change forbidden by the finding's action and by
  this design-only checkpoint; (E.2) dropping the row_kind
  assertion entirely - loses the disjointness pin and lets any
  kind satisfy the oracle; (E.3) kind-agnostic assertions (a
  row at table_id of some kind) - a kind-1 decoy would satisfy
  them vacuously, re-creating the r95 defect; (E.4) re-homing
  the KEEP fixtures onto the fencing scratch namespace -
  conflates lifecycle retention with scratch, contradicting
  D178's (row_kind, table_id) separation; (E.5) changing the

  delta, out of scope for the design checkpoint and unneeded:

  (reverted/deleted in the implementation turn per

- D218 (r97, 2026-10-28): THE ACTUAL-MOVE ADMISSION GATE FOR
  RETENTION GENESIS AND SEALING (round-48 pre-PR implementation
  review on the r96-era implementation, ONE P1 finding; continuity
  markers preserved; every r96 landing stands).
  (A) THE FINDING, VERIFIED (read-only before editing;
  /tmp/e119_verify.log):
  (A.1) THE SYNTHETIC CTX ATTACHES FIRST - pkg/sql/plan/
  bind_update.go:2336-2344 appends the link ctx to EVERY eligible
  single-target UPDATE; eligibility (pkg/sql/plan/
  data_branch_update_link.go:128-153) is every ordinary UPDATE
  of a plain pk user table.
  (A.2) CONTINUITY MARKERS ARE INTENTIONAL AND TXN-LOCAL -
  pkg/sql/colexec/multi_update/pk_move_link.go:420-431 emits a
  never-committed continuity marker even when old/new pk bytes
  are equal (the marker family exists so a LATER statement's move
  can name this row's generation - the r26-F5 lineage, design
  :3124); the fixup's Pass 3 consumes and drops them
  (pkg/vm/engine/disttae/pk_move_link_fixup.go:631-636), so
  markers alone commit NOTHING.
  (A.3) GENESIS STAGES UNCONDITIONALLY - the workspace write
  route stages retention genesis BEFORE the link batch write
  whenever the ctx'd batch has rows
  (pk_move_link.go:290-296 -> stagePkMoveRetentionRows
  :611-643); the S3 ferry flush repeats it for every ferried
  batch with a resolvable owner ctx (multi_update.go:522-531).
  A marker-only batch therefore fires the genesis admission of a
  transaction that never moves a key.
  (A.4) THE LOCK CONSEQUENCES - the txn-private epoch map makes
  EVERY transaction pay exactly one first-touch probe per address
  (probePkMoveGenesis, pk_move_genesis.go:160-247). MISS fires
  pkMoveGenesisOwnedLockFn - the identity key's EXCLUSIVE row
  lock on the OUTER transaction, "held to transaction end"
  (pk_move_link.go:834-838) - and stages the OWNED row; the
  statement-boundary prune
  (cancelGenesisRegistrationsWithoutLinksLocked,
  pk_move_genesis.go:473-508, invoked from
  pruneDeadPkMoveLinkRowsLocked, pk_move_link_fixup.go:
  4080-4088) already destroys that staged row when no live links
  exist, so a continuity-only transaction commits NO ledger row -
  but the prune neither un-fires the probe nor releases the
  lock. HIT fires sealPkMoveRetentionRowShared - a BYTE-IDENTITY
  self-update of the shared retention row through the OUTER
  transaction, an ordinary-DML EXCLUSIVE row lock held to
  transaction end (pk_move_link.go:810-820, :888-925) - and the
  seal write is not pruned.
  (A.5) THE FAILURE SHAPE - T1 `begin; update t set payload='x'
  where id=1;` (NO move) holds the table address's exclusive
  genesis identity lock (MISS shape) or the shared seal row lock
  (HIT shape) until T1 commits, so T2's disjoint `update t set
  payload='y' where id=2` on the same table BLOCKS until T1
  finishes: ordinary disjoint UPDATEs of one table serialize
  cross-session on a synthetic ledger key, in both the ABSENT-
  and EXISTING-retention-row shapes. D206(C.1)'s landed disjoint
  control (data_branch_retire_cells_test.go:1094-1117) used
  AUTOCOMMIT ExecContext twins with eventual-success oracles -
  with autocommit's sub-statement lock lifetime T2 always drains,
  so the serialization passed unnoticed.
  (A.6) THE CONTRACT VIOLATED - D159(A): "one link row per MOVED
  row"; D159(F): the producer charge scales with distinct MOVED
  addresses; D159(A.3)/D161(A): |ledger| = |distinct addresses
  with surviving link rows| + residue. Charging every eligible-
  UPDATE first touch with a probe, an exclusive ledger lock and
  (on HIT) a staged seal expands the actual-moved-address scope
  to ordinary updates across the table. The P1 finding is VALID
  at every cited locus, with the precision that the producer
  files live under pkg/sql/colexec/multi_update and the review's
  :820/:835 numbers land on pkMoveLinkEntryLayoutLocked in the
  current tree - the lock loci are pk_move_link.go:834-838 (MISS)
  and :810-820 (HIT).
  (B) THE CORRECTED ADMISSION CONTRACT:
  (B.1) THE GATE: retention genesis/sealing is admitted for a
  link batch IFF the batch carries >=1 REAL moved-address link
  row - old pk bytes != new pk bytes, the same equality the fill
  hook's isMarker pass uses. A continuity-only (all-marker or
  empty) batch stages NO genesis, fires NO probe, stages NO
  seal, and takes NO ledger lock.
  (B.2) TWO CALL SITES, NO TXN-STATE HALF - the gates guard
  exactly the two staging call sites where the triggering batch
  is in hand: pk_move_link.go:290-296 (workspace write route)
  and multi_update.go:522-531 (ferry flush). No transaction-
  state consult is needed: a transaction whose earlier statement
  moved keys already admitted genesis at that statement (the
  epoch map dedups all later touches); a later continuity-only
  statement skips losslessly; a never-moving transaction skips
  everything; and a move-carrying statement keeps D159(A)'s
  identity-row-FIRST ordering before its own link write, so the
  positional statement cut removes both (rollback symmetry
  unchanged).
  (B.3) THE SEAL IS GATED ATOMICALLY - the seal stages only
  inside the probe's HIT arm, so gating probe invocation gates
  the seal in the same step: D198's WW anchor engages exactly
  when the transaction's OWN links are at stake, matching
  D206(B.1)'s mark premise ("first stages fabric-owned protocol
  artifacts") with no mark-surface change.
  (B.4) INVARIANTS STRENGTHENED - D159(A.3)/D161(A)'s |ledger|
  bound now holds BY ADMISSION (continuity-only transactions
  never stage anything) with the engine prune retained as belt;
  statement atomicity is unchanged - the existing cell-proven
  shape (a move statement failing after the genesis stage aborts
  both rows) guards move-carrying statements exactly as before.
  (B.5) SEAM PINS - the two gated call sites and the shared
  batch predicate (old!=new scan over the producer batch's
  old/new pk vectors) are pinned; ANY modification REOPENS D218
  beside D215's, D216's and D217's pins.
  (B.6) COST - the gate is O(batch rows) byte compares replacing
  one keyed internal probe, one exclusive ledger lock and (on
  HIT) one staged seal per eligible-transaction first touch;
  ordinary UPDATEs regain the pre-stack locking surface and
  D159(F)'s charge resumes its actual-moved-address scope.
  (C) Cells (landing schedule; cheapest discriminating first):
  (C.1) GATE UT PINS (pkg/sql/colexec/multi_update, fabric
  PkMoveGenesisProbe override plus the pkMoveGenesisWriteFn
  indirection): a marker-only batch invokes NO genesis stage

- D219 (r99, CI run 40797678570 repair): the fencing-retirement critical
  section gets a pre-round gate on its own transaction's locked view.
  (A) PREMISE PROBLEM - every branch-member drop, including an unlink
  drop that staged no links and holds no retention identity row, ran the
  full critical section: witness round, watermark fold and D185 envelope
  certification. On multi-CN deployments the git4data/branch drop
  cadence compounded rounds into lockservice starvation (CI PROXY job's
  fulltext 300-second watchdog hang).
  (B) MECHANISM - the retiring transaction takes the EXCLUSIVE
  ledger-row-key lock FIRST (the same grant the round's acceptance
  grant takes), then re-probes (i) committed link presence for the
  retired address and (ii) the row_kind=0 retention identity row, both
  at that locked view through fresh internal statements in the retiring
  transaction. One staged first touch cannot commit invisible behind
  the grant because stage transactions take the same ledger-key lock at
  stage time and hold it to commit; therefore an empty locked view
  proves no writer-staged state exists, the caller's paired deletes are
  in-transaction no-ops, and the witness round, fold budget and
  certification are skipped entirely. When either probe hits, the full
  D168(B) critical section runs unchanged, and the pre-grant binding
  recording shrinks the recorded-binding-change window to the
  gate-to-acceptance gap on an already-held lock (D176(B.2) class (i)
  rollback covers it).
  (C) CELLS - gate-present/gate-absent pins in the existing compile and
  databranchutils fencing families: with neither links nor an identity
  row the round driver is never consulted (witness-round count ZERO);
  with either present the accepted families run byte-identical.
  (D) COST - one exclusive lock plus at most two keyed single-row probes
  per retirement, replacing a witness round + fold + certification on
  the unlink path; engaged paths pay the same two probes in addition.
  (E) REJECTED ALTERNATIVES - (E.1) skipping the lock and probing RC
  lazily: an in-flight first touch could commit between probe and
  round, resurrecting the race the critical section exists to close;
  (E.2) checking only link presence: the identity row alone still
  entitles a fencing round (its reclamation races a last writer);
  (E.3) deferring the gate into the round driver: the driver's pool
  dispatch and fold closure exist precisely to be skipped, so the gate
  must sit at the entry.
  (F) UNTOUCHED - D168(B)'s critical-section shape, the acceptance
  grant classes, D185 certification, the keep/drop funnels, the ledger
  DDL and prune, and every r1-r98 decision.

  subscription-routed segments)

  (A) PREMISE PROBLEM - resolvePkMoveRetentionSource caches the

  handle bound to the first, already-removed transaction (an I7
  violation: a staged identity row can be lost while its link rows

  map (pk_move_genesis.go:212-218) deduping to a zero-row write
  (txn.go:694-708). The defect manifests when a reused operator stages
  an address the first transaction never registered: the
  probe/admission or the staged row rides the removed workspace -
  either a loud txn-closed failure of a legitimate UPDATE, or a
  silently discarded retention registration.
  (B) MECHANISM - (B.1) in Prepare's per-context loop, when

  Reset(proc.GetTxnOperator()) exactly like info.Source

  clears retentionSource alongside info.Source so the lazy resolver
  re-resolves under the executing txn. (B.3) the sticky
  pkMoveRetentionDisabled degrade bit (pre-upgrade tenants) is
  unchanged: the re-bind never fires when resolution degraded, and
  the resolver keeps its cache when the handle is already current.
  (B.4) the disttae side - epoch map, admission, probe - is

  handle cached), Reset, Prepare with txn2, asserting (i) the relation
  re-bind observed with txn2 (spy), (ii) the staged identity row lands
  in txn2's workspace-of-record, (iii) the sticky degrade bit survives

  registration lands via the executing txn, ledger count correct).

  the existing Source resets; no new probes, no catalog reads.
  (E) REJECTED ALTERNATIVES - (E.1) re-resolving the relation fresh

  sticky pre-upgrade degrade bit (a re-resolution can flip the
  degrade decision mid-session); (E.2) dismissing the finding because

  reachable failures, loud or silent, violate I7; (E.3) handling in

  registration loss in place; the producer must not write into a dead
  workspace at all.
  (F) UNTOUCHED - the epoch/admission machinery, probe shapes and
  budgets, retention semantics (D159-D218), the writer protocol
  otherwise, and every D1-D220 decision.

  and r49's doc-text-only correction of the

  (no new decision, no new gate); and
  the r50 set D156-D157 (commit-exact failed-scope
  attribution from the link catalog's own change stream,

  contract), restored to design-first alignment per the r60
  review's I1 objection - D156/D157 are set at the r50
